rows.key_quote: Oscar Health reported Q2 2026 revenue of $4.9 billion, up 70% year-over-year, with MLR improving to 79.2% and SG&A expense ratio at a record low of 14.2%. Earnings from operations surged to $389 million, and net income was $362 million, both up sharply year-over-year. The company raised full-year 2026 earnings from operations guidance to $500-700 million, up $250 million, and improved MLR guidance to 81.5%-82.5%. Management highlighted favorable risk adjustment and utilization trends but remained cautious on CMS program integrity-driven member churn in the second half.

UMH reported Q2 2026 Normalized FFO per share of $0.25, up 9% year-over-year, and net income per diluted share of $0.05, up 67% year-over-year. Same-property NOI grew 9% driven by site rent increases of 5% and higher occupancy. The company maintained its full-year Normalized FFO guidance of $0.98-$1.04 per share. Management expressed strong conviction in growth prospects from factory-built housing policy and their development pipeline.

USPH reported Q2 2026 revenue of $214 million, up 8.5% YoY, with PT revenue up 8.4% to $182 million and IIP revenue up 9.1% to $32 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $27.0 million, roughly flat versus $26.9 million a year ago, while adjusted operating results per share fell to $0.75 from $0.81. The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $102-$106 million, citing expected benefits from hospital affiliations and cost initiatives in the back half. Management noted a headwind from higher self-insured healthcare costs ($3.2 million swing) and front-loaded hospital implementation costs, but expressed confidence in stronger growth ahead, including a potential upward revision to the 2027 hospital affiliation contribution above the original $7.3 million.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was $25 million from uranium, with a 57% gross margin and production cost of $23/lb. Net loss of $33.6 million included $10.7 million in transaction costs. Management highlighted conditional $725 million government loan, progress on ASM acquisition closing late August, and announced VAC acquisition expected to close early 2027. Continued investment in rare earth expansion and maintained strong balance sheet with ~$1 billion liquidity.

UWM reported Q2 Adjusted EBITDA over $180 million on about $40 billion of business, with management emphasizing consistent profitability despite a tough mortgage market. The company announced a $2 billion-plus capital raise with Oaktree (including $550 million from Mat Ishbia) and decided to suspend its dividend to retain equity and strengthen the balance sheet. Management acknowledged a one-time hedge loss and a failed Two Harbors MSR acquisition, but positioned the Oaktree partnership as a strategic long-term win. Guidance outlook is forward-looking, with expectations for a significantly better mortgage market in the next few years.

Marriott Vacations Worldwide reported Q2 2026 contract sales up 22% year-over-year, with VPG up 23% to $4,477, and adjusted EBITDA of $215 million, exceeding the high end of guidance. Adjusted free cash flow for the first half was $201 million versus $22 million a year ago. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $805-$830 million, a $50 million increase, and highlighted record sales months and ongoing owner engagement initiatives.

Victory Capital reported record Q2 2026 results with revenue of $435 million, up 12% sequentially and 24% year-over-year, and adjusted EPS of $2.21, up 21% quarter-over-quarter and 41% year-over-year. Total client assets reached $346 billion, up 11% from Q1, with record net long-term inflows of $4.2 billion. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 55.8%, and long-term margin guidance was raised to at least 50%. The Pioneer integration is complete, with all $110 million in net synergies realized, and management is actively pursuing M&A, citing a deep pipeline.

Via reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $136 million, up 27% year-over-year, with 847 customers (up 23% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA loss narrowing to -$3.4 million from -$8.1 million in the prior year. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $550-$553 million (26.6%-27.3% growth) while maintaining adjusted EBITDA guidance, and noted pipeline doubled for the second consecutive quarter. Gross margin expanded to 41% due to favorable mix, and adjusted net loss per share improved to -$0.01. Growth is driven by strong U.S. performance (up 35% YoY), network deals, and new AI Labs initiatives.

Vital Farms reported Q2 FY2026 net revenue of $166 million, down 10.1% year-over-year, with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $26.6 million, reflecting $28.1 million in supply management and discrete costs including excess breaker sales and butter wind-down. Management reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of $775-$800 million and adjusted EBITDA of $0-$10 million, and expects Q3 sequential revenue improvement with Q4 gross margin exiting around 30%. They noted progress on narrowing price gaps and distribution gains, but raised full-year supply management costs to mid-$30 million and took on new debt while terminating share repurchases.

Vontier reported Q2 FY2026 core sales flat, slightly ahead of guidance, aided by strong EFS performance and tariff refunds. Adjusted operating margin expanded 190 bps, with underlying expansion of 70 bps. The company raised its full-year EPS guidance, citing cost savings and a solid pipeline. Repair Solutions remains a drag with margins down 180 bps, but management is addressing it with leadership changes and operational focus.

VSE reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $449 million, up 65% year-over-year with 14% organic growth, and record adjusted EBITDA of $86 million, up 98%, with margin expanding 320 bps to 19.2%. The quarter benefitted from the PAG and NorthStar acquisitions, and management raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 61%-64% and adjusted EBITDA margin to 18.7%-19%. Integration and synergy capture are underway, with leverage at 2.4x and improving cash generation expected in the second half.

Q2 revenue was $1.64 billion, down 4% YoY (down 3% ex-divestiture), while Adjusted EBITDA rose 3% to $624 million. The company raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, though expects Q3 and Q4 EBITDA to decline YoY due to higher sports rights costs. Platforms grew 9% ex-divestiture, and advertising improved to -0.6% YoY. Management announced a $100 million accelerated share repurchase, and highlighted strategic deals including Bundesliga and Full Swing acquisition.

Verastem reported Q2 2026 net product revenues of $25.1 million, showing a meaningful rebound and quarter-over-quarter growth in CO-PACK adoption, with management confident in reaching self-sustainability for the LGSOC franchise by end of 2026. The company secured up to $75 million in non-dilutive royalty financing and a $15 million COPIKTRA milestone, extending cash runway into the second half of 2027. VS-7375 development progressed with completion of enrollment in dose expansion cohorts and initiation of three phase II registration-directed studies, with a data update expected in October. Non-GAAP adjusted net loss improved to $30.6 million versus $41.3 million in the prior year.

VTEX reported Q2 2026 subscription revenue of $63.8 million, up 11% in USD and 1.3% FX neutral, coming in just above the bottom of guidance. GMV grew 18% in USD and 7% FX neutral. Profitability was strong with non-GAAP operating income up 62% and free cash flow up 79%. Management lowered full-year FX-neutral subscription revenue guidance to low single-digit growth, citing macro headwinds in Brazil and Argentina and a mix shift to larger accounts.

Viatris delivered Q2 2026 revenue of $3.8 billion, up 3.5% operationally year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $1.2 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.69, exceeding expectations. The company raised its full-year guidance across all key financial metrics. Growth was led by Greater China (up 16% year-over-year) and strong complex generics in North America, while emerging markets declined 2% due to supply constraints. Management also highlighted strategic progress including FDA approval for Gwyn Lo, the planned sale of Tyrvaya, and continued capital returns of $550 million to shareholders.

Warner Bros. Discovery reported record streaming revenues of over $3 billion in Q2 2026, with subscriber-related revenue growth accelerating 200 basis points sequentially to 10% ex-FX. Streaming adjusted EBITDA rose more than 60% year-over-year to $512 million, a nearly 17% margin. The studio segment faced a tough film quarter due to weak releases and a difficult comparison, but management reiterated the long-term $3 billion EBITDA target. Management noted international linear advertising was weaker in Q2, and the company remains confident in its pending sale to Paramount Skydance.

WaterBridge reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $217.8 million (up 8% sequentially) and Adjusted EBITDA of $115.8 million (up ~12% sequentially), with Adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 53%. Management raised full-year 2026 volume and Adjusted EBITDA guidance for the second consecutive quarter and raised CapEx guidance by $100 million to $530-$590 million. The quarter included the closing of the Ranger acquisition, announcement of the NDB Landfill acquisition, and acceleration of the New Devon project. Speedway Phase I launched on schedule in July with volumes expected to ramp toward ~100,000 barrels per day and exit the year above that.

Walker & Dunlop's Q2 FY2026 core business grew modestly with transaction volumes up 3% to $14.4 billion and adjusted core EPS up 3% to $1.19, but reported diluted EPS was $0.09 due to $23 million in charges related to fraudulent loan repurchases. Management confirmed Freddie Mac's investigation is complete and expects $12-16 million additional charges in Q3 for Fannie Mae, with no further repurchases expected. Guidance for the year was not formally revised but management expressed confidence in core earnings excluding these charges, with GSE market share up to 15% and $114 billion in remaining GSE capacity.

Weave reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $67.5 million, up 15.5% year over year, with payments revenue growing roughly double that rate. The company added record gross and net new locations, especially in dental, and expanded adjusted operating margin to nearly 5%, up from roughly breakeven a year ago. However, management noted a go-to-market transition led to bookings slightly below expectations, reflected in the revenue outlook. CEO expressed strong optimism about demand and AI-driven monetization opportunities.

WES reported record Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $737 million, up 19% YoY, driven by Delaware Basin throughput, the Brazos acquisition (closed mid-June), and higher commodity prices. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint by $250 million to $2.85 billion, and increased DCF and FCF guidance midpoints by $200 million. Management highlighted new Powder River Basin G&P agreements adding 270,000 dedicated acres with MVCs, and expects increased throughput from customers accelerating activity into H2 2026. Q2 distribution held at $0.93 per unit.

Westrock Coffee reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net sales of approximately $306 million, up 8.8% year-over-year, with Beverage Solutions net sales growing nearly 17%. Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA was a record $21.3 million, up nearly 39% year-over-year, and the company turned free cash flow positive at $20.2 million for the quarter, ahead of schedule. Management reaffirmed the full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $90-$100 million, citing continued momentum and a robust pipeline. The company also highlighted improving operating leverage from its AI-native operating core and a structural shift to lower capital expenditures.

Willdan reported a strong Q2 FY2026 with contract revenue up 33% year-over-year to $231 million, net revenue up 23% to $117 million, and record adjusted EBITDA of $33 million, a 51% increase. Adjusted EPS rose 38% to $2.07, and GAAP EPS increased 53% to $1.58. Management raised full-year financial targets, citing robust demand, especially from commercial data center projects, and margin expansion driven by mix and AI-enabled productivity. They guided to a 25% adjusted EBITDA margin for 2026, up from 21.8% in 2025, though noted Q2's 28.2% margin was aided by revenue acceleration and may not persist.

During Q2 FY2026, WPP reported like-for-like net sales of -4.7% for H1, in line with guidance (mid-to-high single digit decline), with Q2 improving to -2.8% from Q1's -6.7%. The company maintained broadly stable margins while reinvesting cost savings into growth initiatives. Management highlighted strong new business wins and client retention improvements but noted a difficult macro environment, with Middle East down 10% and continued volatility. Guidance for the second half implies a low-to-mid single digit decline in like-for-like net sales, with easier comps of 2.9% in Q2 and a 1-point easing in Q4.

Warby Parker reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $236 million (up ~10% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of ~$33 million (14% margin), including an $11.8 million tariff refund benefit. Eye exams grew over 30% YoY to ~7% of revenue, and e-commerce glasses/contacts order volume grew low double digits excluding the Home Try-On sunset. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, excluding any Intelligent Eyewear revenue benefit, while investing ahead of the fall launch. Traffic remained soft, with late-June weakness followed by a July rebound, but the company sees e-commerce, exams, and insurance momentum and expects Home Try-On headwinds to fade through 2026.

WSC reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $612M, up 4% YoY and above the ~$585M expectation, with leasing and services revenue up 6% and D&I revenue up 25%. Adjusted EBITDA was $228M, exceeding the $223M outlook, though margins compressed ~500 bps YoY to 37.2% due to upfront activation costs and mix. Management modestly raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance, citing strong modular activations (up 16% YoY), order book growth (up 13% YoY), and enterprise account revenue up 21%, while noting headwinds in transactional product lines and a step-down from World Cup activity in Q3.

W&T Offshore reported Q2 2026 net income of $12.6 million ($0.08 per share) and adjusted EBITDA of $54 million, in line with Q1. Free cash flow rose 50% sequentially to $31 million, and net debt fell to $200 million with leverage at 1.2x. Production was 34.7 MBOE/d at the midpoint of guidance and up 3% year-over-year, while LOE was below the low end of guidance. The company reiterated full-year guidance and guided Q3 production above 35 MBOE/d midpoint, with management expressing confidence in the balance sheet and litigation upside.

Watts Water delivered record second-quarter sales of $763 million, up 19% reported and 12% organic, with adjusted EPS of $3.66, up 18%. Data center sales more than tripled year-over-year and reached 8% of total sales in the first half. Management raised full-year organic sales growth guidance to 8-11% and adjusted operating margin expansion to up 20-80 basis points, citing better-than-expected data center growth, price, and Europe/APMEA performance. However, macro softness persists in residential and non-institutional construction, and Middle East conflict and tariff uncertainty remain headwinds.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was $151M, or $149.4M excluding $1.6M non-recurring settlement revenue, up 3% YoY. Total consumables revenue grew 7%, with double-digit growth in Chromium consumable reaction volumes. The company highlighted exceptionally strong early order flow for the new Atera spatial platform, exceeding the prior 40-instrument guidance, and announced the acquisition of Proteintech Genomics to enhance proteomics capabilities. Management guided to sequential consumables revenue step-down in Q3 due to Atera transition, then a step-up in Q4 largely driven by Atera instrument shipments.

Xeris reported record Q2 2026 total revenue of $92.1 million, up 29% year-over-year, and net product revenue of $91 million, up 34%. RECORLEV grew 81% to $56.8 million, Gvoke rebounded sequentially to $22.5 million, and KEVEYIS delivered $11.7 million. Adjusted EBITDA rose over 50% to $19.3 million. The company raised the bottom end of full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $385-390 million, reflecting 33% growth at the midpoint. It also fully retired its convertible notes with a one-time non-cash charge of $31 million, and advanced its XP-8121 pipeline toward a planned phase III start by year-end.

US Foods delivered record adjusted EBITDA of $604 million, up 10%, with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 29 basis points to a record 5.7%. Adjusted EPS grew 21%. Independent restaurant case growth reached 5.1%, the strongest since Q4 2023, with 21st consecutive quarter of share gains. The company raised Pronto sales guidance to $1.3 billion for 2026 and $1.7 billion for 2027, up from prior estimates. Management remains confident in achieving over $300 million in cost savings by 2027, with $50 million already realized in H1 2026.

Unusual Machines reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $16.7 million, up 687% year-over-year and 107% quarter-over-quarter, with enterprise sales accounting for about 95% of revenue. GAAP net loss narrowed to $0.16 per share from $0.32 a year ago, and adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $400,000 from $1.6 million in Q1. Gross margin was 34.7%, slightly below target due to scaling. The company raised $60 million at $30 per share in May, ending the quarter with $229 million cash and over $367 million in working capital. Management reiterates strong demand and supply constraints through 2027, citing the Drone Dominance Gauntlet and other government programs, but acknowledges infrastructure buildout is needed and that Q3 will not show top-line impact from these investments.

SVC reported Q2 2026 Normalized FFO of $55M, down 4.5% YoY, in line with consensus; per-share FFO was $0.43. RevPAR for retained hotels grew 6.6% YoY and 9% excluding Nautilus disruption; July RevPAR grew 7.1%. Net lease NOI increased 2.2% QoQ, occupancy at 96.6%, TA rent coverage improved to 1.34x. Management maintained full-year guidance and continues capital recycling with hotel dispositions and debt reduction.

Urban Edge Properties reported a strong Q2 2026 with FFO as adjusted of $0.40 per share, up 10% year-over-year, and same-property NOI growth of 3.2%. The company raised its full-year FFO guidance by $0.02 to $1.50-$1.54 per share and increased the low end of same-property NOI guidance to 3.25%. Leasing activity remains robust with new lease cash spreads of 13% in the quarter and nearly 30% year-to-date, though shop occupancy dipped to 91.7% due to strategic recaptures and the Wren Kitchens bankruptcy. Capital recycling continued with acquisitions in Virginia and Massachusetts funded by asset sales, and management expressed confidence in continued rent growth driven by limited supply and strong demand.

Savers Value Village reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $448 million, up 7.4% with U.S. comps up 6.6%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 8% to $75 million with margins at 16.6%. The company is rolling out ThriftIQ, which has shown 100 basis points higher gross profit growth in pilot stores. Guidance was updated to net sales of $1.77-$1.79 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $265-$275 million for FY2026.

In Q2 FY2026, Molson Coors reported net sales revenue down 3.6%, underlying pre-tax income down 27.8%, and underlying EPS down 22.9% on a constant currency basis. The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 guidance despite challenging category conditions, cost inflation (including $40 million higher COGS from Midwest premium), and a U.S. industry decline of 4.2%. Management highlighted progress in portfolio transformation, with Monaco and Fever-Tree each on track to contribute 1-2% of NSR, while noting continued share pressure in core brands and heightened competition in EMEA-APAC.

Turtle Beach reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $56.4 million, essentially flat year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to 38.8% including tariff refunds (excluding one-time items, about 31.2%). Adjusted EBITDA improved to $1.3 million from -$3.0 million, but net loss widened to $7.3 million due to increased marketing and higher interest. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance of $335-$355 million revenue and $44-$48 million adjusted EBITDA, citing strong second-half catalysts like GTA VI and Call of Duty. They highlighted early Q3 weekly year-over-year watch-through growth and repurchased $25 million of stock in the quarter.

Q2 FY2026 results showed adjusted NII of $0.21 per share, NAV declined 2.1% to $6.58 due to portfolio markdowns, and non-accruals improved to 1.6% at fair value. Management announced a major portfolio sale to a continuation vehicle at a 5% discount, reducing NAV by 10.4% but cutting net leverage to ~0.4x, and initiated a strategic review with KBW. Repayment activity was strong, and the Domo sale is expected to repay $69 million in Q4.

Tucows Q2 FY2026 revenue increased 2% YoY to $100.6M with gross profit up 17% to $25.8M, but adjusted EBITDA declined 2% YoY to $12.3M and GAAP net loss widened to -$20.5M. Ting posted its first positive adjusted EBITDA quarter (+$1.5M) with revenue up 32% YoY, while Domains revenue declined 4% but gross profit was stable. Wavelo revenue and profitability declined, and corporate headwinds from mobile and higher professional fees persisted. Management completed a credit facility extension and retired Ting preferred equity, but guided that corporate results face continued headwinds and mobile resolution is actively being sought.

USA TODAY Co. reported Q2 2026 with positive net income for a second consecutive quarter, $20 million free cash flow (up 11% year-over-year), and record digital-only ARPU (up 34% year-over-year). Digital-only subscription revenue grew for the second consecutive quarter and digital other revenue also grew, but content licensing was lumpy and search-driven traffic declined. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, expecting improved revenue trends, EBITDA and margin expansion, and fourth consecutive year of free cash flow growth, with a goal of becoming majority digital in the back half of 2026.

Triple Flag reported a strong Q2 with nearly 29,000 GEOs sold, $117 million adjusted EBITDA, and operating cash flow per share up 42% year-over-year. The company announced a settlement with Steppe Gold, closed the Ravenswood acquisition, raised 2026 guidance to 100,000-110,000 GEOs, and increased its dividend for the fifth consecutive year. Management expressed confidence in continued growth, citing multiple development projects and a strong balance sheet with over $1.1 billion in liquidity.

Teleflex reported Q2 2026 revenues of $570.3 million, up 4.7% on a pro forma adjusted constant currency basis, with adjusted EPS of $1.76, a 1.7% increase year-over-year. Adjusted operating margin was 19.6%, and gross margin declined 280 basis points to 61.7% due to tariffs and the VI acquisition. The company beat revenue, margin, and EPS expectations, with strong Vascular and Surgical growth, but Interventional revenue declined 1% due to slower-than-expected VI integration. Management raised adjusted EPS guidance while tempering full-year revenue outlook, and closed the OEM divestiture, returning capital via share repurchases and debt reduction.

Trekor reported record revenue of CAD 331 million in Q2 FY2026, with adjusted EBITDA of CAD 125 million and operating cash flow of CAD 183 million. Florence produced over 5 million lbs of cathode in its first full production quarter, while Gibraltar produced 30 million lbs; the company maintained annual guidance. Management expressed confidence in ramp-up progress and highlighted strong copper prices and a contracted negative TC of -CAD 140/t for 2027, while noting cost pressures and higher sustaining capital.

Tecnoglass reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $295.3 million, up 15.6% YoY, with record backlog of $1.4 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $51.7 million (17.5% margin). Margins fell sharply due to higher aluminum costs (+77% YoY), peso appreciation, and Section 232 tariffs ($17M expense). Management narrowed FY2026 revenue guidance to $1.08-1.12B and adjusted EBITDA to $220-230M, expecting Q3 EBITDA roughly flat sequentially. Demand remains strong, pricing actions are flowing through starting Q3, and automation is on track, but margin headwinds persist.

TIC Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $584 million, up 3.3% year-over-year (organic growth 2.5%). Adjusted gross margin expanded 135 basis points to 38.2%. C&E grew 16.8% to $207 million, Geo grew 7.9% to $81 million, but I&M declined 5.5% to $297 million due to site losses and outage timing. Combined backlog rose 20% to a record $1.18 billion, and the company expects improved growth in the second half.

Millicom delivered record Q2 FY2026 results: service revenue of $2 billion, up 5% organically YoY (strongest since 2021) and 60.1% reported; adjusted EBITDA of $1 billion (first time surpassing that milestone) with organic growth of 9.1% YoY; record equity free cash flow of $327 million, up 50%+ YoY. Management raised FY2026 equity free cash flow guidance from at least $900 million to around $1.1 billion and improved the year-end leverage target to below 2.5x. The board approved an additional interim dividend of $1.50 per share payable in two installments.

Q2 FY2026 net sales grew 1.7% YoY to $324 million, in line with guidance, while orders rose 6.6% and backlog reached $127 million. Robotics AMR sales grew 37% YoY, but gross margin and adjusted EBITDA fell short due to ERP optimization delays, EMEA competitive pressures, and higher operating expenses. Management raised full-year net sales outlook and lowered adjusted EBITDA guidance, citing slower ERP recovery and ongoing cost pressures.

Tandem reported record Q2 sales of $255 million, up 6% YoY, with 33,000 pumps shipped worldwide (10%+ YoY growth). Gross margin improved to 57%, up 5 points YoY, and the company reiterated full-year guidance despite infusion set supply constraints. Pharmacy channel adoption reached 10% of U.S. sales in the first full quarter of PayGo, and management expects continued momentum into 2027 with the Mobi Tubeless launch.

Starling Oncology reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $161.3 million, up 34.6% year-over-year, driven by Specialty Pharmacy growth of 57.6%. Gross margin improved to 16.8% from 14.6%, and adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $0.2 million versus a loss of $4.1 million a year ago. The company raised full-year revenue and gross profit guidance, narrowed adjusted EBITDA to $2-7 million, and announced new capitated contracts, including a California exclusivity expansion adding 230,000 lives. Management remains confident in achieving positive adjusted EBITDA for the year.

TPL reported record quarterly total revenue of ~$246M, up 31% YoY, with record net income and free cash flow of $156M. Oil and gas royalty production averaged ~39,700 BOE/d, up 20% YoY, and produced water royalty volumes rose 15% YoY. The company reaffirmed FY CapEx guidance of $65-75M and highlighted progress on data center/power initiatives, including a $100M land acquisition in Shackelford/Jones County and completion of a desalination facility. Management expressed confidence in near-term deal announcements despite a sequential decline in water sales volumes due to weak gas prices.

Targa Resources reported record Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.603 billion, up 14% sequentially and 38% year-over-year, driven by record Permian volumes of 7.2 Bcf/d, record NGL transportation and fractionation volumes, and record LPG exports. Management raised expectations to the top end of the $5.7-$5.9 billion full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance range, suggesting near $1 billion growth over 2025. Marketing optimization outperformed by ~$250 million in H1, though some of that is expected to moderate in H2. Dividend increased 25% to $1.25 per share, with $80 million of buybacks in Q2.

In Q2 FY2026, TripAdvisor's continuing operations (experiences and hotels) reported revenue of $442M and adjusted EBITDA of $76M, with revenue in line and EBITDA above expectations. Experiences bookings grew 5% overall, with Viator up 10%, but TripAdvisor POS faced SEO headwinds (~5 pts of growth drag). Hotels revenue declined 21% due to sustained volume headwinds. Management announced the sale of TheFork for $700M, expects to close before year-end, and reiterated long-term confidence in experiences while remaining cautious on macro and Q3 guidance.

Tronox reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $868 million, up 19% YoY, driven by strong TiO2 and zircon volumes, with TiO2 volumes at the high end of guidance and zircon exceeding expectations. Adjusted EBITDA was $73 million, down 22% YoY due to exchange headwinds, pricing, and costs, but within guided range. Pricing improved sequentially for both TiO2 and zircon, and the company expects further sequential price increases and EBITDA of $95-$115 million in Q3, with positive full-year free cash flow. Management highlighted anti-dumping progress, including India and a context reinstatement of duties on Chinese TiO2, and noted cost headwinds from Middle East conflict and input costs.

Trevi's Q2 2026 call highlights continued pipeline execution: OCEAN-1 phase III and LAKE-2b phase IIb trials initiated, with OCEAN-2 expected in Q3. Cash of ~$319M extends runway into 2030, funding IPF and non-IPF ILD programs. The highly anticipated FDA meeting for non-IPF ILD is a near-term catalyst, and the competitive RCC program termination is viewed positively, reinforcing Trevi's potential first-in-class position. Guidance unchanged.

Tenaris reported Q2 sales of $3 billion, down 4% YoY and sequentially, with EBITDA down 12% sequentially to $649 million and net income down 13% to $492 million, primarily due to Strait of Hormuz disruption and higher costs. Management kept H2 2026 revenue and EBITDA guidance in line with H1, with Q4 expected to improve on volume and pricing as offshore backlog and North American activity ramp. The board doubled the interim dividend to ~$600 million, signaling sustained capital returns. Full-year outlook is underpinned by higher prices and cost recovery, but the reopening of Hormuz is removed from the base case.

Revenue growth fell short of expectations due to macro pressures on CPG and auto advertisers, with revenue under JBPs growing 6x faster than overall revenue. The company highlighted product launches (measurement framework, Audience Unlimited, Zuma) and strong regional growth (EMEA/APAC ~30% YoY, China >100% YoY) but guided conservatively with limited visibility. Leadership changes were emphasized as a driver of future improvement.

TWFG reported a strong Q2 2026 with total revenues up 45.1% to $87.5 million, organic revenue growth of 37%, and adjusted EBITDA up 75.8% to $26.6 million with 530 bps margin expansion. MGA channel commission income grew 290%, while consolidated written premium retention improved to 93%. Management raised 2026 guidance across revenue, organic growth, and adjusted EBITDA margins, citing strong MGA performance and acquisitions.

Twilio delivered record Q2 revenue of $1.5 billion, up 22% reported and 17% organic year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross profit growth accelerating to 18%. The company raised its full-year organic revenue growth guidance to 13%-13.5% from 9.5%-10.5% and raised full-year non-GAAP operating income and free cash flow guidance. Management highlighted strong growth in messaging, voice, and software add-ons, plus early customer wins for the new Conversations Layer.

Revenue for Q2 FY2026 was $151 million, or $149.4 million excluding non-recurring settlement revenue, up 3% YoY. Total consumables revenue grew 7%, with strong growth in Chromium and Xenium utilization. The company launched Atera, a new spatial platform, and reported very strong early order flow exceeding initial expectations, with 40+ instruments expected to ship in the second half, mostly in Q4. Management raised guidance, expecting a sequential step-up in Q3 to Q4 revenue driven by Atera instrument sales and consumables, while noting some near-term cannibalization of Xenium and Visium orders.

Q2 revenue approached $1.7 billion, up 11.1%, with comparable sales up 6.2% and traffic up 3%. Restaurant margin dollars rose 6.9% though margin as a percentage of sales declined 66 bps. Diluted EPS decreased 0.7% to $1.85. Commodity inflation guidance was lowered to approximately 5% for the full year, and the company plans a 1% menu price increase in Q4. Development remains on track with 35 company openings planned for 2026.

Unity reported a record Q2 with strategic revenue up 63% year-over-year to $329 million, driven by Vector's 23% quarter-over-quarter growth. Adjusted EBITDA grew 77% to $160 million with margins at 29%, and free cash flow hit $202 million. The company raised Q3 guidance to 44-47% strategic revenue growth and pulled forward GAAP net income profitability to Q3. Key strategic moves include closing the Supersonic sale, sunsetting the ironSource ad network, and investing in AppsFlyer.

Xponential Fitness reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $66.0 million, down 13% year-over-year, with same-store sales down 6.8% globally (Club Pilates down 5%). The company lowered full-year guidance due to weaker same-store sales, merchandise revenue challenges, and Q2 shortfall. Management highlighted initiatives to improve top-of-funnel and digital experiences, while the strategic alternatives review continues.

Q2 FY2026 revenue declined 4.1% as reported (6.3% constant currency), with adjusted EPS flat at $0.52, supported by $44 million in tariff refunds. The company maintained its 2026 outlook of $3.5-$3.6 billion net sales and adjusted EPS of $1.40-$1.50, excluding tariff refunds. Management expects Q3 earnings to be below Q2, with improvement weighted to Q4 as investments ramp.

Exzeo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $58 million, up from $56 million sequentially, with adjusted revenue exceeding $56 million, up $4 million YoY. Managed Premium grew to $1.4 billion, Adjusted EBITDA margin was above 53%, pre-tax income was over $31 million (above guidance), and EPS was $0.26. Full-year guidance remains unchanged, with Q3 pre-tax income expected between $28-$31 million and Managed Premium around $1.4 billion. The company also signed GEICO as its eighth carrier, doubled agent count and quote volume year-to-date, and launched Exzeo Ventures for AI-driven initiatives.

Yelp's Q2 2026 revenue rose 1% YoY to $376 million, $8 million above the high end of guidance, but Adjusted EBITDA fell 9% to $91 million and net income dropped 28%. Services ad revenue was flat YoY, RR&O ad revenue declined 10%, and paying ad locations fell 1%. Other revenue surged 98% YoY to $33 million, driven by Hatch, data licensing, and food orders, with Hatch annual run-rate revenue up 59% to $35 million. Management guided Q3 revenue to $365-370 million and full-year revenue to $1.460-1.470 billion (narrowed lower at the top end), with Q3 Adjusted EBITDA expected at $70-75 million and full-year at $315-325 million, reflecting continued investments.

Peloton delivered Q4 FY2026 revenue of $608M, slightly above guidance, with gross margin up 260bps to 56.7%. Adjusted EBITDA was $142M (or $166M excluding one-time legal contingencies), above guidance, and FY2026 marked the first full year of positive net income ($63M) and operating income ($161M). Management projects record gross margin, EBITDA, and net income in FY2027, while expecting churn to be roughly flat year-over-year. The company is also executing a balance-sheet refinancing and plans new consumer product launches in fall 2027.

QuinStreet reported record Q4 FY2026 with revenue up 43% YoY to $373.9M and adjusted EBITDA up 87% to $41.4M, driving margin expansion. Full-year revenue grew 18% to $1.3B with adjusted EBITDA up 38%, and the company guided to continued strong growth in FY2027, expecting 16% revenue growth and 38% EBITDA growth at the midpoint, with opportunities for upside. The home services vertical, boosted by HomeBuddy, grew 88% YoY, while financial services grew 24% with auto insurance up 37%.

ResMed reported Q4 FY2026 revenue growth of 8% constant currency, non-GAAP EPS up 16%, and gross margin expansion. For FY2026, they achieved 10% headline revenue growth, 180bps operating margin expansion, and over $1.6 billion in free cash flow. They announced a 10% dividend increase, accelerated buybacks, and raised FY2027 guidance that beats consensus. The company also closed the Noctrix acquisition, plans to divest MatrixCare, and reaffirmed tariff relief for their products.

Atlassian reported Q4 FY2026 total revenue of $1.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year, with cloud revenue growing 31% to $1.2 billion. RPO grew 44% to $4.8 billion, and GAAP operating margin was 12%. Management highlighted record enterprise deal activity, with $3M+ ARR customers growing over 50% and $5M+ ARR customers growing over 70%. Guidance for FY2027 subscription ARR growth is 18%, down from 23% in FY2026, reflecting prudence on macro uncertainty and the DX acquisition boost lapping.

AMSC reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $94.1 million, up 30% year-over-year, with Grid up 27% and Wind up 45%. GAAP net income was $9.5 million ($0.21 per share), while non-GAAP net income was $7.6 million ($0.17 per share), down from $0.30 a year ago due to purchase accounting and tax timing. Orders reached over $130 million, including a record $25 million mining utility order, and 12-month backlog exceeded $300 million. Q2 guidance calls for revenue above $85 million and non-GAAP EPS above $0.17, with fiscal 2026 expected to be better than fiscal 2025.

Q1 FY2027 adjusted revenues fell 5.2% YoY to CAD 698M and adjusted EPS was CAD 0.35. Adjusted EBIT dropped 13.4% to CAD 68.1M, with gross margin up 18 bps to 30%. Management initiated an 18-month Fixed-Cost Transformation Program targeting ~CAD 20M annualized savings in the first phase (Europe), about 30% of total opportunity, and reiterated the 15% operating margin target. Q2 revenue guidance is CAD 660M-CAD 700M, with margins expected to strengthen in H2.

In Q1 FY2027, Coincheck Group reported total revenue of JPY 114.3 billion ($703M), up 36% YoY, driven by institutional and covered counterparty transaction revenue. Adjusted revenue rose 19% to JPY 2.92 billion ($18M), boosted by a full quarter of 3iQ staking and investment management fees. Customer assets fell 37% to JPY 631.6 billion due to crypto price declines, and adjusted EBITDA loss widened to JPY 516 million from JPY 398 million in the prior year. Management emphasized strategic partnerships (Mercari, KDDI, Credit Saison) and progress in Japan's regulatory framework, positioning for future growth.

Doximity reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $157M, up 7% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $75M (48% margin), both exceeding the high end of guidance. The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $6M to $671-$681M, while maintaining EBITDA guidance at $309-$329M as it accelerates AI investments. AI Search launched late April, with first cohort onboarded and majority of contracted revenue expected to be recognized in Q3. Q2 guidance implies 1% YoY growth due to tough comparison, with stronger growth expected in Q3.

Gen delivered Q1 FY2027 with bookings and revenue both up 11% year-over-year, above the high end of guidance, and non-GAAP EPS grew 19%. The company raised full-year FY2027 guidance to 9%-11% revenue growth and 14%-18% EPS growth. Cyber Safety grew mid-single digits, while Trust-Based Solutions grew 25%, with Engine crossing a $500 million annual revenue run rate. Management highlighted record paid customers of over 80 million and continued margin stability at 50%.

Graham Corporation delivered record first-quarter revenue of $71.3 million, up 29% YoY (17% organic), with defense revenue up 40%, space up 86%, and energy/process up 5%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 28% to $8.8 million, but gross margin declined to 25% from 26.5% on sales mix. Backlog reached a record $557 million, and the company reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 guidance of 18% revenue growth and 44% adjusted EBITDA growth, alongside a three-year framework for 8-10% organic growth and 14-16% EBITDA margins by FY2029.

Haemonetics reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $339 million, up 6% reported and organic, and adjusted EPS of $1.14, up 4% year-over-year. The company raised full-year guidance for revenue growth to 5%-8% reported and 4%-7% organic, while reaffirming operating margin expansion of 50-100 basis points. MedSurg grew 6%, apheresis grew 6% organic, and interventional technologies returned to 3% organic growth. Free cash flow conversion was 75% for the quarter, with $50 million debt repaid during the quarter and another $50 million after quarter end.

Roivant reported a quiet Q1 FY2027 with $200M R&D expense, ~$100M non-GAAP G&A, and cash just under $4B before receiving $772M from Moderna's settlement. The company initiated Phase III for cutaneous sarcoidosis ahead of schedule, with top-line data expected in 2028. Management reiterated readiness for brepocitinib launch in dermatomyositis by end of September and expects a busy second half with multiple readouts. They continue share repurchases, having bought back ~$200M in the quarter at average high-$20s per share.

ORIX reported record first-quarter net income of JPY 280.8 billion, up JPY 173.5 billion year-over-year, driven by Kioxia-related gains and strong core earnings. Full-year net income guidance remains at JPY 530 billion, but first-half profit is forecast at JPY 840 billion, including JPY 540 billion of Kioxia gains. The dividend policy was revised to exclude Kioxia gains from adjusted profit, resulting in an interim DPS of JPY 107.27. Management expressed confidence in growing adjusted profits in the second half.

Q1 FY2027 results beat expectations with net sales of $1.47B, up 12% pro forma, and Adjusted EBITDA of $422M (28.6% margin), both above the high end of guidance. Fiber cement organic growth was 20%, driven by strategic initiatives and a destocking comp. Management raised the full-year guide, maintains cost pressures of $80-100M, and confirmed synergy targets. They also announced expanded distribution agreements and redeemed $400M of notes, reducing leverage to 2.7x.

Lionsgate Studios reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $777 million, up 48% year-over-year, with adjusted OIBDA of $79 million and adjusted EPS of $0.06. Motion picture revenue more than doubled to $587 million, driven by Michael and The Housemaid, achieving record first-quarter segment profit. The company hit its mid-4x leverage target early, ending net debt at $1.5 billion, and reaffirmed fiscal 2027 growth outlook, citing a $1.5 billion backlog and upcoming Hunger Games release. TV revenue declined on timing but management expects significant growth later in the year.

Microchip reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $1.485 billion, up 13.2% sequentially and 38% year-over-year, beating the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP EPS was $0.76, $0.07 above the midpoint, with gross margin at 63.8%, operating margin at 35.1%, and strong free cash flow. Data center sales soared 97.8% year-over-year, with full-year 2026 data center sales expected to reach ~$1 billion, up 69%. September quarter guidance is for net sales up 8% sequentially and non-GAAP EPS of $0.91-$0.95, with gross margin forecast at 66%-67%, above the long-term target of 65%. Bookings were the strongest in about four years, and distribution inventory correction is complete, with lead times stretching due to capacity constraints.

Q1 FY2027 revenue was $1.485 billion, up 13.2% sequentially and 38% year-over-year, beating the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.76 beat guidance by $0.07; gross margin expanded to 63.8% (up 222 bps sequentially) and operating margin to 35.1% (up 452 bps sequentially). Guidance for September quarter is strong: revenue up 8% sequentially, gross margin 66-67%, EPS $0.91-$0.95 (up 165.7% YoY at midpoint). Data center sales are booming, up 97.8% YoY in the June quarter, with calendar 2026 expected to reach ~$1 billion (up 69% YoY).

NetScout's Q1 FY2027 revenue rose 12.7% to $210.4 million, with EPS up to $0.52 from $0.34. Growth was driven by service assurance (up 19.7%) and government orders pulled forward by $10-15 million; normalized growth was mid-single digits. The company reaffirmed its full-year outlook and highlighted strong margin expansion (operating margin up 660 bps to 20.8%). Cybersecurity grew only 0.6% due to a tough comparison, but management remains optimistic on long-term opportunities.

Prestige Consumer Healthcare reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $265.7 million, up 6.5% YoY, with organic growth of 3.2%, and adjusted EPS of $0.98, up from $0.95. The company raised its full-year guidance to include the Breathe Right and LaCorium acquisitions, expecting adjusted gross margin of just over 57% and at least $270 million in adjusted free cash flow. Growth was driven by GI and dermatological categories, while Clear Eyes remained supply constrained and international revenue fell 2.1% organically due to order timing.

Q1 FY2027 revenue grew 13% in constant currency, exceeding the mid-to-high single-digit outlook, with Asia up 25%, North America up 13%, and Europe up 5%. Adjusted gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 73.6%, and AUR increased 15%. The company raised its full-year outlook while maintaining caution on Europe due to macro uncertainty. New customer acquisition was 1.5 million in DTC, and core product sales grew mid-teens.

Roivant reported a quiet Q1 FY2026 with R&D expense of ~$200 million, non-GAAP adjusted G&A just under $100 million, and cash of just under $4 billion before receiving the $772 million Moderna settlement payment. The company is on track for a brepocitinib launch in dermatomyositis by end of September, with patient enrollment completed in the phase III cutaneous sarcoidosis study. Management expects a busy second half with multiple data readouts and remains committed to a slow and steady launch approach. Share repurchases accelerated, with ~$200 million in the quarter at an average price in the high $20s.

Q1 FY2027 results showed as-reported revenue growth of 7% and constant currency organic growth of 6%, with EPS of $2.59, up 11% YoY. Gross margin expanded 70 bps to 46%, and EBIT margin rose 100 bps to 23.8%. The company maintained its FY2027 revenue and EPS guidance, and announced a $600 million investment in a new Formulated Chemistry Center of Excellence, increasing CapEx guidance to ~$450 million, while keeping free cash flow at $800 million. Healthcare services grew 10% and consumables 9%, but AST services volume was soft due to inventory destocking, with expectations of acceleration in the second half.

StepStone reported strong Q1 FY2027 results: fee-related earnings of $106 million, up 30% YoY, with a 39% FRE margin; adjusted EPS of $0.48, up from $0.40. Gross inflows were $10 billion, with record private wealth subscriptions of $2.8 billion and SPRING inflows of $1.7 billion. Management raised the quarterly dividend by 18% to $0.33 per share, and repurchased shares. They see no limiting factor to sustaining multi-billion dollar inflows, with expansion into defined contribution and data/tech partnerships as long-term growth levers.

Q1 FY2027 EPS fell to $0.63 from $0.73, with net income down to $123 million from $142 million. Equipment rental and storage revenues grew modestly, but operating expenses rose $55 million, including a $22.5 million freight cost increase, pressuring margins. Same-store occupancy fell 456 basis points to 88.3% due to the prior year's hard line on delinquencies. Management expects freight costs to peak in July and then ease, but remains cautious about inflation and the resale market.

In Q1 FY2027, Universal Corp reported consolidated revenue of $524 million, down 12% year-over-year, and an operating income of $2.3 million versus $33.8 million in the prior year, driven by a steep decline in tobacco segment operating income from $35.7 million to $3.5 million due to oversupply and delayed customer watching. The ingredients segment posted a $700,000 operating loss as consumer headwinds and high fixed costs persisted. Management maintains full-year customer demand is consistent with plan, with second-half-weighted shipments expected, and sees less risk of large inventory write-downs. The company noted a net loss of $5 million versus a net income of $8.5 million last year, but highlighted net debt reduction of $52 million and a $1.1 billion liquidity position.

ADS reported record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $1 billion, up 21% YoY, with organic growth of 9% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 35.8%, the second highest in company history. Results benefited from $25-30 million of demand pulled forward ahead of price increases; excluding that, organic growth was mid-single digits. Management maintained full-year guidance of $3.35-3.55 billion sales and $1.0-1.05 billion EBITDA, citing dynamic inflation and a tepid demand environment. Non-residential end markets beat expectations, while residential demand was modestly worse.

HUTCHMED reported strong H1 2026 results with oncology revenue of $162 million, up 23% year-over-year, and China product sales growth led by ELUNATE and SULANDA at over 40%. FRUZAQLA ex-U.S. in-market sales grew 70%, and the company remained profitable with net income of $16 million. Full-year guidance was reiterated at $330-$415 million, with management confident of at least beating the lower end and potentially exceeding the high end with business development and milestones. The company advanced its ATTC pipeline with two assets in Phase I and a third IND cleared, and expects key data readouts from SAFFRON and SANOVO in H2.

Parker-Hannifin reported record Q4 FY2026 results with sales up 10% (organic up 8%), adjusted segment operating margin up 110 bps to 28.0%, and adjusted EPS up 21% to $9.27. Full-year sales hit $21.5 billion with organic growth of 6.6% and adjusted EPS of $32.31, up 18%. Management raised the long-term margin target to 30% by FY2031 and initiated FY2027 guidance of 7% organic sales growth at the midpoint, with all market verticals guiding positive for the first time. Order rates accelerated across segments, with total orders up 19% on a 3-month basis and Aerospace backlog up 15% to a record $8.5 billion.

OpenText reported Q4 FY2026 total revenue of $1.35 billion, up 2.9% YoY (0.9% constant currency), with core portfolio revenue up 5.3% (3.1% cc) and cloud revenue up 6.0% (4.3% cc). Core cloud revenue grew 8.9% cc, and enterprise cloud bookings rose 24.1% YoY, above the 16%-20% target. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 37.1%, non-GAAP EPS was $1.23 (up 26.8%), and operating cash flow was $186 million (up 17.5%). Management guided FY2027 core revenue growth of 2%-3% and cloud revenue growth of 8%-10%, calling FY2027 a 'foundation year' with investments in sales capacity and ecosystem partnerships.

Fox delivered record fiscal 2026 results with revenue up 5% to over $17 billion and EBITDA up 8% to a record $3.9 billion. Q4 revenue grew 28% to $4.2 billion and EBITDA grew 27% to $1.2 billion, driven by a 78% advertising revenue increase from the FIFA World Cup and Tubi's 35% revenue growth. Management raised the semi-annual dividend to $0.29 and expects continued momentum in fiscal 2027 with World Cup knockout stages and midterm elections. The pending Roku acquisition is on track for closing in first half calendar 2027.

Liquidity Services reported strong Q3 FY2026 results with GMV up 10% to a record $453 million, revenue up 8% to $129.6 million, GAAP EPS up 39% to $0.32, and Adjusted EBITDA up 30% to $22 million, marking the 10th consecutive quarter of YoY EBITDA growth. Retail and GovDeals segments achieved record GMV and profitability, while CAG GMV declined 1% but direct profit rose 13% on a 270 bps take rate improvement. Guidance for Q4 projects GMV of $450-$455 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $22-$25 million, positioning FY2026 for the highest annual Adjusted EBITDA in 13 years.

Q2 2026 net product revenue grew 11% sequentially to $105.8 million, with the commercial business remaining profitable. Management emphasized pipeline progress, including zoci moving toward global pivotal trials and expected U.S. accelerated approval in 2028, plus ZL-1503 first-in-human data later this year. They guided for stable operating expenses and expect a return to meaningful growth in 2027, with potential first U.S. product launch in 2028. The tone is confident but acknowledges near-term revenue impact from NRDL dynamics and supply constraints.

Zoetis reported Q2 FY2026 organic revenue and adjusted net income declines of 1% and 2% respectively, with U.S. revenue down 7% and companion animal portfolio down 6%, while international grew 6% and livestock grew 11%. The company cited intensified competitive pressure and softer clinic visits, leading to increased promotional spending and a revised full-year outlook reflecting continued near-term headwinds. Management highlighted strength in diagnostics (revenue up 12%) and livestock, but acknowledged price realization could be flat to -2% for the year due to gross-to-net adjustments.

Atmos Energy reported fiscal 2026 YTD EPS of $7.33, up 14.5% year-over-year, and reaffirmed full-year EPS guidance of $8.40-$8.50. Strong rate increases and customer growth drove operating income, but APT spreads narrowed sharply in late June/July as new takeaway capacity came online sooner than expected, leading management to guide toward the lower end of the $0.08-$0.12 second-half APT range. O&M guidance was raised to $875-$885 million, and capital spending remains on track at ~$4.2 billion.

BD reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $5 billion, up 4.4% FX-neutral, with adjusted EPS of $3.23, up 4.9%, both ahead of expectations. The quarter saw double-digit growth across key platforms like biologic drug delivery, APM, PureWick, and advanced tissue regeneration, partially offset by Alaris and China vaccines headwinds. Management raised the midpoint of full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $12.62-$12.72 and now expects revenue growth toward the high end of the low-single-digit range. Margins contracted due to tariffs but productivity gains continued, and free cash flow rose 45% year-to-date.

Q3 FY2026 revenue was $138M, up 1% sequentially; GAAP net loss narrowed to $240M from $378M, driven by a smaller Bitcoin mark-to-market loss. Adjusted EBITDA was negative $113M including that non-cash item, but positive $20M when normalized. The major event was a 20-year triple net lease at Sandersville for $6.6B in contracted revenue (up to $11.6B with extensions), with the Texas portfolio under exclusivity for 885MW. Management reaffirmed no equity raise for Sandersville and expects project financing at >90% loan-to-cost.

Compass Minerals reported Q3 FY2026 total Adjusted EBITDA of $39.9 million, slightly down from $41 million a year ago, with a net loss of $5.7 million improved from a $17 million loss. Salt revenue rose 5% to $173.9 million on 9% pricing gains, but salt Adjusted EBITDA fell 15% due to higher costs and lower volumes. Plant Nutrition Adjusted EBITDA jumped 32% to $15 million, prompting a full-year segment guidance raise to $49-$57 million. Management raised consolidated EBITDA guidance midpoint to $230 million (range $218-$242 million) but narrowed salt guidance, citing cost pressures and operational delays; bid season pricing is strong with double-digit increases, but tariffs remain a risk.

Cerence reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of approximately $70 million, within guidance and up 12% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $13.5 million beating the high end of guidance and free cash flow of $20 million. The company raised FY2026 free cash flow guidance to $76-82 million, authorized its first share repurchase program, and highlighted continued growth in Connected Services revenue (up >20% YoY) as well as progress with Cerence xUI, including a new Stellantis deal and a first customer for Mobile Work Agent. Variable license revenue declined 15% YoY due to a tough comparison, but xUI ramp and non-auto growth are expected to support FY2027 growth.

ESCO Technologies reported Q3 FY2026 with 14% sales growth (8% organic), adjusted EPS of $2.20 (up 37.5%), and record backlog of $1.54 billion. Book-to-bill was 1.21 across all segments, with test orders up 42% and Doble orders up 30%. Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $8.30-$8.40, up 38%-39% from prior year, and management remains confident in long-term demand drivers across aerospace, utility, and test markets.

EZCORP reported a strong fiscal Q3 2026 with adjusted EBITDA up 48% to $65.6 million and adjusted diluted EPS up 47% to $0.47. Core pawn revenues grew 24% and core pawn gross profit rose 28%, with same-store core pawn gross profit up 13%. Latin America and SMG contributed significant growth, and management raised no formal guidance but expressed confidence in continued momentum. Scrap margins normalized sequentially as expected, and the company completed full ownership of SMG.

Fluence Energy reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $650M, up 8% YoY but about $90M below prior expectations due to production startup delays at two new contract manufacturing facilities. Record order intake of $1.44B and record backlog of $6.4B (up 14% QoQ) were highlights, with first data center orders and awards totaling $850M. However, guidance was lowered: FY2026 revenue midpoint cut to $3.0B (from ~$3.4B) and adjusted EBITDA midpoint cut to -$10M (from +$50M), primarily due to ~$400M of revenue pushed into 2027 and $15M battery supply loss. Management expressed confidence in long-term demand but acknowledged execution risks during the ramp-up.

HP delivered strong Q3 FY2026 results with adjusted EBITDA of $236 million, beating guidance midpoint, and direct margins exceeding ranges across all segments, including North America Solutions at the high end with $241 million. Management raised Q4 and full-year guidance for North America Solutions and remains committed to $45 million+ quarterly direct margins in International Solutions, with strong growth in Argentina. Geothermal and international activities expanded, including three new rig agreements and a four-year offshore contract renewal, while the Middle East conflict still creates some disruption. The company highlighted ongoing tightness in super-spec supply and expects a multi-year upstream growth cycle leading into 2027.

Kulicke & Soffa delivered a strong fiscal Q3 2026 with revenue up 36.2% sequentially and 123% year-over-year, beating expectations. Gross margin was 47.8%, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.20. The company guides Q4 revenue to $375 million (up 13.5% sequentially) and non-GAAP EPS of $1.42. Management highlights broad-based recovery, record advanced solutions revenue, and expects strength to continue into fiscal 2027, with TCB revenue potential of $150-200 million next year.

Magnera reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $857 million with adjusted EBITDA of $99 million, a 9% increase and 70 basis point margin improvement year-over-year. The company reaffirmed free cash flow guidance of $90-$110 million but moved adjusted EBITDA to the lower end of prior guidance due to persistent inflation and macroeconomic uncertainty. Americas EBITDA rose 16% to $71 million, while Rest of World declined slightly. New product Universa launched and Project CORE synergies are at full run rate.

Fox reported record fiscal 2026 revenue of over $17 billion, up 5%, and record EBITDA of $3.9 billion, up 8%. Q4 revenue grew 28% to $4.2 billion and EBITDA grew 27% to $1.2 billion, driven by a 78% advertising revenue increase from the World Cup and strong Tubi growth. Adjusted EPS rose 41% in Q4 to $1.79. Management raised the dividend to $0.29 per share and expects continued momentum into fiscal 2027 with World Cup and midterm advertising tailwinds.

Mitek reported Q3 FY2026 total revenue of $54 million, up 18% year-over-year and above guidance, with Adjusted EBITDA margin around 38%. Fraud and identity revenue grew 14% to $29 million, while check verification revenue grew 24% on renewal timing. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $195-200 million, fraud and identity revenue to $105-109 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin to 32-34%. Key highlights include a top-five U.S. bank joining the Check Fraud Defender consortium, Fiserv live as a reseller, and a 73% year-over-year increase in CFD ACV to over $22 million, alongside an unexpected surge in age verification demand.

Maximus reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $1.28 billion, in line with expectations; adjusted EPS of $2.22 beat prior year's $2.16, with adjusted EBITDA margin up to 15.0% from 14.7%. However, a customer-directed pause on the VA MDE performance incentives reduces Q4 EPS by ~$0.35, cutting full-year EPS guidance midpoint from $8.40 to $8.05. Revenue guidance is reiterated at $5.2-5.35 billion with a bias to lower end. Cash collections accelerated with $245 million received since June 30, supporting free cash flow guidance of $425-475 million.

MACOM reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of $342.2 million, up 18.4% sequentially and 35.8% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $1.40. All end markets grew sequentially, led by data center (up ~40%) to $137.6 million, with I&D and telecom also up. Book-to-bill was a record 1.6:1, and gross margin expanded 120 bps to 59.7%. The company expects continued growth with data center and defense strength, launching CW laser production potentially in late calendar 2027.

Q3 FY2026 was a record quarter: net sales grew 4.1% to $395.9M, adjusted EBITDA rose 24.3% to a record $107.4M with margin expansion of 440 bps to 27.1%, and adjusted EPS increased 47.1% to $0.50, partly helped by a one-time tax benefit. Management raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $367M-$372M and narrowed net sales growth to 2.8%-3.5%, while lowering SG&A and tax rate guidance. WMS led growth with sales up 10.3% and EBITDA margin up 650 bps to 28.1%, and specialty valves are seeing traction in industrial water/data centers.

rows.company_name: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage Inc
rows.key_quote: Natural Grocers reported Q3 FY2026 net sales of $334.7 million, up 1.8% YoY, with daily comparable store sales growth of 1.2%, accelerating from 0.5% in Q2. Gross margin declined 60 basis points to 29.3% due to mix, shrink, and freight, and adjusted EBITDA fell 7.6% to $22.5 million. EPS was $0.48, down from $0.50, and guidance for FY2026 comp sales and EPS was narrowed/lowered. The company opened three stores in Q3, including its first in Wisconsin, and launched a DoorDash partnership.

RMR reported fiscal Q3 2026 distributable earnings of $0.48 per share and adjusted EBITDA of $19.7 million, both in line with guidance. Recurring service revenues rose sequentially to $45.5 million, boosted by higher enterprise values at managed REITs and the Greenwich JV acquisition fee. Management noted continued improvement at managed REITs, including DHC and ILPT, and highlighted opportunities in private capital and multifamily despite a global fundraising slowdown. Next quarter guidance implies adjusted EBITDA of $19-21 million and distributable earnings of $0.48-0.50 per share; full-year adjusted EBITDA is expected at $76.5-78.5 million, excluding incentive fees.

StoneX reported Q3 FY2026 net operating revenues of $719.7 million, up 47% YoY, and net income of $127.9 million, up 102% YoY, with diluted EPS of $1.00, up 85%. Strong growth was driven by Commercial and Institutional segments, with net operating revenues up 90% and 56% respectively, and record volumes in securities. RJO integration is on track, contributing $78.8 million in net operating revenues for the quarter, and Benchmark contributed $29.5 million, its best performance to date. Guidance was not explicitly provided, but management expressed confidence in the diversified business model and continued momentum.

Suburban Propane reported an adjusted net loss of $17.7 million ($0.27 per unit) for Q3 FY2026, wider than the prior year's loss of $10.8 million ($0.17). Adjusted EBITDA fell to $18 million from $27 million. Retail propane volumes declined 1.8% to 70.6 million gallons, mainly due to warm April weather, partially offset by customer base growth. The company highlighted RNG project progress, with new facilities expected to boost annual injection to 750,000-800,000 MMBtus for FY2027, and noted improving environmental credit prices.

In Q3 FY2026, UGI's reportable segment EBIT fell to $58M from $72M a year ago, driven by warmer weather and continued customer attrition at AmeriGas, partially offset by utility growth. Year-to-date, segment EBIT rose modestly to $1.187B, but adjusted diluted EPS declined from $3.55 to $3.17 due to lost investment tax credits and higher interest. Management reaffirmed FY2026 EPS guidance of $2.75-$2.90, despite a noted guidance cut for midstream growth investments. AmeriGas is expected to resume distributions to the parent in 2027.

CACI reported Q4 and FY2026 with record revenue, EBITDA margin, and free cash flow. Q4 revenue was $2.7B (+17.6% YoY, 11.6% organic), EBITDA margin 13% (up 150 bps), adjusted EPS $8.91 (+6.1%), and free cash flow $233M. Full-year revenue grew 10.9%, EBITDA margin 12.3%, free cash flow $735M (up 68% per share), and contract awards exceeded $10B. Fiscal 2027 guidance calls for revenue growth of 11.3%-13.4%, high-12% EBITDA margin, adjusted EPS of $32.96-$33.86, and free cash flow of at least $900M. Executives highlighted strength in electronic warfare, space, and counter-UAS, with the $500M Domestic Shield award and a classified counterspace win. Leverage reduced to 3.7x and expected to reach low-3s by June 2027.

Covista reported Q4 FY2026 revenue up 9.7% to $501.4 million and full-year revenue up 9.3% to $1.954 billion, exceeding the high end of raised guidance. Full-year adjusted EPS of $8.25 grew 23.7%, also above the high end. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps to 26.7% for the year. Management initiated FY2027 guidance and highlighted new partnerships, including Advocate Health, and expects continued momentum across segments.

Diageo reported a mixed fiscal 2026: organic net sales declined 2% (down ~0.5% ex-Chinese white spirits), but organic operating profit grew 2% and EPS pre-exceptionals rose 0.7% to $1.653. Free cash flow rose $463 million to $3.2 billion, net debt fell to $20.5 billion, and leverage improved to 3.1x from 3.4x. North America suffered an 8.4% organic sales decline with tequila down 21%, while Europe, LAC, and Africa grew. Management announced a $1.2 billion restructuring plan (over two years) with around $1 billion in savings, and will provide fiscal 2027 guidance at the Capital Markets Day.

Silvaco reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $17.8 million, up 48% year-over-year, with IP revenue surging 238% YoY and record IP bookings. The company achieved its first non-GAAP operating profit since late 2024, at $635,000, and executed $20 million in annualized spending reductions. Announced partnerships with NVIDIA and Dassault Systèmes, plus a $10 million convertible note investment from Micron. Guidance calls for Q3 revenue of $17 million ±10%, record Q4 revenue, full-year revenue above $70 million, and double-digit revenue growth in 2027.

Vistance Networks' Q2 FY2026 results showed net sales of $320 million, down 1% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $36 million, down 32%, and adjusted EPS of $0.12, down 8%. The Aurora segment saw revenue of $319 million (down 1%) and EBITDA of $46 million (down 43%), which was in line with expectations but impacted by memory chip issues and stranded costs. Full-year Aurora EBITDA guidance was lowered to $200-225 million, and the company announced a $5 per share special distribution from the RUCKUS sale proceeds of $1.846 billion. Management highlighted a strong DOCSIS 4.0 position and order strength with $200 million received in July, but cited customer upgrade delays and limited visibility on memory chip costs.

REGENXBIO reported Q2 2026 cash of $106 million, strengthened by a $100 million AbbVie milestone and a $108 million follow-on offering, pro forma cash over $310 million with runway into Q4 2027. Key milestones completed: enrollment in RGX-202 confirmatory study ahead of schedule, FDA alignment on accelerated approval for RGX-121 BLA resubmission, and first patient dosed in NAAVIGATE trial for diabetic retinopathy. BLA submission for RGX-202 initiated in Q3 2026, with top-line wet AMD data from ATMOSPHERE and ASCENT expected in Q4 2026. Management expressed confidence in upcoming data and financial position.

Qiagen reported Q2 2026 net sales of $535 million, flat at CER, beating guidance for a ~2% decline, and adjusted EPS of $0.62, above the outlook of at least $0.60. Growth pillars grew 5% CER, with Sample Technologies up 9% and QIAcuity double-digit, but PCR was down 8% and QIAstat-Dx fell 7% on respiratory comparison. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance of 1-2% CER growth and EPS of at least $2.43, expecting second-half growth to improve to 3-4% CER. Operating income margin contracted to 29.4% from 29.9%, and the dividend was raised 40% to $0.35.

RXO reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $40 million (above the high end of guidance), and adjusted EPS of $0.06. Brokerage volume grew 2% YoY, with truckload spot mix up 900 bps sequentially to 42% and truckload gross profit per load up 11% sequentially, the largest gain in four years. Last mile stops grew 3%, and managed transportation won ~$100 million in freight under management. Management guided to continued brokerage volume and gross profit per load growth in Q3, but expects weakening in last mile. Free cash flow was -$42 million due to working capital, expected to convert strongly in Q3.

Red Cat reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $20.2 million, up 520% year-over-year, with gross margin improving to 16.1% from 11.6% a year ago and 12.7% sequentially. Management highlighted continued scaling, new product introductions (Hellcat, Blue Ops Variant 7), and strong demand, expecting a 'dramatic' revenue ramp in Q3 and Q4. Cash stood at $325.6 million, and they reaffirmed a focus on profitability in 2027.

Rayonier reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.10 and adjusted EBITDA of $124 million, driven by PotlatchDeltic contributions and strong segment performance. Southern and Northwest Timber EBITDA rose significantly year-over-year, while Wood Products posted its best quarter since 2022. The company completed a tax-efficient land exchange with RMS, repurchased $72 million of shares, and affirmed full-year guidance with stable to higher lumber pricing trends.

Sabre's Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 4% to $712 million, with normalized adjusted EBITDA up 19% to $151 million, exceeding guidance. Full-year pro forma adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to approximately $600 million and free cash flow to -$65 million. Air distribution bookings grew 1%, ahead of expectations, with noted resilience in corporate volumes and ongoing impacts from Middle East conflict and fuel prices. The company reported strong growth in hotel revenue, payments gross spend, and NDC, while highlighting agentic AI progress with doubling of active partners to 60.

StandardAero's Q2 2026 showed revenue up 4.6% to $1.6B, adjusted EBITDA up 12.3% to $230M with record 14.4% margin, and adjusted EPS up 24% to $0.40. Both LEAP and CFM56 DFW programs reached profitability, and the company raised full-year guidance for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, and adjusted EPS. CRS segment margin declined 270bps on timing issues but is expected to recover in H2. A new $180M license expansion is expected to add ~$25M annual EBITDA over the next few years.

Progyny reported record Q2 2026 revenue, gross profit, and adjusted EBITDA, with revenue up 5.3% reported and 11% excluding a former client's transition agreement. Gross margin expanded 180 basis points year-over-year. Management highlighted strong watching season momentum with early commitments ahead of last year and retention de-risked for 2027, reiterating the target of adding 1 million or more lives. The company announced a new $200 million share repurchase program and continued to generate strong cash flow, with over $50 million in operating cash flow for the fourth time in five quarters.

In Q2 2026, RBI reported 3.8% same-store sales growth, 6.7% organic Adjusted Operating Income growth, and 12.9% Adjusted EPS growth, with Burger King US delivering an exceptional 8.6% same-store sales, beating the industry by over nine points. Tim Hortons was flat, Popeyes declined 5.2%, but International grew 5.5%, and Firehouse grew 0.4%. The company reiterated its 2026 algorithm and expects improving momentum, with Popeyes returning to positive comps in H2 and Burger King's elevation driving sustained outperformance, though beef costs remain a near-term headwind.

Park-Ohio reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $440 million, up 10% year-over-year, with record revenues in Supply Technologies and Engineered Products. Adjusted EPS rose 24% to $0.93, and operating income increased 22% year-over-year. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance for net sales to $1.7-1.73 billion and adjusted EPS to $3.10-3.30, citing strong demand across multiple end markets. Management also noted strong backlogs and continued operational improvements, while reviewing strategic alternatives for Southwest Steel Processing, which is expected to be a drag this year.

PENN reported record Q2 retail revenues of $1.5 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $517.2 million, up 4% and 6% year-over-year, respectively. Interactive segment revenue was $349.4 million with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $9.5 million, improving year-over-year. The company raised full-year retail revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $5.87 billion and $1.963 billion at the midpoint, while fine-tuning interactive revenue guidance down to $1.57 billion and reiterating an interactive adjusted EBITDA loss of $20 million. Management highlighted strong development project performance, balance sheet improvements, and a disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Planet Fitness reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $365 million, up 7% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA up 3.5%. System-wide same club sales increased 1.7%, entirely driven by rate, with Black Card penetration up 210 bps to ~68%. Membership reached 21.5 million, up 3.6% year-over-year but flat sequentially; attrition at 3.5%. The company reiterated its guidance with no negative comp quarters expected in Q3 or Q4, but noted the marketing initiatives will take time to gain traction.

PureCycle reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of approximately $4.5 million, up substantially year-over-year, with production of 4.5 million pounds of PureFive and about 5 million pounds of feedstock processed. The company completed a major turnaround ahead of schedule and below budget, set a new daily throughput record in June, and brought compounding in-house. Management reiterated the second-half Ironton breakeven target, citing accelerated customer qualifications following New Jersey's approval of PureFive as recycled content and commercial production of Procter & Gamble's Downy caps, with Tide caps and Vicks ZzzQuil lids scheduled for Q3 and Q4.

Star Bulk reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $1.21 and adjusted EBITDA of $184.2 million, with a daily cash margin of $17,944. The company declared a $0.09 per share dividend and continues to return 100% of operating cash flow. Management highlighted strong cash generation, low leverage (net debt at 50% of demolition value), and ongoing fleet rejuvenation with new Kamsarmax deliveries, while noting expectations for Simandou volumes to ramp from 15-20 million tons in 2026 to 120 million by 2029.

SandRidge reported record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue up 48% YoY to $51M, adjusted EBITDA up 49% to $34M, and net income of $27M ($0.72/share). Production grew 11% YoY (22% oil growth), driven by higher oil prices and the Cherokee drilling program. The company announced a bolt-on acquisition in the Cherokee Play, continues to pay dividends, and maintains a strong balance sheet with no debt. Guidance for 2026 remains intact with $76-97M capex and 10 wells planned.

Solaris reported record Q2 2026 with revenue of ~$219M, up 12% sequentially, and adjusted EBITDA of ~$108M, up 30% sequentially, with adjusted pro forma EPS of $0.39. The company raised Q3 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $90M-$105M and introduced Q4 guidance of $100M-$120M, reflecting GESA acquisition and new contract ramps. Management highlighted multiple contract expansions with three investment-grade tech customers, a new nuclear SMR investment, and strong demand with multiple gigawatts in active negotiations.

Senseonics reported Q2 2026 revenue of $14.5 million, up ~120% YoY, with U.S. revenue up >150% to $12.6 million. Gross margin was 59%, above guidance and the highest organic performance in company history, leading to raised full-year revenue guidance to $62-66 million and gross margin guidance to 58-61%. The Eon Care Network added 28 providers, surpassing 90 total and on track to exceed the 100-provider goal by year-end. European transition caused some revenue timing delays but full-year outlook unchanged.

Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 2% constant currency, with ex-China growth of 6%; adjusted EBITDA rose 21% to $129 million with margin up 310 bps to 20%. China revenue declined 23% and respiratory season is expected to be soft, leading to guidance cuts for FY2026 revenue ($2.52B-$2.60B), adjusted EBITDA ($540M-$560M), and adjusted EPS ($0.65-$0.90). Free cash flow guidance was withdrawn, and operating cash flow was negative $111 million for the quarter.

Republic Services reported Q2 FY2026 revenue growth of 4.6% and adjusted EBITDA growth of 4.5%, with adjusted EPS of $1.85. The company maintained adjusted EBITDA margin at 32.1% despite headwinds from prior-year landfill event volumes. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance across revenue, adjusted EBITDA, EPS, and free cash flow, citing higher fuel recovery fee revenue, increased recycling commodity prices, and acquisitions. Volume declined 1.6% on total revenue due to tough comps, but underlying pricing exceeded cost inflation and management expects sequential volume improvement.

Relmada reported Q2 2026 results with no revenue, a net loss of $12.9M ($0.11 per share) compared to $9.9M ($0.30) in the prior year, and cash of $217.7M expected to fund operations through 2029. Management reiterated plans to file NDV-01 IND by year-end 2026 and initiate the phase III rescue program, while noting manufacturing is the final critical step and sepranolone IND is also targeted for year-end. Guidance for first phase III data was pushed to likely first half of 2027, with management emphasizing the need for a meaningful patient count before disclosure.

D-Wave reported expanding commercial momentum with new and expanded customer engagements (AT&T, Optum, NTT) and a Nature-published validation of its dual-rail gate model architecture. The company reiterated its roadmap: 17 physical qubit system by end of 2025, 49 qubit in 2026, 181 qubit in 2028, 10 logical qubits by 2030, and 100 logical qubits by 2032. Management guided to roughly 2-3 annealing system sales per year at $20M-$40M each, with revenue recognized over two quarters per system.
