No specific financial figures for revenue, EPS, or margins were provided in the transcript excerpt.

AVITA Medical reported Q2 2026 revenue of $21.7 million, up 18% year-over-year and 13% sequentially, exceeding $20 million for the first time. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $86-89 million (20-24% growth) and introduced new guidance to achieve cash flow breakeven in Q4 2026. Gross margin improved to 81.9%, operating loss narrowed to $6.9 million, and net cash use improved to $3.2 million. RECELL U.S. volumes grew over 10% sequentially to 2,600 units, with strong RECELL GO mini adoption in smaller wounds, and CMS has proposed 2027 RVUs for new Category 1 CPT codes.

Occidental reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.40, with production of 1.43 million BOE/d, exceeding the midpoint of guidance by 23,000 BOE/d. Free cash flow was approximately $3 billion, the highest since Q3 2022, and midstream and marketing set a new record with adjusted earnings of about $960 million. The company reduced principal debt to $11.8 billion, raised the dividend by 8%, and reaffirmed a plan to add over $4 billion of annual sustainable cash flow by 2030, with approximately 85% achievable at lower prices. Guidance reflects expectations for normalized Waha/Gulf Coast spreads partially offset by upstream price improvements, while Middle East disruptions could impact sulfur sales and freight costs.

Ouster delivered record Q2 2026 revenue of $55 million, up 56% year-over-year, with over 17,000 sensors shipped, marking the 14th consecutive quarter of product revenue growth. GAAP gross margin was 49%, aided by a one-time refund of ~1,000 basis points, while Adjusted EBITDA improved to -$4 million. Q3 revenue guidance of $54.5-57.5 million implies a slight sequential decline as Rev8 ramps to production, and full-year guidance remains unchanged. The company raised substantial capital, ending the quarter with $263 million in cash and no debt, and subsequently raised ~$191 million net, which management says fully funds its operating plan.

OTF reported Q2 2026 adjusted NII of $0.30 per share, stable NAV of $16.48, and non-accruals at 10 basis points, among the lowest in the industry. Net leverage rose to 0.93x, near the low end of the target range, and the company completed $500 million unsecured bond, $150 million secured facility, and extended its revolver. Management expects to cover the base dividend by mid-next year and continues repurchasing shares, with $195 million still available. The investment environment has improved with wider spreads, and management remains confident in portfolio quality despite slower technology deal activity.

Redwire reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $117.1 million, up 89.6% year-over-year, with record gross margins of 27.8% and backlog of $542.1 million. The company raised substantial capital via ATM, reducing debt and interest expense significantly. Guidance implies continued growth in the second half. Key wins include a NATO Penguin contract, SpaceMD Starfall spacecraft purchase, and new facility expansions.

Radian reported Q2 2026 with total revenues of $575 million, up 93% year-over-year, driven by the Inigo acquisition, and net earned premiums up 116% to $504 million. Adjusted net operating EPS grew to $1.14, with adjusted net operating ROE of 13%. Mortgage segment new insurance written rose 14% to $16.3 billion, and persistency improved to 82%. Specialty net premiums earned increased 9% to $267 million, with plans for second-half earned premiums to be about 20% higher than first-half. Guidance for full-year share repurchases was raised to the upper end of the $200-250 million range, and expected Radian Guaranty dividends increased to $650 million or more. Market conditions in specialty insurance are more competitive, and a $30 million Middle East reserve was established.

Q2 FY2026 GMV hit an all-time high of $617 million, up 22% YoY (fourth consecutive quarter above 20%), with revenue up 17% to $193 million. Adjusted EBITDA reached $13.5 million (7% margin), expanding 290 bps YoY and beating prior guidance. Active buyers rose 11% to 1.1 million, and the company raised its full-year revenue and EBITDA outlook while guiding Q3 GMV to $610-620 million. Management highlighted Athena automation, AI pricing, and high-value item growth as key drivers.

The Real Brokerage reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $700.6 million, up 30% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $27.6 million, up 38% year-over-year. Despite a challenging housing market, closed transactions rose 27% to a record 62,380. The company reaffirmed its pending RE/MAX transaction, expecting to complete it in H2 2026 and targeting $30 million in cost synergies within three years. Guidance indicates Q3 sequential declines due to seasonality, with combined company guidance planned for the Q3 call.

PDF Solutions reported Q2 FY2026 revenues of $61.5 million, up 19% year-over-year, with first-half revenues up 22%. Backlog grew to $271 million, up 10% sequentially and 16% year-over-year, driven by multiple eight-figure contracts (secureWISE and DirectScan) and record Cimetrix bookings. Gross margin was 73%, down sequentially due to higher perpetual licenses in Q1, but management expects expansion toward the 77% target. The company reaffirmed 20% full-year revenue growth guidance, despite increased CapEx for eProbe tools.

In Q2 FY2026, Rocket Companies delivered adjusted revenue of $2.8 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $766 million (28% margin, up from 26% in Q1), and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.16, its most profitable quarter in four years despite a challenging spring market. The company achieved record market share in both purchase (6.2%) and refinance (14.3%), and is executing ahead of plan on the Redfin and Mr. Cooper integrations. Management emphasized a diversified revenue base, with over 70% of revenue recurring or less rate-sensitive, and expressed confidence in long-term earnings power.

Ring Energy reported Q2 2026 production of 19,990 BOE/d, up 3% sequentially, with realized oil prices up 38% to $95.45/barrel, but hedges limited upside. The company completed an equity offering, reducing debt to about $360 million and leverage to 1.7 times. Management raised second-half 2026 oil sales guidance midpoint by about 2% and lowered LOE midpoint guidance slightly, while increasing full-year 2026 capital spending to $158-$178 million. Initial 2027 guidance shows BOE volume growth of about 10% and a ~10% midpoint reduction in capital spending.

Riley Exploration Permian reported Q2 FY2026 with oil production near the high end of guidance, 5% sequential growth, and a June exit rate of 24.4 thousand barrels per day. The company raised full-year oil production guidance to ~30% year-over-year growth, with Q3 expected to be up >20% sequentially. Midstream constraints in April-May reduced oil production by ~2,000 barrels per day, but new Targa pipeline is expected in early Q4 2026. Full-year CapEx guidance was increased by 12% at the midpoint, and free cash flow declined to $6 million in Q2 due to higher capital spend.

Revenue surged 115% YoY to $451 million with record operating cash flow of $335 million, up 119%. Adjusted EPS rose 41% to $2.56. Guidance for gold and silver is tracking well; copper and other metals trending around or above top end. Management noted strong portfolio diversification and progress simplifying Sandstorm assets.

Palladyne AI reported record Q2 2026 revenue of approximately $5.8M, up 63% sequentially, with backlog increasing to $25M from $17M. The company reiterated full-year revenue guidance of $24M-$27M and expects cash burn to decline in the second half. Management highlighted successful field exercises, contract awards, and broad-based momentum across business units.

Rigetti reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $5.1M, up from $1.8M a year earlier, driven by on-premises Novera QPU sales. Gross margin improved to 43% from 31%, while GAAP net loss widened to $52.6M due to non-cash warrant and earn-out fair value adjustments; non-GAAP net loss was $16M or $0.05 per diluted share. The company highlighted technical progress, a $100M CHIPS Act letter of intent, and expanded HPE/Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center collaboration, with guidance expectations for the remainder of the year referenced but not fully quantified in the transcript excerpt.

Transocean beat its Q2 FY2026 guidance on revenue and cost, with revenue of $966 million at the upper end of the range and adjusted EBITDA margin of 32%. Fleet uptime hit 98%, and backlog grew by about $300 million excluding a pending $1 billion Equinor award. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance, expects to close the Valaris acquisition in Q4, and plans to call $200 million of 8% notes, reducing gross debt to below $4.8 billion.

BRC Group reported Q2 2026 net income of $18.5 million and operating adjusted EBITDA of $66 million, the best core operating quarter in nearly three years. Total revenues were $239 million, up $14 million year-over-year, driven by a $30 million increase in management fees from carried interest in SpaceX funds. The company reduced total debt by $497 million since December 2024 to $1.277 billion, with net debt down $87 million to $285 million. Management highlighted reactivated institutional accounts, a strong capital markets pipeline, and expects to comfortably cover $306 million in upcoming senior note maturities with cash and investments.

Pulse Biosciences reported Q2 FY2026 results, highlighting significant progress in its nPulse cardiac catheter pivotal study, which surpassed halfway enrollment ahead of schedule and is expected to complete in early October, three months earlier than originally planned. The company raised $57.5 million in net proceeds through an ATM program, ending the quarter with over $100 million cash on hand, and amended its study protocol to increase enrollment target to 164 patients. Vybrance disposable sales rose sequentially to $434,000 from $400,000. Management expressed confidence in the technology's differentiated efficacy and workflow advantages, and announced a partnership with the Clayman Thyroid Center.

PAR Technology reported Q2 FY2026 with ARR of $338 million, up over 17% year-over-year and 12.3% organic, and adjusted EBITDA of $14.3 million, beating the prior guidance range of $9.5-$11.5 million even excluding a $1.3 million one-off hardware project. The company highlighted nearly 100% multi-product attachment on new deals, six PAR Ordering wins, and PAR Intelligence reaching roughly 20,000 restaurant sites, with 17,000 retail sites. Management raised the full-year outlook, citing strong pipeline and deployment momentum, and remains confident in accelerating ARR growth in the second half.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was $731.1 million, up 5% YoY but down 1.8% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA was $206.1 million with a 28.2% margin, up from 16.8% in Q1. D2C revenue grew 63.1% YoY to reach 39.3% of revenue. Management maintained full-year guidance but expects to land near the lower end, citing deliberate front-loaded marketing spend reduction and softening consumer demand. Disney Solitaire revenue grew 15.5% sequentially despite lower marketing spend, but management expects sequential revenue declines in the second half due to spend timing.

Sunstone Hotel Investors reported Q2 RevPAR growth of 9.3% (4.3% excluding Andaz Miami Beach), with adjusted EBITDAre of $77 million, up 6% year-over-year, and adjusted FFO per share of $0.32, up 14%. The company raised full-year guidance, now expecting RevPAR growth of 7%-9% for the 13-hotel portfolio, and completed the sale of Hyatt Regency San Francisco, deploying proceeds into stock repurchases. Management remains cautious on macro headwinds but notes strong group and transient pace into 2027.

PubMatic reported a strong Q2, returning to double-digit revenue growth well ahead of schedule, with expectations for acceleration in the second half. The company highlighted leadership in agentic advertising with over 80 agentic campaigns, up from 30 a quarter ago, and new initiatives like Decision Fabric. CFO Steve Pantelick announced retirement but remains through Q1 2027 and in advisory role until July 2027. Guidance likely raised or reaffirmed with accelerating growth, though exact figures are not provided in the excerpt. The company sees political advertising as a tailwind in Q3 and Q4.

In Q2 FY2026, Power Solutions International reported net sales of $152.5 million, up 18.6% sequentially from Q1, exceeding expectations, but down 21% year-over-year due to softer oil and gas demand and shipment timing. Gross margin improved sequentially by 420 basis points to 27.1%, driven by operational improvements at Wisconsin, though year-over-year it declined from 28.2%. Operating cash flow was strong at $56.6 million, enabling $30.8 million debt reduction. Management expects H2 2026 sales to exceed H1, roughly in line with H2 2025, but provided no formal guidance due to order timing variability and continued oil and gas softness.

PRA Group reported Q2 2026 cash collections of $559 million, up 4% year-over-year, and total revenues up 29% to $372 million. Net income was $58 million. The company increased European ERC by $349 million due to over-performance, and highlighted continued cost discipline with 135 roles eliminated and $20 million annualized savings. Management raised no explicit guidance but signaled improved forecasting and record ERC of $8.9 billion.

Serve Robotics reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.2 million, up 9% sequentially and over 400% YoY, but below expectations due to a decline in Uber delivery volume. The company materially lowered full-year revenue guidance from $26 million to $9-$10 million, citing the removal of assumed second-half growth from Uber. Management says the Uber agreement may not be renewed in early 2027 and is reallocating resources to diversified channels, including DoorDash (up ~50% sequentially), advertising (~50% of robot delivery revenue), and hospital robotics. Gross margin was -271% with a gross loss of ~$8.8 million, but fleet gross margin improved sequentially.

Q2 revenue of $72.1 million fell 7.8% YoY and came in at the low end of guidance, with equipment sales down 18.4% and consumables down 3.5%. Adjusted EBITDA of $17 million beat guidance of $11-13 million, driven by gross margin expansion and cost discipline. Management lowered the full-year revenue outlook to $280-290 million while raising adjusted EBITDA guidance to $39-46 million. They introduced a new device rental program, received FDA clearance for SkinStylus periorbital wrinkles, and plan to repay the October 2026 convertible maturity with cash.

Papa John's Q2 2026 North America comps declined 8.3% while international comps grew 1.5%; total performance pressured by softer consumer and heavy QSR discounting. Management revised 2026 guidance to global system-wide sales decline of 2%-4% and adjusted EBITDA of $180-$190 million, including an incremental $18 million investment. Transformation is taking longer than expected; management announced leadership changes and expects 200-250 of planned closures to occur in 2026.

Permian Resources reported record Q2 free cash flow of $751 million, up nearly 50% quarter-over-quarter, and record FCF per share of $0.88. Oil production increased 3% sequentially to about 198,000 bbl/day, helped by a 50% increase in workover rigs and higher working interest (82% vs original 75% expectations). Full-year oil production guidance was raised to 199,000 bbl/day (10% above 2025), while CapEx midpoint is $1.95 billion, about 1% lower than last year. Management highlighted aggressive year-to-date acquisitions of about 55,000 net acres for ~$1.05 billion, with leverage at 0.5x.

Q2 2026 showed strong results with revenue up 35.8% to $298M and adjusted EBITDA up 48.2% to $24.3M, driven by acquisitions and operational excellence. Adjusted EPS rose 33.3% to $0.36. Management raised full-year guidance, citing momentum and better-than-expected acquisition transitions. Home health and hospice segments delivered strong same-store growth, while senior living showed stable improvements.

Privia Health reported strong Q2 results: practice collections grew 12.4% to $970 million, adjusted EBITDA increased 29% to $37.4 million with margin expanding 310 bps to 28.3% of care margin. Implemented providers grew 10.1% and attributed lives grew 19.2%. The company raised its 2026 guidance across most metrics, citing strong first-half performance. Management remains confident in long-term growth and margin expansion, despite minor CMS cash timing delays.

In Q2 FY2026, SIGA reported product-related revenues of $38 million, including $24 million of IV TPOXX delivered to the U.S. Strategic National Stockpile and $13 million of oral TPOXX to international customers. Net income was $12 million, with fully diluted EPS of $0.17. The U.S. contract process is slower than expected, but management remains confident in TPOXX's role, and they are targeting a new international contract with delivery by March 2027.

Praxis reported Q2 FY2026 with two NDAs in late-stage FDA review for ulixacaltamide and relutrigine. Mid-cycle meetings showed no advisory committee plans and no findings from BIMO inspections. Operating expenses rose to $96.9M and cash ended at $1.4B. The vormatrigine POWER1 study missed primary endpoints but met a key secondary endpoint, with plans to amend POWER2/POWER3.

Q2 FY2026 revenue was CAD 2.5 million, up 12% year-over-year, but was impacted by CAD 3.1 million of TULSA shipments delayed to July; excluding that, revenue would have been ~CAD 5.6 million, representing 153% growth. Gross margin rose to 78%, net loss narrowed to CAD 9.5 million, and cash stood at CAD 38.3 million. Management maintained full-year 2026 revenue guidance of ~CAD 25 million (56% growth), citing record order activity and a qualified pipeline of ~CAD 70 million. Reimbursement tailwinds include a proposed 14.9% Medicare payment increase for TULSA and expansion of covered lives by 18.3 million in Q2, with Johns Hopkins and Prime Healthcare employer plans newly covering TULSA.

SmartStop Self Storage reported Q2 FY2026 FFO per share of $0.49, up 17.6% year-over-year, with same-store NOI growth of 3.7% and 150 bps margin expansion. The company raised its full-year same-store revenue and NOI guidance and FFO guidance to $1.98-$2.04 per share, citing better-than-expected momentum. They also introduced the Deca Initiative, aiming for a $10 billion capitalization level, and increased capital deployment guidance to $55-$75 million. Management expressed confidence in the acquisition pipeline and recovery from L.A. fire restrictions.

SM Energy beat expectations in Q2 FY2026, generating $467 million adjusted free cash flow, $1.4 billion adjusted EBITDAX, and $2.19 adjusted EPS. The company raised its second half production outlook, lowered G&A guidance by $50 million, and reduced net debt by $1.1 billion, with 95% of merger synergies actioned. Management emphasized integration progress, buybacks, and a strong balance sheet, positioning 2027 for full earnings power.

Sempra reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.16, up from $0.89 in Q2 2025, with GAAP EPS of $1.21. The company affirmed its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $4.80-$5.30 and 2027 guidance of $5.10-$5.70, along with long-term EPS growth of 7%-9%. Management highlighted strong Texas demand, with 44 GW of Batch Zero load requests (140% increase over current peak), and Oncor's incremental capital opportunities totaling $10 billion. The pending sale of a 45% stake in SI Partners is expected to close later this quarter, deconsolidating ~$9 billion of debt, and the company expressed rising confidence in Oncor's capital plan roll-forward.

Primerica reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted operating revenues up 8% YoY and adjusted net operating income up 11%, with adjusted operating EPS up 17% to $6.41 including a $0.15 tax benefit. The ISP segment grew revenues 21% and pre-tax income 31%, with record AUM of $140 billion and $397 million in net inflows. Term Life premiums grew 3.4% but issued policies declined 12%, and the company guided full-year issued policies down mid-single digits. Management raised ISP sales guidance to 10%-15% growth for 2026, while maintaining full-year expense growth of 7%-8%.

In Q2 FY2026, SharonAI reported a major expansion in secured AI factory capacity to 212 MW from 132 MW prior, and contracted capacity grew to 120 MW with total contract value reaching approximately $8.8 billion year-to-date. Key wins include a six-year $4.9 billion NVIDIA partnership, a $1.32 billion take-or-pay with a global AI lab, and a $373 million agreement at a record price over $4 per GPU hour. The company raised about $2.2 billion in capital since December 2025, including a $1.6 billion oversubscribed round. Management expressed confidence in demand outpacing supply and guides for material revenue ramp from Q3 through 2027.

South Bow reported strong Q2 2026 results, with record throughput on the U.S. Gulf Coast segment and raised full-year normalized EBITDA guidance to CAD 1.04 billion (within a 2% range) and distributable cash flow guidance to CAD 665 million (within 2%). Leverage improved to 4.4x net debt to EBITDA, and the board approved a CAD 0.50 quarterly dividend. Management highlighted the successful open season securing 465,000 bpd of 20-year commitments, advancing Prairie Connector and Liberty Bridge projects toward a mid-2027 FID, and noted pressure restrictions on Keystone are expected to be lifted in phases through 2026 and 2027.

Perdoceo reported Q2 2026 net income of $48 million ($0.75 per diluted share), up from $41 million ($0.62) a year ago, with revenue rising 1.8% to $213.4 million. Adjusted operating income grew 4.4% to $64.2 million and adjusted EPS increased 19.4% to $0.80. Management raised full-year 2026 adjusted operating income guidance to $258-$263 million and adjusted EPS to $3.10-$3.16, while boosting the quarterly dividend by 13.3% to $0.17. Enrollments grew 0.7% overall, with CTU up 0.6% for an 11th consecutive quarter, AIU down 1% due to Trident, and St. Augustine up 6%.

Sprout Social reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $123.8 million, up 10.8% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating margin of 12.9%, up 370 basis points. CRPO and RPO accelerated, with CRPO growing 12.4% to $202.7 million. The company announced a 20% workforce reduction and expects to begin a $50 million share repurchase program. Guidance was not detailed in the provided excerpt, but management noted improved retention rates and positive early demand for Essentials, while expecting sub-$30,000 revenue to decelerate and go slightly negative this year.

Sezzle reported record Q2 2026 results with GMV up 37.9% YoY to $1.3 billion and revenue up 51.7% to $149.7 million. Net income reached $40.8 million (27.2% margin) and adjusted EBITDA was $58 million (38.8% margin), both ahead of prior trends. Active subscribers surged 76.4% YoY to 854,000, with record purchase frequency of 7.2x. Guidance was raised: revenue growth now targets 35% (upper end of prior 30-35% range), adjusted net income raised to $185 million, and EPS to $5.25, while new products SezzleCash and Sezzle Send are conservatively modeled.

Sotera Health reported strong Q2 2026 results with 8% constant currency revenue growth and 8.7% constant currency adjusted EBITDA growth, beating expectations. The company raised its full-year 2026 outlook for constant currency revenue growth to 5.25%-6.75% and adjusted EBITDA growth to 5.75%-7.25%, and improved adjusted EPS guidance to $0.95-$1.01. All segments grew, with Sterigenics up 7% cc, Nordion up 16.7% cc, and Nelson Labs up 5.4% cc, and the company reached its target leverage range of 3x. New CEO Alton Shader struck a confident tone, highlighting broad-based momentum and strategic focus on growth.

Scholar Rock's Q2 2026 results show a strong cash position of $492 million, including $63 million from ATM sales, with no revenue or EPS reported since apitegromab is pre-launch. The company has submitted its BLA with two fill-finish facilities, maintaining a September 30 PDUFA date, and has initiated the phase II FORGE trial for FSHD. Enrollment in OPAL is robust, and commercial readiness is advanced.

Somnigroup (formerly Tempur Sealy) reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $1.8 billion, adjusted EPS of $0.58 (up 9% YoY), and adjusted EBITDA of $297 million. North America margins expanded sharply (gross +680 bps, operating +400 bps) on synergies, but Mattress Firm margins fell on financing and investments. Full-year EPS guidance was $2.85-$3.15, implying mid-single-digit industry decline and low-single-digit like-for-like growth for most segments; management noted a weak July 4th period and ongoing ERP challenges at Dreams, but reaffirmed confidence and highlighted the Leggett & Platt deal on track to close in Q3.

Sweetgreen reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $192.7 million, up ~4% YoY, but comparable restaurant sales declined 6.2%, with adjusted EBITDA near breakeven at a loss of $0.2 million. Management noted sequential monthly improvement in transactions, with flat transaction comps in June, but flagged the impact of a Cyclospora outbreak and a jalapeno recall on outlook. Guidance for Q3 was lowered, reflecting recovery assumptions, and the company emphasized disciplined investment and menu innovation like wraps, which lifted transactions but created a check drag.

STWD reported Q2 2026 distributable earnings of $152 million or $0.40 per share, with no new non-accrual or 5-rated loans. The company deployed $2.5 billion in the quarter and another $1.7 billion in July, bringing year-to-date investments to $6.7 billion. Management expects to resolve approximately $800 million of non-accrual and REO assets by year-end, and anticipates the strongest origination quarter in Q3. Guidance was not explicitly provided, but management signaled continued recovery and growth.

LGI Homes reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $516 million, up 4% in homebuilding revenue, and delivered 1,440 homes, up 9% YoY. Homebuilding gross margin was 19.8% and adjusted gross margin 23.2%, both above the midpoint of raised guidance. The company raised full-year gross margin guidance for the second consecutive quarter and increased ASP guidance by $5,000, while reaffirming closing and community count guidance. Net orders decreased 4.8% and cancellations rose to 49.4%, but backlog increased 61% YoY and July closings are expected to grow 11.5%.

NGL reported record produced water volumes of 3.32 MMbpd, up 19.6% YoY, and record Water Solutions adjusted EBITDA of $179.9M, up 26% YoY, driving consolidated adjusted EBITDA to $186.2M vs $143.9M a year ago. Management raised FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance by $10M to $725M-$735M, citing strong execution and long-term customer commitments, and plans to redeem about 50% of Class D preferreds this year while potentially reinstating the common distribution in 2027. Growth capex will exceed $200M, with new capacity additions and the LEX II Extension project on track.

ePlus reported Q1 FY2027 net sales of $649.1 million, up 1% year-over-year, with product revenue up 0.6% and managed services up over 15% to exceed $50 million for the first time. However, professional services declined 5.1%, gross margin fell to 23.3% from 23.9%, and non-GAAP EPS decreased to $1.28 from $1.41. Open orders rose over $650 million year-over-year, and management maintained fiscal 2027 guidance while noting ongoing memory chip shortage and geopolitical headwinds.

IPG Photonics reported Q2 2026 revenue of $279 million, up 11% year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $0.58, both above expectations. Adjusted gross margin of 40.7% beat guidance, aided by a $4.7 million tariff refund and lower costs. Bookings improved with book-to-bill above one, led by strong welding and battery manufacturing demand. The company announced a binding offer to acquire Lumibird Medical and provided Q3 revenue guidance of $265-295 million with adjusted EPS of $0.30-0.60.

Lime reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $304 million, up 23.6% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $84 million (28% margin). Average operational fleet grew 22.1% to 408,000 vehicles, and MAU grew 22.1% to 5 million. RVD of $8.20 grew 1.2% reported but mid-single digits on a same-market basis. Management highlighted the early success of LimePrime, which launched globally in February and now represents a double-digit percentage of the user base, though it is weighing on near-term adjusted gross margin (52.1% vs. 55.7% last year) due to upfront investment. The company reaffirmed expectations for a record year with strong growth and profitability, and planned meaningful cash flow generation.

Transcat reported strong Q1 FY2027 results with consolidated revenue up 22% to $92.9 million, driven by double-digit growth in both segments. Service revenue grew 27% (13% organic), marking 69 consecutive quarters of YoY growth, with service gross margin expanding 90 basis points. Adjusted EBITDA increased 19% to $14 million, while adjusted diluted EPS was $0.51. Management reaffirmed expectations for high single-digit service organic growth and service gross margin expansion for the full year, and highlighted continued strategic M&A including the SCM acquisition.

Viasat reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $1.2 billion (down ~1% YoY), adjusted EBITDA of $381 million (down 7%, flat excluding discrete items), and net loss of $52 million (improved $5 million). Company-wide awards rose 10% to about $1.3 billion and backlog reached $4.2 billion (up 19%). Free cash flow was $72 million (up 19%), and net leverage improved to 3.2x. Company highlighted record DAT awards including PTSG, but called out continued challenges in maritime and legacy commercial services, offset by growth in aviation and government SATCOM. Guidance for FY2027 was not explicitly provided in the excerpt.

IQM reported Q2 FY2026 with strong commercial traction: cumulative 26 full-stack quantum computers sold, 17 delivered, and eight in production. The company completed a dual listing on Nasdaq and expanded into new markets with enterprise sales and a LUMI contract worth EUR 33 million. Full-year order intake guidance is EUR 65-75 million, with a cautious but confident outlook, and cash runway extended to Q2 2028. Cloud revenue remains small but is expected to grow as applications mature.

Intapp reported a strong Q4 FY2026 with cloud ARR growth of 29% year-over-year, marking 20 consecutive quarters of above-25% growth. Cloud net revenue retention held steady at 123%, total net new ARR surpassed $100 million for the year, and free cash flow reached a record 25% margin. Celeste, the Firm AI platform, moved to general availability in July 2026 and already contributed to record AI bookings, representing over 20% of net new bookings in Q4. Guidance was not explicitly provided in this transcript, but management expressed confidence in continued momentum into FY2027.

8x8 reported a strong Q1 FY2027 with record service revenue, fifth consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth, and exceeded guidance for service revenue, total revenue, non-GAAP operating margin, and operating cash flow. AI adoption surged 121% YoY, AI Studio gained over 200 customers and 2,900 agents within 3.5 months of launch, and the company raised its fiscal year revenue outlook. Management emphasized ongoing momentum, multi-product adoption, and a partner-first strategy while acknowledging near-term volatility.

TransDigm reported Q3 FY2026 results that exceeded expectations, with revenue up approximately 19% at the midpoint and EBITDA margin of 52.8%. Commercial aftermarket grew 18% in the transport component, defense grew 11%, and commercial OEM grew 17%. The company raised full-year guidance for sales by $150 million, EBITDA by $100 million, and adjusted EPS to $41.04. They also announced the $1.1 billion acquisition of Prince & Izant, while withdrawing from the Stellant Systems deal due to DOJ challenges.

Jackson Financial reported record Q2 2026 adjusted operating EPS of $7.30, with ex-notables EPS of $7.68, up 55% year-over-year. Retail annuity sales rose 34% to about $6 billion, with record RILA sales of $2.3 billion. First-half free cash flow reached $575 million (up 14% YoY) and capital returned to shareholders was $547 million. Management reaffirmed full-year free capital generation target of $1.2 billion and capital return target of $900 million to $1.1 billion, and announced CEO transition.

Knife River reported Q2 2026 revenue growth of 13% year-over-year, with aggregates volumes up 14%, ready-mix up 15%, and asphalt up 24%, but adjusted EBITDA was flat as-reported due to fuel costs, weather delays, and project timing. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $3.4-$3.6 billion and reaffirmed adjusted EBITDA guidance of $520-$560 million. They expect volumes up high single digits for aggregates and asphalt, mid-teens for ready-mix, and anticipate improved contracting services margins in H2.

Kimberly-Clark's Q2 2026 organic sales fell ~100 bps below internal expectations, hit by a China diaper disruption in late June, a North America trade inventory reduction, and softer category growth. Adjusted operating profit and EPS beat expectations, helped by a $45M U.S. tariff refund and 6.4% productivity. Full-year outlook was adjusted down due to discrete headwinds, but management expressed confidence in the underlying business, highlighted progress on the Kenvue integration and a new alternative natural fiber program.

Broadridge reported fiscal 2026 revenue up 8% constant currency, adjusted EPS up 12%, and record fourth-quarter closed sales of $158 million, with full-year closed sales of $305 million. The company returned over $1 billion to shareholders, including a 12% dividend increase and $600 million in buybacks, and guided fiscal 2027 to 6%-8% recurring revenue growth and 8%-12% adjusted EPS growth. Management highlighted strong position growth (16% total equity records, 12% equity revenue positions), progress in tokenization with the DLR platform reaching $360 billion in daily volume, and AI-driven productivity savings of $25 million expected in fiscal 2027.

Kimco reported Q2 FFO per share of $0.46, up 4.5% year-over-year, and same-property NOI growth of 3.5%. Small shop occupancy hit a record 92.9%, and overall pro-rata occupancy matched the all-time high at 96.4%. Management raised the full-year outlook midpoint and increased the quarterly dividend by 12%. The company also highlighted strong leasing spreads (40.4% on new leases) and a growing SNO pipeline with $75 million incremental ABR.

Kodak delivered a strong Q2 2026 with revenue of $311 million, up 18% YoY, and Operational EBITDA of $36 million, up 300% from $9 million. Gross profit rose 61% to $82 million, with gross margin expanding to 26% from 19%. The company achieved its fourth consecutive quarter of YoY growth in revenue, gross profit, and Operational EBITDA, and reduced total debt to EBITDA ratio from 23x to 1x. Management emphasized stability and growth, highlighting strength in both Advanced Materials & Chemicals (revenue up 40%) and Print (up 10%).

Stride reported FY2026 revenue of $2.518B (+4.7% YoY), adjusted operating income of $498.4M (+7%), adjusted EBITDA of $617.6M (+8.2%), and adjusted EPS of $8.33. Career Learning revenue grew 19% to $1.04B, while General Education revenue fell 2% to $1.42B. The company noted a CFO leadership transition, a non-renewal by Roscoe ISD, and guided to flat/up revenue per enrollment for FY2027, with formal guidance deferred to Q1 results. Management expects count-date enrollment growth to be modest due to tougher comparisons.

Paylocity reported Q4 FY2026 total revenue up 11% YoY and recurring revenue up 12.4%, beating the top end of guidance by $11.3 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $145.5 million (32.7% margin) exceeding guidance by $12.9 million. Full-year recurring revenue grew 12.2% to ~$1.8 billion, with 44,400 clients (up 7%) and ARPU up 5% to ~$37,200. The company launched Paylocity Ignite AI, Elevate Solutions, Paylocity Retirement, and acquired Aidora for automated leave management. Fiscal 2027 guidance assumes an accounting change benefit of 120-140 bps to adjusted EBITDA, but includes two 25 bps rate cuts and a difficult comparison due to tax legislation.

Kratos reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $458.8 million, above its estimated range of $400-410 million, with 19.1% organic growth, and adjusted EBITDA of $38.2 million above the high end of guidance. The company raised its full-year organic revenue growth guidance to 19%-23%, up from prior 15%-20%, and expects Q3 growth of 19%-25% and Q4 growth of 19%-31%. Management highlighted new awards including hypersonic programs (Kraken One, Two, Nemesis), a directed energy award (~$160M), and a space domain awareness award (~$100M), with a $15 billion bid pipeline. They noted continued margin expansion and significant investments for future growth.

Q2 2026 revenue grew 5% YoY to $981M, with Protein Solutions up 11% and Prepared Food & Beverage flat. Adjusted EBITDA was $168M, impacted by $20M of delayed revenue and discrete items, including $17M in IEEPA tariff refunds and $5M in accelerated LTIP expense. Management maintained full-year guidance despite PFB segment margin disappointment, citing strong backlog and operational improvements, with steeper Q4 ramp expected. Orders exceeded $1B for the third consecutive quarter, up 10% YoY.

Leidos reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.56B, up 7% total and 4% organically year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 13.8% and non-GAAP EPS of $3.26. The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $200M at the lower end, EPS by $0.10, and operating cash flow by $50M, citing strong bookings and defense growth. However, health segment faced VBA incentive payment suspension and MHS GENESIS transition, but management expressed confidence in offsetting these headwinds.

Sysco delivered Q4 FY2026 revenue over $22 billion (up 4.7%) and adjusted EPS of $1.53, beating prior guidance; full-year adjusted EPS was $4.61, above the guided range. USFS local case volumes grew 2.6% in Q4 with 130 bps sequential improvement on a two-year stack, and international posted 11th consecutive quarter of double-digit adjusted operating income growth (up 15.7%). Management guided fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS growth of 9%-11% and reiterated expected close of Restaurant Depot acquisition by Q3 FY2027, with $250 million cost synergies and day-one EPS accretion.

Digital Turbine reported Q1 FY2027 revenue of $166M, up 27% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $42.5M, up 69% YoY with 25.6% margin. On-device solutions grew 15% to $110M, App Growth Platform grew 56% to $56.6M. Company raised full-year guidance, citing AI-driven demand, brand growth, and international momentum.

InvenTrust reported Q2 FY2026 Same Property NOI growth of 4.1%, with year-to-date Nareit FFO up 11.1% and Core FFO up 9.1%. Leasing activity remained strong with 76 leases, 88% retention, and 8.5% blended lease spreads. The company acquired six properties for $290 million, expanding into emerging Sun Belt markets, and reaffirmed full-year Same Property NOI and Core FFO guidance while raising Nareit FFO guidance to $2.01-$2.07. Management remains confident in the portfolio and external growth pipeline.

CSWC reported Q1 FY2027 pre-tax NII of $0.57 per share, with total investment income up to $61 million from $57.8 million in the prior quarter. The company declared $0.64 per share in total dividends for September 2026, including a $0.06 supplemental, and raised $64 million via ATM at 141% of NAV. NAV per share declined slightly to $16.61, while the credit portfolio grew 24% YoY to $2 billion. Management remains confident in pipeline strength, with expected near-term originations of $250-$300 million, and highlighted progress at CapTrin JV with a new $150 million revolver.

Gartner's Q2 2026 revenue was $1.7 billion, up 3% as reported and 2% FX neutral, with EBITDA of $466 million up 6% and adjusted EPS of $4.37 up 24% year-over-year. Contract value grew 2% year-over-year, accelerating from Q1, and free cash flow rose 9% to $378 million. Management raised full-year EBITDA, adjusted EPS, and free cash flow guidance, and expects CV growth to continue accelerating. The company is optimistic about AI-driven demand and its Business and Technology Insights transformation.

Hamilton Lane reported Q1 FY2027 with revenue up 21% and fee-related revenue up 44% year-over-year, with fee-related earnings up 49%. Total fee-earning AUM grew 12% YoY to $83.7 billion, driven by a 25% increase in specialized funds. Evergreen net inflows were $640 million with positive flows in 10 of 12 products, though one non-U.S. multi-strategy equity fund saw elevated redemptions. Management expects five key strategies to be in market over the balance of fiscal 2027 and early 2028, and highlighted strong fundraising momentum including a $3.8 billion direct equity fund close.

Independence Realty Trust reported Q2 FY2026 core FFO per share of $0.28, ahead of internal expectations, with same-store NOI growth of 1.2% outpacing the original guidance midpoint. The company raised its full-year same-store NOI growth guidance midpoint by 70 basis points to 1.5%, but maintained core FFO per share guidance at $1.14 due to higher interest expense and lower non-same-store NOI. Management highlighted accelerating new lease spreads, a successful Wi-Fi initiative contributing $400,000 in Q2 revenue, and a commitment to value-add renovations as key drivers for 2027 momentum.

Lucid reported Q2 2026 results with CEO Silvio Napoli acknowledging past execution failures and a need for a fundamental reset. The company reduced its U.S. workforce by 20% and eliminated a production shift, generating $115 million in annualized savings, and identified $1.4 billion in cash flow improvements for 2026. Guidance was not explicitly provided, but the focus is on cost reduction, quality improvements, and key projects like the Uber-Nuro robotaxi. The tone is candid about challenges but committed to a turnaround.

OrthoPediatrics reported Q2 2026 revenue of $70.5 million, up 15% year-over-year, with record adjusted EBITDA of $6.8 million. Trauma & Deformity grew 26%, OPSB grew over 20%, and international grew 22%, while scoliosis revenue declined 9% due to zero 7D unit sales and lower Brazil set sales. Management raised full-year guidance to $265-$269 million (12%-14% growth) and affirmed confidence in achieving positive free cash flow in H2 and breakeven or better for the full year.

Tower Semiconductor reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $460M with record gross margin of 30%, operating margin of 20%, and net margin of 20%. Guidance for Q3 is $520M midpoint, implying a $2B+ annualized run rate. The company raised its 2028 model to $3.6B revenue, $1.63B gross profit (45% margin), and $1.2B net profit (33% margin). Silicon photonics revenue grew over 270% YoY with an annualized run rate of $680M and targets $1B in Q4 2026, supported by $1.3B in customer contracts for 2027.

Grab delivered a record Q2 2026 with adjusted EBITDA up 54% year-over-year to $168 million, margin expanding to 16.9% from 13.3%, and on-demand GMV up 21% year-over-year. Monthly transacting users reached a record 54 million, despite elevated fuel prices. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance, incorporating Superbank consolidation, Stash acquisition, and FX headwinds, while reiterating financial services profitability in the second half. Groceries (GrabMart) grew at 1.7 times the rate of food deliveries, and the company announced a $750 million share buyback, expanding cumulative authorizations to $1.75 billion.

Centerspace reported Q2 FY2026 Core FFO of $1.27 per share with same-store NOI up 30 basis points year-over-year. The company sold or contracted to watch 20 communities for ~$530 million over 14 months, reducing leverage and exiting tertiary markets. Due to the reconstituted same-store pool, full-year same-store NOI growth guidance was lowered to flat to down 1%, and Core FFO midpoint lowered to $4.63 per share. Management remains confident in the portfolio repositioning, expects Denver to recover in 2027, and anticipates a special distribution in Q4 to maintain REIT status.

Enlight Renewable Energy reported Q2 2026 revenue and income of $210 million, up 55% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $160 million, up 67%. Net profit reached $31 million. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $790-820 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $565-585 million. Key milestones include financial close on the $2.6 billion CO Bar Complex, a PPA with Google for 200 MW in Oklahoma, and safe harboring 17.9 FGW of capacity.

Ecopetrol reported strong Q2 2026 results with revenue up 35% YoY to COP 40.2 trillion, EBITDA up 59% to COP 17.7 trillion, and net income up 235% to COP 6.1 trillion, driven by higher Brent prices and record refining throughput. Management highlighted improved crude differentials, record refining margins, and continued investment progress, while noting production impacts from external disruptions and a higher FEPC receivable. The company expects to consolidate Brava Energia results in Q3 2026 and reaffirmed its dividend commitment.

DaVita's Q2 FY2026 adjusted operating income was $579 million, adjusted EPS $4.02, and free cash flow $256 million, with U.S. treatment growth of 56 basis points YoY, slightly above expectations. The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance, with adjusted operating income midpoint of $2.2 billion and adjusted EPS midpoint of $14.65. Management highlighted accelerating volume growth and progress on middle molecule clearance, but noted revenue per treatment declined sequentially and policy rate updates track below cost trends.

Duke Energy reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.43, up from $1.25 in the prior year, driven by electric utility growth and infrastructure investments. The company reaffirmed its 2026 EPS guidance of $6.55-$6.80 and its 5%-7% growth through 2030, expressing confidence in top-half results from 2028. Management highlighted a favorable North Carolina rate settlement, 7.8 GW of data center ESAs, and $5B-$10B of potential capital-plan upside.

Dorman reported record Q2 2026 sales of $545 million, up ~1% YoY, and record adjusted EPS of $3.08, up 50% YoY, with a $1.18 one-time refund benefit from IEEPA tariff costs. Excluding that benefit, comparable EPS was $1.90. Light Duty sales were flat YoY on tough comps, Heavy Duty grew ~7%, Specialty Vehicle declined 1%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to 3%-5% net sales growth and adjusted EPS of $8.50-$8.80, reflecting lower tariff environment and pricing actions. Heavy Duty margin improved 150 bps ex-refund, but freight market remains challenged.

DigitalOcean reported Q2 2026 revenue of $281 million, up 29% YoY, exceeding guidance on all key metrics. The company raised its full year 2026 revenue growth outlook to approximately 30% and reaffirmed at least 35% growth by Q4 2026, while expressing heightened confidence in 50%+ growth for 2027. Inference services grew nearly 800% YoY and now represent over 70% of AI customer ARR, with over 6,000 Inference Engine customers. Management highlighted strong profitability with 40% adjusted EBITDA margin and record incremental ARR of $93 million in the quarter.

3D Systems reported Q2 FY2026 with printer sales up over 45% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for new platforms like DMP 350, SLA 825, and NextDent 300. Healthcare remained the largest segment with solid growth, while industrial revenue was modestly lower due to older system replacements, but aerospace/defense and data center infrastructure both grew double digits. The company announced a leadership transition and signed a CRADA with Savannah River National Laboratory for nuclear materials. Guidance implies a small EBITDA loss in Q3, with management confident in reaching positive EBITDA through volume growth and material pull-through.

DuPont reported Q2 FY2026 organic sales growth of 4%, operating EBITDA margin up 80 basis points to 24.6%, adjusted EPS up 21% to $1.88, and free cash flow conversion of 127% for the quarter. The company raised full-year guidance again: organic growth to slightly ahead of 4%, operating EBITDA midpoint to $1.760B, and adjusted EPS midpoint to $7.24 (up $0.15). Management also announced a Q3 $250M share repurchase and expects full-year free cash flow conversion ahead of the 90% target. Strength was driven by healthcare, aerospace, industrial water, semiconductor, and electric vehicle battery applications, with continued momentum expected in the second half.

Danaos reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted net income of $133.1 million ($7.29 per share), up from $117 million ($6.36 per share) year-over-year, driven by a strong dry bulk segment where adjusted EBITDA jumped from $5.9M to $18.8M. Backlog increased by $683 million to a record $4.6 billion, with 100% container coverage for 2026, 93% for 2027, and 61% for 2029. Net debt was low at $224.5 million (0.3x EBITDA), cash stood at $1 billion, and fleet remains 78 of 87 vessels debt-free. Management expressed caution on new investments at elevated prices and expects FID for Alaska LNG around September.

Crexendo reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $24.6 million, up 49% year-over-year, beating top-line expectations, with GAAP net income of $1.1 million ($0.03 per share) in line with expectations and non-GAAP net income of $4.1 million ($0.12 per share), beating expectations by 200 basis points. Adjusted EBITDA of $4.1 million was up 46% year-over-year, and margins expanded across all segments, with consolidated gross margin up 500 basis points sequentially to 66%. The company added six new NetSapiens logos in the quarter (11 year-to-date vs. 2 last year), ESI acquisition contributed $6.9 million in revenue, and remaining performance obligation increased 97% to $139 million. Management maintained double-digit organic growth guidance for the year and expects AI-related revenue to become meaningful in 2027.

Centuri delivered record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $962M, up 33% YoY, with adjusted net income up 44% to $24.4M. Base revenue grew 36% and base gross profit grew 21%, though base gross margin contracted to 7.9% from 8.9% due to fuel costs and capacity investments. The company raised full-year guidance, expecting revenue of $3.59-$3.79B and adjusted EBITDA of $285-$310M, including the JJ White acquisition. Backlog is up 21% to $6.4B and the pipeline grew to $16B, with data center demand a key driver.

Custom Truck One Source reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $563M, up 10% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $117M, up 25% YoY. SER revenue grew 20% to $219M with utilization up 400 bps to 81.6%, and STEM third-party revenue hit a record $345M. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to $2.1B-$2.2B and adjusted EBITDA to $437.5M-$455M, citing a 'transmission demand super cycle' and strong order flow. Net leverage improved to 3.85x, and management expects meaningful free cash flow generation in 2026.

Crescent Energy reported record Q2 2026 results with production of 335 Mboe/d (2% above guidance midpoint), oil production 4% above midpoint, and record levered free cash flow of $418 million. Adjusted EBITDAX was $798 million. The company raised full-year production guidance and improved opex guidance, while maintaining capex. Permian synergies were increased to $250-$300 million, roughly three times the original target, and the company sees continued upside.

Energy Transfer reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $5.1 billion, up from $3.9 billion in the prior year, with record volumes across multiple segments. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18.8-$19.1 billion, an increase of about $500 million at the midpoint. Management highlighted strong performance across all segments, including record NGL and crude volumes, and noted continued momentum in natural gas demand for power generation and data centers. The Hugh Brinson Pipeline is in commercial service with full Phase I capacity expected by September 2026, and the company also announced a major ethane export expansion at Nederland.

Coupang reported Q2 2026 product commerce revenue growth of 8% in constant currency, improving sequentially from 5% in Q1, with consolidated revenue up 10% in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA came in within guidance, but product commerce gross margin contracted 210 bps YoY due to supply chain headwinds, promotional activity, and a $410 million regulatory fine. Membership recovered above pre-incident levels, and underlying customer spend (excluding non-returned cohort) grew 16% YoY, but management guided Q3 to 8-9% growth, citing calendar effects and the missing cohort. Management expects margin recovery for product commerce by mid-2027.

Compass reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.3 billion, up 14% year-over-year on a pro forma basis, and record adjusted EBITDA of $363 million, both above guidance. The company raised its year-one cost synergies target to $330 million from $300 million, achieved five months ahead of schedule, and increased 2026 in-year net synergies to $220 million. Brokerage GTV grew about 16% year-over-year versus market up 6%, an acceleration in outperformance from Q1, and net debt/EBITDA fell to 3.3x from 4.2x sequentially.

Cummins reported record Q2 sales of $9.5 billion, up 9% YoY, and record EBITDA of $1.7 billion (17.5% of sales), though EBITDA margin decreased from 18.4%. The company raised its full-year revenue growth guidance to 10%-13% (from 8%-11%) and increased EBITDA margin midpoint to 18%-18.5%. Strong demand in power generation, data centers, and China drove results, with global power generation revenue growth expected to remain 15%-25%, though capacity constraints persist.

Chatham Lodging Trust reported a strong Q2 2026, with RevPAR up 3%, pro forma GOP margins up 170 basis points, and hotel EBITDA margins up 220 basis points, beating internal expectations. The company increased its annual guidance by approximately 20% since the start of the year, citing strong business travel, robust performance from the recently acquired six-hotel portfolio (RevPAR up 9% in Q2 and 13% in July), and accelerating Silicon Valley demand (July RevPAR up 26%). Management remains optimistic about the lodging upcycle but exercises conservatism in second-half guidance due to Middle East conflict and limited visibility.

Cipher Digital reported strong Q2 2026 execution, highlighted by early delivery of data center capacity at Black Pearl two months ahead of schedule, with rent commenced. The company priced an $810 million bond offering at 6% coupon for Stingray, and added a new 900 MW site (Apollo) plus a 200 MW expansion at Stingray, expanding the portfolio to ~5.3 GW across 11 sites. Management expressed confidence in ERCOT Batch Zero inclusion for several sites and noted strong HPC tenant interest in Odessa. Pipeline additions and construction progress underpin a positive outlook.

Certara's Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 1% YoY to $93.3M, with software revenue up 4% and services revenue down 3%. Adjusted EBITDA was $26.2M (28.1% margin), slightly down from $27M. The company reaffirmed guidance of 0-4% revenue growth for the full year, citing positive pipeline growth of 25-27% and momentum in software bookings, offset by services weakness and restructuring costs. Management highlighted a new Chief Commercial Officer, AI-driven productivity gains, and continued regulatory tailwinds.

CCEP delivered strong Q2 FY2026 results with revenue of EUR 10.7 billion, up 6.1%, volumes up 5.6% (2.2% day-adjusted), and operating profit of EUR 1.5 billion, up 8.1%. Diluted EPS rose 10.6% to EUR 2.20, and free cash flow was EUR 435 million. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance, citing broad-based growth, share gains, and strong execution. They highlighted record World Cup activation, double-digit growth in energy and sports/hydration, and zero-sugar volume up 10%.

Central Bancompany reported Q2 FY2026 net income of $113.8 million, or $0.47 per share, with adjusted net income up 16% year-over-year. Net interest margin expanded 13 basis points to 4.43%, and asset quality remained consistent with net charge-offs at 10 basis points. Management noted broad-based loan growth (6.5% annualized ex-consumer), robust pipelines, and a refreshed $100 million buyback authorization, while seeing value in the stock despite trading at a discount to peers. They expect deposit costs to be stable and loan yields to grind higher with back-book repricing, but highlighted intense price competition and a shift to lower-yielding mortgage loans.

Caterpillar reported record Q2 FY2026 sales and revenues of $20.5 billion, up 24% year-over-year, and adjusted EPS of $8.17, up 73%. All three primary segments grew sales to users, with backlog up $9 billion sequentially to $72 billion. The company raised its full-year sales and revenue growth outlook to mid-to-high teens and expects higher adjusted operating profit margin than previously guided, excluding IEEPA tariff recoveries. Management remains confident in strong demand across power generation, data centers, and mining, while noting tariff and geopolitical uncertainties.

Callaway Golf reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $612 million, up 2% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA of $125 million, up 36% YoY, both exceeding guidance. Gross margin expanded 460 basis points to 48.5%, driven by margin initiatives and tariff benefits. The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $15 million and EBITDA guidance by $31 million at the midpoint, reflecting strong Q2 performance and improved tariff outlook. Management highlighted continued market share gains in golf balls and clubs, while noting strategic actions that will negatively impact second-half results.

Credit Acceptance reported Q2 2026 GAAP EPS of $12.66, up 71% YoY, and adjusted EPS of $12.12, up 21%, driven by lower credit loss provisions and higher yields on newer loans. Unit volume declined 1% YoY, an improvement from Q1's 4.3% decline, with monthly volumes returning to growth in June and July. Forecasted net cash flows declined 0.3% during the quarter, a smaller decline than the prior year, though the 2025 vintage underperformed modestly. Management highlighted ongoing data-driven transformation and disciplined capital allocation, expressing confidence in continued progress.

BuzzFeed reported Q2 2026 revenue of $36.3 million, down 21.8% year-over-year, with advertising revenue down $5.3 million, content down $0.7 million, and commerce/other down $4.1 million. Adjusted EBITDA swung to negative $1.7 million from positive $2 million a year ago, and net loss widened to $11.8 million from $10.6 million. Management cut headcount by ~35% for ~$30 million in annualized savings, paid down term loan to $25 million, and emphasized full-year operational targets instead of quarterly guidance.

Entegris reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $883 million, up 11% year-over-year and above guidance, with adjusted EPS of $0.93, up 42%. Gross margin was 47.6%, its highest since early 2022, and free cash flow was $120 million. The company raised its 2026 MSI growth outlook to 7-8% from mid-single digits, guided Q3 revenue to $905-935 million (up ~14% YoY), and expects to end the year with net leverage below 3x. It also announced the exit of its Life Sciences Fluid Management business and further facility rationalization.

EVERTEC reported Q2 2026 revenue of $275 million, up 20% year-over-year (16% on a constant currency basis), with adjusted EBITDA of $109 million (up 18%) and adjusted EPS of $1.05 (up 18%). The quarter included significant strategic wins, including a multi-year agreement with Transbank in Chile and a contract with Clip in Mexico, and the acquisitions of Dimensa and BBChain closed in the quarter. Management confirmed existing guidance and noted synergies from acquisitions are expected to be more meaningful in 2027.

Innovex delivered Q2 2026 revenue of $245 million and adjusted EBITDA of $48 million, both at the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 20%. International/offshore revenue rose 11% sequentially, while NAM land fell 4% sequentially due to Canada seasonality. The company closed the TCO Group acquisition for $95 million and guided Q3 revenue to $260-270 million and adjusted EBITDA to $51-57 million, implying sequential growth. Management cited strong subsea momentum, Mexico activity, Saudi market share gains, and expects U.S. land growth in the back half.

Q2 2026 revenue before reimbursements was $68.3 million, slightly below guidance, and adjusted EPS of $0.34 was at the midpoint. Management highlighted an inflection point with over $30 million in significant new platform-led deals closed, expected to drive Q3 EPS of $0.37-$0.39 and a strong Q4 and 2027. Gross margin improved to 44.1% from 42.3% sequentially, and cash flow from operations was $15.2 million.

Ingredion's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 1% to $1.85 billion, in line with expectations, but adjusted operating income fell 5% to $258 million and adjusted EPS declined $0.05 due to Argo production issues and Mexico macro pressures. Texture & Healthful Solutions delivered 7% volume growth (ninth consecutive quarter) and its second-highest quarterly operating income, but tapioca costs rose over 40% year-to-date. U.S./CAN sales fell 7% and operating income was $58 million; management expects sequential improvement in the back half from Argo recovery. The pending Tate & Lyle acquisition received shareholder approval, with expected EPS accretion above 15% in the first full year.

IIPR reported Q2 2026 revenue of $63.3 million, down from $69 million in Q1, with AFFO per share of $1.83 versus $1.88, due to reduced payments from default tenants. The company fully funded its $270 million IQHQ commitment, completed an upsized $402.5 million exchangeable notes offering at 6%, and repaid its $291 million senior debt maturity, ending with $300 million liquidity and net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 1.7x. Leasing activity included 389,000 sq ft of new leases in H1, plus 488,000 sq ft of agreements on former 4Front assets, while Parallel defaulted on two Florida properties totaling 593,000 sq ft. Management expressed confidence in life sciences diversification and federal cannabis reform progress.

IDEXX reported Q2 2026 revenue up 10% as reported and 9% organically, with CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue growing 10.3% organically, led by double-digit volume growth in both U.S. and international. EPS was $4.27, up 15% on a comparable basis, with comparable operating margin up 110 basis points. Management raised full-year revenue and EPS guidance, citing strong performance and momentum, while noting headwinds from FX and planned incremental investments in the second half.

Hut 8 reported Q2 FY2026 results, emphasizing its energy infrastructure platform and progress on AI data center campuses. The company announced a second Beacon Point lease for 352 MW, bringing total contracted AI data center capacity to about 949 MW with roughly $26.6 billion of expected base term contract value. Construction milestones at River Bend are on track, and the company highlighted two investment-grade construction financings, with Beacon Point on better terms. Management remains confident in delivery and cost efficiency, noting building costs are declining per building.

HealthStream reported record Q2 FY2026 revenues of $83.7 million, up 12.5% YoY, and record adjusted EBITDA of $20.6 million, up 16.9%. Organic growth was 8.3%, with notable strength in CredentialStream (+14%), ShiftWizard (+30%), and myClinicalExchange (+29%). The company raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance but trimmed net income guidance due to planned incremental investments in career networks. A $2 million one-time revenue catch-up from an ANSOS contract contributed to results and is not recurring.

Henry Schein reported strong Q2 2026 with accelerated internal local currency sales growth and margin expansion, driving double-digit earnings growth. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance, though EPS guidance was only modestly increased due to excluding further remeasurement gains. Management highlighted broad-based strength, with high-growth businesses now nearly 50% of operating income and continued momentum expected.

HSBC reported H1 2026 revenue of $38.2 billion, up 6% YoY, and PBT of $20.4 billion, up 6%, with an annualized RoTE of 19.1%, above the 17% target. Banking NII guidance was raised to at least $46 billion for the full year. CET1 ratio was 14.1%, and the company announced a $1 billion share buyback, resuming after a pause. Cost of risk was 47bps for H1, with Q2 HK CRE charges of $0.2 billion; full-year guidance of 45bps was reiterated.

Harmony Biosciences reported record Q2 2026 WAKIX net revenue of $261.3 million, up 30% year-over-year and 21% sequentially, and reiterated full-year guidance of $1.0-$1.04 billion, on track to exceed $1 billion. The company disclosed encouraging phase I SAD data for BP-205, an orexin-2 agonist, showing a 25-hour half-life, once-daily dosing potential, and no serious adverse events, with MAD data expected in Q4 and phase II trials planned for mid-2027. Management emphasized strong balance sheet with ~$963 million cash and IP protection for WAKIX to 2030.

Rockwell Automation reported Q3 FY2026 sales up 8% reported and 10% organic, with adjusted EPS of $3.49, up over 20% year-over-year, both exceeding expectations. The company raised full-year guidance to 7.5%-9.5% organic sales growth and adjusted EPS to $13-$13.30, up $0.35 at the midpoint. Segment growth was led by Software & Control up 18% and Intelligent Devices up 10%, while Lifecycle Services declined 2%. Management expressed confidence in broad-based demand strength but noted continued weakness in large capital projects and food & beverage CapEx.

Horizon Quantum reported Q2 2026 net loss of $115.2 million, driven mainly by a $108.3 million non-cash warrant derivative remeasurement charge. Operating expenses rose to $7.2 million from $2.8 million a year ago, reflecting increased R&D and public company costs. Cash reached $113.3 million, boosted by $27.5 million in warrant exercise proceeds. Key progress includes Beryllium early access, Ember-1 testbed opening to users, and a new internal applications team, while management notes a large non-cash loss that does not affect runway.

Q2 FY2026 revenue of $213M grew 53% YoY, beating guidance of $200-202M; operating income of $62M doubled YoY with 29% margin (up from 19%), and free cash flow reached $100M (47% margin). LTM billings hit $862M, up 52%. The company raised guidance on yield-driven strength and announced a definitive agreement to acquire Cylinder Health for $105M cash to enter GI, plus a $300M share buyback. Management cited strong pipeline, SMB growth, and rapid adoption of the new Migraine program.

HLMN reported Q2 FY2026 net sales up 10% to $442M, in line with long-term growth targets, with adjusted EBITDA up 2.5% to $77.1M. The company announced the acquisition of Kanebridge Corporation for $315M, which is expected to add $15M in sales and $5M in adjusted EBITDA in 2026, and raised the midpoint of full-year net sales guidance to $1.695B (9% growth) and adjusted EBITDA to $285M. RDS segment showed strong growth with adjusted EBITDA up 10.4% and margins healthy. New business wins contributed 4.5 points of growth, including about 1 point from the Win the Pro focus, and the company remains confident in its long-term 8-12% growth target.

Grainger delivered strong Q2 FY2026 results with total sales up 10.3% reported and 13.7% on a daily organic constant currency basis, driven by broad-based demand acceleration. Operating margin expanded 120 bps to 16.1%, and EPS rose over 20% to $12.01, aided by IEEPA tariff refunds. The company raised its full-year guidance, now expecting daily organic constant currency sales growth of 11.5%-13% and EPS of $45.50-$47.25, with preliminary July sales up over 13%.

In Q2 2026, Diamondback Energy increased production by ~4% from year-start, responding to price signals with a 3-4% hike in March. Management cited low global inventories and expects continued low single-digit organic growth in 2027 while maintaining capital efficiency. They reduced net debt by $1.6 billion, translating to $5.60 per share of value, and allocated modestly to buybacks. Gas outperformance and EOR results were highlighted, with initial EOR wells showing 100-150 bbl/d uplift on average, though dispersion is wide.

The call did not provide specific reported financials for Q2 FY2026; instead, management discussed strategic plans. They mentioned a $1.2 billion MSA contract with a neocloud provider, targeting first 10 MW of critical load online by end of 2026 and next 10 MW in Q1 2027. Management presented a projection of $300 million-$350 million enterprise value next year and anticipates reporting EBITDA starting in 2027. They acknowledged ongoing dilution concerns and the need to raise capital, while planning to reduce corporate overhead.

In Q2 2026, Gulfport highlighted strong momentum heading into the second half, with production accelerating and liquids volumes expected to be over 50% higher than H1. Management announced a $140 million discretionary land budget for 2026 and disclosed a recent $83 million state land auction purchase, boosting net Appalachia location count by ~20%. New CEO Nick Dell'Osso emphasized operational efficiency, inventory quality (about 15 years of drilling inventory with best-in-class breakevens), and disciplined capital allocation including buybacks. The company remains optimistic about in-basin gas demand from AI data centers and is exploring value in the Scoop asset. No specific financial figures were provided in the text.

Graphic Packaging reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $2.2 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $247 million at the top of guidance, adjusted EPS of $0.14, and adjusted cash flow of $138 million, up $55 million year-over-year. Margins expanded sequentially to 11.3%, with volumes steady despite higher gas prices. The company raised its 2026 inflation estimate to $150 million, achieved $85 million in cost savings, and reduced capital expenditure guidance to below $450 million, but lowered adjusted cash flow guidance to $600-$700 million due to inflation and inventory timing. Management announced price increases and progress on footprint optimization, but noted softness in household and foodservice segments.

Gilead reported strong Q2 2026 results with base business sales up 10% YoY, driven by HIV, Trodelvy, and Livdelzi. HIV sales grew 12% YoY, with PrEP sales doubling to exceed $1 billion quarterly for the first time. The company raised full-year HIV growth guidance to 9%-10% from 8%, citing strong Biktarvy and PrEP momentum. Trodelvy sales were up 26% YoY on new first-line approvals, while cell therapy declined 14% YoY amid competition. Management highlighted upcoming launches for BIC/LEN and anito-cel before year-end.

Global Industrial reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $386.6 million, with average daily sales up 9.3% YoY (third consecutive quarter of high single-digit ADS growth). Non-GAAP gross margin was 34.7% (more in line with historical performance, down from a record 37.1% that included FIFO tariff timing benefits), and non-GAAP operating margin was 7.3%. The quarter included a one-time $26 million benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds (excluded from non-GAAP). Management noted continued momentum into Q3, with GPO annualized sales on pace to hit $100 million and e-procurement connections now greater than 1,300. Guidance was not explicitly provided, but management indicated gross margins should remain around 34.7%-34.8% for the balance of the year, and reiterated CapEx of $3-$4 million.

First Watch reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue growth of 15.2% to $354.7 million, with same-restaurant sales up 3.4% and traffic nearly flat at -0.4% but improving sequentially. Restaurant-level operating profit margin improved 20 basis points to 18.8%, helped by commodity deflation and labor productivity, though beef costs pressured margin by ~100 basis points due to strong LTO demand. Management maintained FY2026 guidance and updated long-term targets to 50 annual openings and positive free cash flow by FY2027, while emphasizing marketing effectiveness and robust development pipeline.

Freshworks reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $237.4M, up 16% YoY, above the high end of guidance. Non-GAAP operating margin was 24%, and the company achieved positive GAAP net income of $3.2M ahead of schedule. EX ARR grew 24% constant currency to $567M, while CX ARR grew 4% to $400M. The company raised full-year guidance, citing a $4M beat inclusive of a $2M FX headwind, and reaffirmed confidence in mid-20s EX ARR growth.

Finance of America reported Q2 2026 adjusted net income of $19 million ($0.84 per share), up 53% year-over-year, despite a GAAP net loss of $29 million driven by non-cash fair value adjustments. Funded reverse mortgages totaled $730 million, up 21% year-over-year, and submissions exceeded $1 billion, up 19% year-over-year. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance of $2.8-3.1 billion in funded volume and $4.50-$5.00 adjusted EPS, and highlighted strong cash generation of $58 million in the quarter, used to fund the Onity MSR acquisition and debt payments. Management expressed confidence in achieving guidance and continued investment in growth.

FMS reported Q2 FY2026 with solid 5% organic revenue growth and 23% operating income growth at constant currency, plus 180 bps margin expansion. However, U.S. same-market treatment growth declined 0.9%, and management lowered expectations for 2026 U.S. same-market treatment growth to around Q2 levels due to referral execution gaps. The company confirmed full-year guidance, completed a EUR 1 billion buyback and launched a second, while absorbing external cost headwinds and regulatory pressures in China.

Flywire reported strong second quarter FY2026 results with robust revenue and EBITDA growth, signing over 200 new clients across 45 countries for the second consecutive quarter. Management emphasized strategic vendor consolidation, geographic diversification, and software-led monetization as structural growth drivers, with education revenue outside the big four growing over 30% year-over-year. The company reiterated long-term targets of $1 billion annual organic revenue and 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, while acknowledging a challenging macro environment with negative U.K. visa trends and stricter regulations. AI-driven automation is already resolving ~45% of customer inquiries automatically, with a target of over 50% by year-end.

FIS reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $3.4 billion, up 5.3% pro forma, with banking growing 6.1% at the high end of guidance and capital markets growing 3.2% at the low end. Adjusted EBITDA grew 7.4% with 113bps margin expansion, adjusted EPS up 8.8%, and free cash flow more than tripled to $525 million, leading to a $100 million raise in full-year free cash flow guidance. However, capital markets underperformed due to client attrition from UBS/Credit Suisse and weaker lending volumes, prompting a rebased full-year outlook and a review of strategic alternatives for some capital markets products.

Fortune Brands Innovations reported Q2 2026 sales of $1.2 billion, down 4%, with operating income up 18.4% to $236 million and EPS of $1.35, both benefiting from $81 million net tariff refunds ($0.52 EPS). Excluding tariff refunds, results were in line with expectations; Water sales fell 6.5% due to service challenges and supply chain issues, while Outdoors and Security showed some growth. Management lowered full-year 2026 guidance to fund incremental investments of about $0.20 EPS for service and new product development, and reaffirmed a $70 million cost program with $15 million savings in 2026. The tone was realistic and candid, acknowledging execution gaps and emphasizing a return to customer focus.

LeMaitre Vascular reported Q2 2026 sales growth of 10% organically (7% price, 3% units), excluding catheters 12% organic growth. EPS grew 23% to $0.74, with a record operating income of $20.4 million and a 29% operating margin. Guidance was lowered: full-year organic revenue growth reduced from 12% to 11%, and reported revenue guidance cut to $276.3 million, reflecting FX headwinds, export delays, and RFA supply constraints. Artegraft remains a standout, growing 34%, with 2026 sales expected at $11 million.

BellRing Brands reported Q3 net sales growth of 4%, with Premier Protein RTD shake volume up 3% and Dymatize sales up 27%, both beating expectations. However, adjusted gross margin fell to 27.7% from 35.1% due to protein and freight cost inflation, tariffs, and a $28 million inventory-related charge. Management raised full-year net sales guidance to 1-3% growth but lowered adjusted EBITDA guidance to $275-$295 million, and announced a double-digit price increase on Premier Shakes for fiscal Q1 2027, expecting elasticities slightly greater than one. A new CEO, Mike Axelrod, joined and acknowledged execution issues while outlining actions to improve profitability in fiscal 2027.

Powell Industries reported record quarterly orders of $934 million in Q3 FY2026, nearly three times higher year-over-year, lifting backlog to a record $2.4 billion. Revenue grew 9% to $312 million, with gross margin steady at 30.6% and EPS rising to $1.42 from $1.32. The company is aggressively expanding capacity, planning a new facility and expects strong performance into FY2027.

Red Rock Resorts reported Q2 FY2026 Las Vegas operations net revenue of $503.2 million, down 2% year-over-year, and Adjusted EBITDA of $227.5 million, down 5%, with margin of 45.2% (down 143 bps). Consolidated revenue including North Fork was $510.3 million, down 3%; consolidated Adjusted EBITDA was $208 million, down 9.3%. Management noted stable slot trends, with April stronger than May and June, and reiterated full-year capital spend guidance of $375-425 million. Durango North expansion remains on schedule for second half 2027 opening, and North Fork is expected to open early Q4 2026.

Smith & Nephew reported Q2 FY2026 underlying revenue growth of 1.6%, below expectations, with weak U.S. Orthopedics and Advanced Wound Bioactives offsetting strong Sports Medicine & ENT (+8.6%) and Emerging Markets (+10.6%). Revenue guidance for 2026 was lowered to around 4% underlying growth from prior expectations. Trading profit was strong at $566 million, up 9% ex-M&A, supported by efficiency savings and tariff refunds, and 2026 profit guidance was maintained with a $200 million efficiency savings target. Skin substitute headwinds are tracking towards the upper end of the $20-$40 million range, with SANTYL expected to return to growth in H2.

Q2 FY2026 combined net revenue for Revuforj and Niktimvo was $115M, with Revuforj at $55M (up 91% YoY, 12% QoQ) and Niktimvo at $60M (up 67% YoY, 9% QoQ). Revuforj saw a Q2 fluctuation in new patient starts, but management expects a return to growth; Niktimvo continued steady new patient starts and an increasing average treatment duration. Management highlighted upcoming Phase II data in IPF and frontline chronic GVHD in Q4, plus new pipeline assets, and expressed continued confidence in long-term growth.

USA Compression reported Q2 2026 revenues of $342.1M, up 37% YoY, driven by the J-W acquisition and higher revenue per horsepower.
