Adjusted gross margin was 63.5%, and leverage stood at 3.72x, just below the 3.75x target. Management reiterated full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $770-800M and DCF of $480-510M, while announcing plans for ~2.5% annual horsepower growth through 2029 and early contracting for 2027/2028 deliveries. They also noted a $1M/month incremental lube oil cost in H2, with no direct pass-through, but CPI escalators in contracts.

SMP reported strong Q2 FY2026 with adjusted sales up 6.7%, record adjusted EBITDA of $63.5 million (12.1% of sales), and non-GAAP EPS up 8.6% to $1.40. Vehicle Control sales fell 1.6% due to wire set decline, but Temperature Control surged 15.7%, Engineered Solutions up 16.8%, and Nissens up 4.8%. Full-year guidance is unchanged: low-to-mid single-digit sales growth and 11%-12% EBITDA margin. Management remains bullish, citing strong performance despite tariff and Middle East uncertainties.

UTL reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $0.29 and first-half adjusted EPS of $2.17, up 7% year-over-year. The company reaffirmed 2026 EPS guidance of $3.20-$3.36 and 5%-7% long-term growth. The Aquarion New Hampshire water acquisition closed June 30, expected to be earnings neutral in 2026. Rate cases in Maine and New Hampshire are progressing, and the five-year capital plan increased 24% to $1.2 billion through 2030.

Solid Power reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of negative $300,000, impacted by a $1.2 million reversal of previously recognized revenue from an SK On license agreement due to changed milestone assumptions. Net loss was $23.8 million ($0.11 per share), with operating expenses of $30 million. The company advanced its continuous manufacturing pilot line, completed the stage one ISO 9001 audit, and received a milestone payment from SK On, while negotiating a new collaboration agreement. Management expects to announce a joint venture for commercial electrolyte production in South Korea by year-end.

Shoals Technologies reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $163.4 million, up 47% year-over-year, within guidance. Adjusted gross margin was 30.6% and adjusted EBITDA rose 28% to $31.6 million. Record backlog and awarded orders reached $801.4 million, up 19% year-over-year, with a book-to-bill of 1.3. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance of $600-$640 million revenue and $118-$132 million adjusted EBITDA, and announced a TerraFlow MOU for up to 5 GW of storage deployments, with revenue expected to begin in 2027.

Sabra reported Q2 2026 normalized FFO per share of $0.38 and normalized AFFO per share of $0.40, up 3% and 5% year-over-year, respectively, in line with the prior quarter. Total cash NOI rose to $144.3 million from $138.7 million sequentially, driven by managed senior housing growth and rent resets. Same-store managed senior housing revenue grew 8.6% YoY with cash NOI up 13.7%, and portfolio occupancy increased to 88.2%. The company raised and reaffirmed 2026 FFO and AFFO per share guidance, projecting roughly 7% and 8% growth at midpoint, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA fell to 4.61x from 5.04x. Investment activity was robust with about $599 million closed year-to-date and an additional $100 million awarded, plus $330 million in pipeline, with deals yielding about 7.5% initially.

Q2 2026 marked the first full quarter of the U.S. launch of IMCIVREE for acquired hypothalamic obesity, with strong early demand: over 400 start forms from ~300 unique prescribers in 14 weeks, and positive payer access. Management highlighted encouraging RM-718 phase II data showing 11.6% mean BMI reduction at 16 weeks, comparable to setmelanotide and bivamelagon, with no generalized hyperpigmentation. The company reaffirmed its long-term conviction in HO and plans to initiate the bivamelagon phase III trial in HO by end of 2026. No specific financial figures were disclosed in the provided text.

Revvity reported Q2 FY2026 pro forma organic growth of 3%, with total revenue above the high end of expectations and pro forma adjusted EPS of $1.41, well above guidance. The company raised full-year organic growth guidance to 4%-5% (from 3%-4%), adjusted operating margin to ~28.7%, and adjusted EPS to $5.30-$5.40 (up $0.10). Diagnostics grew 11% organically, with Reproductive Health in mid-teens and Newborn Screening reagents up high-single digits. High-content screening demand accelerated, with orders outpacing production capacity, and the company signed a definitive agreement to divest its China Immunodiagnostics business.

In Q2 FY2026, Revolve Group reported net sales of $347 million, up 12% year-over-year, with REVOLVE segment up 13% and FWRD up 11%, and international up 16%. Active customers grew 11% year-over-year to exceed 3 million, and the 115,000 quarterly growth is the highest in four years. Gross margin was 56.6%, including a 160 basis point benefit from tariff refunds; adjusted EBITDA rose to $27 million from $23 million, with EPS of $0.26 versus $0.14 in the prior year. Management expects double-digit revenue growth for the full year and noted July sales up 18% year-over-year.

Q2 2026 net product sales rose 14% YoY to $67M, with record TAVALISSE sales of $47.4M (+18%) and REZLIDHIA up 27% to $8.9M. Guidance was raised on contract revenue to ~$30M (from $20-30M range) while product sales guidance was maintained at $255-265M excluding VEPPANU. VEPPANU launch is on track for mid-August, with no initial sales guidance provided.

Palvella reported Q2 2026 milestones including a successful pre-NDA meeting with FDA for QTORIN rapamycin in microcystic lymphatic malformations, rolling review granted, and first NDA module submitted. The company is on track to complete NDA submission in 2H 2026 with potential approval in 1H 2027. Management increased planned launch sales force to ~40 reps and strengthened balance sheet with $250 million cash, guided pricing range of $100k-$200k per patient per year for mLM. Pipeline expansions include potential approvals in cutaneous venous malformations (2029) and clinically significant angiokeratomas (2031), with a fourth indication to be announced later this year.

Versigent reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with net sales of $2.4 billion, up 11% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA up 25% to $272 million with margin expanding 120 basis points to 11.1%. Adjusted EPS was $1.92. The company initiated a quarterly dividend, and the CEO reiterated that the 2028 outlook does not rely on adjacent market contributions. Management raised confidence in full-year guidance, while noting EMEA softness and China export strength.

RB Global reported Q2 FY2026 total GTV growth of 11% to $4.7 billion, with automotive GTV up 13% and heavy equipment and transportation up 8%. Adjusted EBITDA grew 6%, adjusted EPS rose 6%, and service revenue increased 5% despite a 110 basis point decline in service revenue take rate to 20%. Management raised 2026 guidance, now expecting GTV growth of 9%-11% and adjusted EBITDA growth of approximately 8.6% at the midpoint, including about CAD 500 million from the BigIron acquisition. The company also increased its quarterly dividend by 6.5% and repurchased CAD 150 million of shares.

Viemed reported record Q2 revenue of $78.1M, up 24% YoY, with active ventilator patient count reaching all-time high of 12,635 (up 4.5% sequentially). PAP and resupply grew strongly, and equipment sales nearly doubled to $19M. Adjusted EBITDA was $13.7M (17.6% margin), down YoY partially due to a $1.2M swing in equipment disposal gains. Guidance was raised at the low end for revenue ($314-$320M) but lowered EBITDA to $64-$68M, while net CapEx outlook was cut to 8.5%-10% of revenue.

Vornado reported Q2 2026 comparable FFO of $0.67, beating consensus by $0.10, up from $0.56 a year ago. Manhattan office same-store NOI rose 13.7% GAAP and 11.9% cash, with occupancy up to 92.2% and a pipeline of 2.2M sq ft, expecting occupancy above 93% by year-end. Management raised full-year FFO guidance, citing strong leasing momentum and the 350 Park Avenue investment. Liquidity stands at $2B, with asset sales in progress and a stock buyback of 1.8M shares at $29.92.

In Q2 2026, Viper Energy turned 691 gross horizontal wells to production with an average 3% net revenue interest, and initiated Q3 production guidance implying ~4.5% sequential growth and ~15% annualized per-share oil growth. The company announced a 32% increase in its base dividend to $2 per share annually (~4.5% yield), while removing the previous 75% quarterly payout commitment to fund buybacks, M&A, or debt reduction. Management expressed confidence in the new capital allocation framework, citing a protected dividend to $30 oil and a robust A&D market.

Ultragenyx reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $214 million, driven by strong commercial execution and a rebound in orders after seasonal softness. The company reaffirmed full-year revenue and expense guidance, highlighting continued growth across all products, with Evkeeza up 50% year-over-year. Management emphasized readiness for two gene therapy launches (DTX-401 and UX-111) with PDUFA dates in the coming months, and expects top-line data from the Angelman syndrome phase III ASPIRE study in September or October. The company reiterated a clear path to profitability in 2027, supported by revenue growth, expense discipline, and potential priority review voucher monetization.

BSM reported Q2 FY2026 net income of ~$106M, adjusted EBITDA of $91M, and distributable cash flow of $80M. Production averaged 33.5 MBOE/day, down from Q1 due to lower Haynesville gas volumes, but oil volumes and prices were strong, with realized prices up 7% to $37.82/BOE. The company increased its quarterly distribution 7% to $0.32/unit while maintaining 1.18x coverage. Management remains confident in future production growth, citing increased rig activity and development agreements in the Shelby Trough/Haynesville, and expects more wells online later in 2026.

Voyager Technologies delivered record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $53 million, up 51% sequentially and 15% year-over-year, with record bookings of $113 million (2.1x book-to-bill) and record backlog of $336 million. Adjusted EBITDA loss was $38 million, modestly ahead of internal expectations. Management raised full-year revenue guidance to $275-$305 million (66%-84% growth) and completed the Astrobotic acquisition, expecting $40-$50 million revenue contribution in 2026. Gross margin guidance implies mid-to-high teens in Q3 and low-20s in Q4.

Qualys reported Q2 FY2026 revenue growth of 11% to $182.2 million. The company highlighted strong innovation in AI-driven Risk Operations Center (ROC) and QFlex adoption, but noted macro pressure with a small customer cohort delaying decisions. QFlex rolled out to enterprise customers, and recurring revenue growth was modest. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance and expects growth to accelerate in the back half.

Vitesse Energy reported Q2 2026 production of 17,354 BOE/d, up 9% sequentially, with adjusted EBITDA of $40.2 million and free cash flow of $16.3 million. The company raised the bottom end of its 2026 CapEx guidance to $65-80 million and narrowed production guidance to 16,300-17,200 BOE/d. It continues to pay a $1.75 annualized dividend, has hedged 70% of oil at a weighted average floor of $63.57, and maintains net debt below 1x EBITDA.

Wayfair reported Q2 2026 net revenue growth of 7.5% year-over-year, with U.S. revenue up 8.7% and international down 1.3%. Orders grew 6% YoY and 12% sequentially, with active customers up over 3%. Perigold grew over 35% and specialty retail brands nearly 20%. The company highlighted accelerating order growth for the fourth consecutive quarter and provided Q3 guidance for high-single-digit growth. Management expressed confidence in durable growth and profitability expansion.

SpaceX reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.8 billion, up 92% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $3.5 billion, up 191%. Net loss narrowed to $541 million from $1.008 billion. Starlink added a record 1.7 million net subscribers, holding ARPU at $66, while the space segment grew 29% YoY albeit with a negative adjusted EBITDA due to Starship R&D. The company highlighted early Starship V3 flight success, a new $6 billion US government contract win, and plans to deploy V3 satellites and Starlink Mobile services next year.

Spotify's Q2 2026 revenue grew 15% YoY on a constant currency basis, accelerating from 14% in Q1. Gross margin reached a record 33.4%, and the company crossed 300 million subscribers, beating guidance. Management highlighted strong growth in ads business with active advertisers up 60% YoY, and early success of Reserved ticketing and AI features like Prompted Playlist. They guided to moderate OpEx growth in Q3 and expect Q4 moderation, while noting deliberate friction in free service in emerging markets to boost conversion.

Upstart reported Q2 FY2026 total originations of $4.2 billion, up 50% year-over-year and 23% sequentially, with core personal loans growing 27% quarter-over-quarter. Total revenue was approximately $365 million, up 42% year-over-year, and contribution profit hit an all-time high of $193 million, up 37% year-over-year. Unsecured contribution margin improved to 62% from 56% sequentially, while secured contribution margin improved to -35% from -96%, with expectations to reach breakeven by Q4. The company also received conditional OCC approval for a bank charter, with launch targeted for early 2027, and closed up to $5 billion in new committed institutional capacity.

Q2 revenue was $7.5M, above guidance and up 23% sequentially and more than 80% year-over-year in product sales. The company completed redemption of convertible debt and ended with $21M cash and 314 Bitcoin. Q3 guidance is $8.5M-$10M, with the high end dependent on licensing deals. Supply constraints persist, especially memory, and the company targets breakeven as revenue scales.

TREX reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $418M, up 8% year-over-year, well above expectations. Gross margin was 37.9%, down year-over-year due to mix and temporary manufacturing inefficiencies, but exited June with improved efficiency. The company raised its full-year guidance, increasing adjusted gross margin outlook to ~38% from 37.5%, and announced an additional $150M share repurchase. Demand accelerated through May and June and continued into Q3, with strength across products and channels.

TPG reported Q2 2026 GAAP net income of $93 million and after-tax distributable earnings of $280 million ($0.69 per share). Fee-related revenue grew 27% year-over-year to $628 million, with fee-related earnings up 43% to $315 million and a FRE margin of 50%. AUM reached $327 billion, up 25% year-over-year, and the firm raised $16 billion in the quarter, bringing YTD to $26 billion. Management reiterated confidence in meeting or exceeding its $50 billion full-year fundraising target, citing strong pipelines and record deployment of $14 billion in the quarter. They also highlighted strategic investments in AI including DeployCo commitments of over $4 billion.

Turning Point Brands reported Q2 FY2026 sales up 23% year-over-year to $143 million, driven by Modern Oral (gross up 149%, net up 128% YoY). Modern Oral now accounts for 48% of total revenue, up from 26% a year ago. The company raised full-year Modern Oral gross sales guidance to $330-$350 million and net sales to $260-$270 million, while maintaining EBITDA guidance of $70-$90 million. Adjusted EBITDA declined 50% to $15 million due to increased sales and marketing investments and Zig-Zag softness, partially offset by Modern Oral growth.

Travere delivered record Q2 2026 FILSPARI revenue of over $141 million, with over 2,000 new patient start forms across IgAN and FSGS, and demand in IgAN grew despite new market entrants. The FSGS launch exceeded high expectations, with first-pass payer approval rates tracking ahead of the early IgAN launch. Management raised no formal guidance but expressed strong confidence in continued momentum, while pegtibatinase pivotal data is expected in 2H 2027 and civorebrutinib was added via licensing. IP progress includes a notice of allowance for a sparsentan method-of-use patent in IgAN.

Toast reported Q2 FY2026 with record net location adds of 9,500, ARR growth of 25%, recurring gross profit streams up 28%, and GAAP operating income margin of 26%. The company raised its full-year guidance for recurring gross profit streams, ARR, and adjusted EBITDA, while also increasing investment in new TAMs and AI initiatives. Management cited strong demand and record location adds, but noted higher operating expenses partly due to memory costs and deliberate investments.

TransMedics reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of ~$190M, up 21% YoY and 9% sequentially, with service revenue up 29% YoY and logistics up 39% YoY. Adjusted operating margin was 14% and cash stood at ~$473M. The company raised the low end of full-year revenue guidance to $737M-$757M (22-25% growth), while reaffirming a growth-focused investment strategy across heart/lung, kidney, international expansion, and Gen 3.0 platform. Guidance excludes contributions from ENHANCE Part B, DENOVO, and PAD Aviation investment.

Timken reported Q2 FY2026 total sales of $1.26 billion, up 7.5% year-over-year with organic growth of 4.4%, and adjusted EPS of $1.83, up almost 30% year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 19.6% from 17.7%, with incremental margins over 40%. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance: total sales growth now 5%-6% and adjusted EPS of $6.05-$6.35, up $0.20 at midpoint. Industrial Motion hit a record quarter with sales up 14.6% and margins up 500 basis points to 23.3%.

United Fire Group reported exceptional Q2 2026 results with record net income, record net written premium, and the best second-quarter combined ratio in over 15 years. Net investment income grew 33% to $29 million, and net written premium increased 9%, with a 13.2% return on equity for the first half of 2026. The company maintained a strong competitive position, noting disciplined underwriting and a well-managed catastrophe risk profile, while acknowledging moderating rate achievement and competitive market conditions.

TGS reported Q2 2026 net income of ARS 133 billion, up from ARS 53.8 billion a year ago, driven by a positive financial result variation and strong liquids EBITDA growth. The company announced FID on a $3 billion NGL project with >90% capacity contracted and expects leverage to peak around 3x net debt/EBITDA in 2028-2029. Management noted a reconfiguration in natural gas transportation that will reduce volumes but expects partial tariff compensation, and they are confident about RIGI approval for the NGL project.

In Q2 FY2026, UFPT reported sales up 15.1% to $174 million, with organic growth of 12.4%. Adjusted EPS rose 16.8% to a record $2.92, and gross margin expanded to 29.3% from 28.8%. Growth was broad-based, with top five customers up 14.7% and other MedTech up 19.7%, while the company noted the quarter benefited from a low prior-year comparison. Management expects organic growth to moderate to the 6%-9% target for the rest of the year, and they are progressing on DR transfers, with two of three programs moved and the third still contingent on customer qualification.

Tidewater reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $342.3 million and gross margin of just under 47%, both exceeding expectations. Leading-edge day rates rose 7.5% sequentially, and free cash flow nearly doubled to $64 million. The Wilson Sons acquisition is expected to close around September 1st, and full-year 2026 revenue guidance was modestly reduced to $1.42-$1.47 billion due to the later closing, with gross margin guidance at 49%-50%. Management is confident in a multi-year upcycle, citing tight vessel supply and strong demand trends.

Teradata reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $410 million, flat year-over-year and 2% above the high end of guidance, with recurring revenue up 3% to $363 million, also above guidance. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.69 beat the top end of the range by $0.12, and adjusted free cash flow was $127 million, up significantly year-over-year. Management raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to $2.65-$2.73 and adjusted free cash flow to $330-350 million, while reaffirming ARR, revenue, and recurring revenue outlook. The company launched the Teradata Autonomous Knowledge Platform, expecting new AI product contributions later in the year, but noted consulting services revenue was soft (down 24% year-over-year).

TrueBlue reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $443 million, up 12% and above the high end of guidance, driven by strength in skilled verticals and a return to growth in the on-demand business. Gross margin declined to 20.7% from 23.6% due to one-time prior-year benefits and mix, but SG&A fell 7% and all segments expanded margins. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $11 million from $3 million, and the company guided Q3 revenue growth of 7-11%. Management noted broad-based recovery and improving trends across segments, with energy revenue nearly doubled and commercial driver business growth for the 10th consecutive quarter.

UL Solutions reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $816 million, up 5.2% (organic +6.6%), with adjusted EBITDA up 11.2% to $219 million and margin expansion of 140 bps to 26.8%. Adjusted EPS rose 13.5% to $0.59. Consumer segment saw strong margin growth, while industrial grew 7.8% with slight margin contraction. The company affirmed full-year guidance for mid-single-digit organic growth and ~27% adjusted EBITDA margin, and slightly raised CapEx expectations to ~8.5% of revenue.

Latham Group reported Q2 2026 net sales of $197 million, up 14% YoY with 10% organic growth, and adjusted EBITDA of $45 million, up 12%. Gross margin declined 160 bps to 35.5% due to $2.8 million in ramp-up costs and commodity headwinds, but management expects to recapture most of these costs in H2. The company raised full-year sales growth guidance to 11.7% from 9% and adjusted EBITDA growth to 15.2% from 12.7%, driven by strong demand and share gains, especially in fiberglass and sand states. Management remains confident in momentum despite a flat U.S. pool start market.

Sunoco LP reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $996 million (excluding $14 million of transaction expenses), up sharply year-over-year, with Fuel Distribution EBITDA of $516 million, Pipeline Systems of $190 million, Terminals of $115 million, and Refinery of $175 million. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $3.5-3.7 billion from $3.1-3.3 billion, citing strength across all segments and contributions from recent acquisitions. Distributable Cash Flow as adjusted was $608 million, with a distribution increase of 1.25% sequentially and over 10% year-over-year. Management expressed confidence in continued growth, noting a 2.1x coverage ratio and leverage of approximately 3.7x, below the 4x target.

Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $996 million, excluding $14 million of transaction expenses, leading to a raise in full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $3.5-$3.7 billion, up $400 million from original guidance. Fuel Distribution EBITDA was $516 million, Pipeline $190 million, Terminals $115 million, and Refinery $175 million, with strong volume growth across segments. Distribution was raised 1.25% sequentially and over 10% year-over-year, with trailing 12-month coverage of 2.1x and leverage at 3.7x. Management expressed confidence in continued growth and M&A execution, expecting to exceed their $500 million annual bolt-on acquisition target.

Q2 net sales grew 11.6% to $83.9M and adjusted EBITDA grew 50% to $14.6M (17.5% margin), but the company cited recent third-quarter softness in grocery and widened FY2026 net sales guidance to $360-369M from $367-371M while reiterating adjusted EBITDA guidance of $70-72M. Management outlined action plans including sharper marketing, promotional activity, and distribution gains to target the top end of the range.

Stevanato Group reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of EUR 302 million, up 8% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA up 21% to EUR 78.7 million (26% margin, +180 bps). High-value solutions grew 16% to 45% of revenue, and adjusted EPS rose to EUR 0.14. The company completed the divestiture of Balda C. Brewer, incurring one-time charges of EUR 12.2 million, and updated full-year guidance: revenue reduced to EUR 1.260-1.280 billion, adjusted EBITDA narrowed to EUR 335-345.2 million, and adjusted EPS narrowed to EUR 0.60-0.62. Management remains confident in long-term growth driven by biologics and GLP-1 demand, though Engineering sales cycles remain elongated.

Sterling Infrastructure delivered a strong Q2 2026 with revenue growth of 90% and adjusted EPS growth of 116% to $5.80, beating prior expectations. Adjusted EBITDA more than doubled with margins expanding 150 bps to 22%. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance across revenue, EPS, and EBITDA, citing accelerating demand in E-infrastructure, particularly data centers and semiconductors. Backlog grew significantly to $4.3 billion signed and $5.6 billion combined, with strong book-to-burn ratios, though management noted a potential temporary lull in Q3 awards.

Urban One reported Q2 FY2026 consolidated net revenues of $85.8 million, down 6.4% year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA fell 16% to $11.7 million, with declines across all segments. Management lowered full-year guidance to mid-50s from 60, citing a weak first half, though they expect political spending in Q3 to help. The company repurchased $23.5 million of debt at a discount, closed the Dallas acquisition, and recognized $14.1 million in non-cash impairment charges at Reach Media.

SSR Mining reported Q2 2026 production of 102,000 gold equivalent ounces at an AISC of $2,622/oz, with revenue of $443 million and adjusted EPS of $0.66. The company completed the sale of Çöpler and Hod Maden, exiting Türkiye, and ended the quarter with nearly $1.8 billion in cash and no debt. Management reiterated full-year production guidance but expects AISC to be at the upper end of guidance due to higher fuel costs and accelerated capital spend. Capital returns remain a focus, with $338 million returned via buybacks in Q2 and a reinstated dividend, implying a nearly 8% yield. The company plans to publish an updated Marigold technical report by year-end and is advancing growth projects across the portfolio.

Strata reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with total revenue up 60.7% YoY to $72.5 million, driven by clinical acquisitions and organic growth. Clinical revenue rose 22.6% sequentially, with transplant clinical up 23.8%, and clinical gross margin improved to 26.1%. However, logistics revenue growth slowed, and gross margin fell to 18.4% due to fuel surcharge and customer mix, with a new 3% revenue headwind from one customer. Management raised guidance on acquisition contribution and base business outperformance, while expecting logistics margin to recover to 20% by 2027.

Qnity reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with organic sales up 22% YoY, adjusted EBITDA up 24%, and adjusted EPS up 53% to $1.19, exceeding expectations. Both segments delivered double-digit organic growth, with ICS up 28% and Semi up 17%. Management raised guidance for the full year, citing broad-based demand from AI-driven applications and advanced packaging. The company repriced debt to enhance free cash flow and continues to invest in capacity and innovation.

Waters delivered Q2 FY2026 organic revenue of $828 million, up 9% constant currency, exceeding guidance by ~100 bps, with total revenue of $1.645 billion including $817 million from acquired BD businesses that grew 4% as reported, a 400 bps acceleration from Q1. Adjusted EPS grew 3% to $3.05, hitting the high end of guidance despite FX headwinds. Management raised full-year guidance and highlighted a 10% constant currency organic growth in the first half, with double-digit growth in pharma and academic/government, and strong momentum in acquired businesses with accelerating growth. They also noted 90 basis points of price realization in acquired businesses and a $200 million cost synergy run-rate by Q4.

NJR reported fiscal Q3 2026 NFE of $11.3 million ($0.11 per share), up from $6.2 million ($0.06) a year ago, driven by higher earnings at Clean Energy Ventures and Storage & Transportation. The company raised its fiscal 2026 NFEPS guidance midpoint to $3.52-$3.62, narrowing the range, and increased its capital investment expectations to $815-$950 million, up from the prior $775-$930 million. Management reaffirmed its 7%-9% long-term NFEPS growth target and five-year CapEx outlook, citing strong recontracting at S&T and a deep CEV pipeline. Rate case filings are structured to keep customer bills nearly flat, with no notable regulatory headwinds discussed.

Cabot reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $1.67, up 4% sequentially, with Reinforcement Materials EBIT of $97 million despite pricing headwinds and Performance Chemicals EBIT of $68 million, up 19% year-over-year. The company generated $75 million in operating cash flow and returned $24 million to shareholders. Management reaffirmed battery materials EBITDA of approximately $40 million for fiscal 2026 and revised its U.S. expansion plan from a greenfield Michigan site to brownfield expansions at existing sites, with ~$125 million in capex and capacity coming online in 2028. CEO Sean Keohane announced retirement effective end of fiscal 2026, with CFO Erica McLaughlin appointed as successor.

NMFC reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted net investment income of $0.26 per share, covering the $0.25 dividend, and declared a $0.25 dividend for Q3. NAV per share declined to $10.89 from $10.92, with non-accruals at fair value improving from 2.6% to 1.5%. Management highlighted continued buybacks, portfolio diversification progress, and potential equity monetizations, while industry direct lending volume was weak and pipeline activity is expected to improve.

Metallus reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $29 million, up 9% year-over-year, with net sales of $341 million, up 12%. The company beat prior-year profitability, driven by improved volumes, pricing, and mix, and reaffirmed expectations for sequentially higher adjusted EBITDA in Q3. The order book is up over 50% year-over-year, with record aerospace and defense shipments and a near doubling of industrial backlog. Management guided to slightly higher Q3 adjusted EBITDA sequentially and year-over-year, with price increases announced effective August, fully realized in 2027.

Zeta reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $443 million, up 44% year-over-year (28% ex-M&A), beating guidance by $23 million. Adjusted EBITDA was $92 million, up 56% with margins expanding 170 bps to 20.7%. The company raised full-year revenue guidance by $33 million, marking its 20th consecutive beat-and-raise quarter. Growth was driven by strong customer additions (super scaled customers up 17% to 197) and increased ARPU, with notable contributions from Athena, OpenAI, Snowflake, and Palantir partnerships.

Match Group reported Q2 FY2026 with total revenue down 1% year-over-year and Adjusted EBITDA up 14% year-over-year, beating expectations. Tinder DAU improved to -4% year-over-year, with MAU still declining 7% but improving sequentially, and payers expected to return to growth by Q4 next year. Hinge MAU grew 13% globally with 22% revenue growth, while E&E faces headwinds from Azar's App Store removal. Management raised the outlook for Adjusted EBITDA to at or above the high end and is confident in a Tinder turnaround, with MAU expected flat by Q4 next year and 2027 Tinder revenue up year-over-year.

Millrose Properties reported Q2 FY2026 AFFO of $127.6 million or $0.77 per diluted share, with run-rate AFFO of approximately $0.80 per share at the high end of guidance. Invested Capital reached about $8.8 billion, with $1 billion recycled and $1.1 billion redeployed. The company added two new counterparties including a multifamily land banking relationship with JPI (Sumitomo Forestry), and declared its sixth consecutive quarterly dividend increase to $0.77 per share. No option terminations occurred during the quarter or since inception.

Arrowhead reported Q3 FY2026 results with a strong commercial launch for REDEMPLO in FCS, prescriptions more than doubling quarter-over-quarter. The company announced positive phase III SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 data in SHTG, with 79% and 81% median triglyceride reductions, meeting all primary and secondary endpoints. It acquired a priority review voucher to accelerate FDA review, with sNDA submission expected before end of 2026. Management reiterated confidence in REDEMPLO's potential, citing peak sales estimates of $3-4 billion for SHTG, and expects 23 clinical candidates by year-end.

Merck reported Q2 revenue of $16.6 billion, up 5% (4% ex-FX), with KEYTRUDA family up 4% to $8.4 billion, animal health up 5%, and strong growth from WELIREG (+67%) and WINREVAIR (+75%). The company raised and narrowed full-year revenue guidance to $66.3–67.3 billion (2-4% growth) but EPS guidance of $2.66–2.76 includes a $2.31 per share Terns acquisition charge and a higher tax rate; on an operational basis, they raised EPS guidance. Management expressed high confidence in pipeline progress, noting earlier-than-expected readouts for sac-TMT, I-DXd, and tulisokibart, and reaffirmed 2029 launch timing for their flu vaccine.

TETRA reported Q2 2026 revenue of $185.7 million, up 19% sequentially and 7% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $31.9 million (up 24% sequentially). International and global offshore revenues reached 10-year highs, and the company advanced strategic projects including the Arkansas bromine facility FID and new TETRA Neptune Z-Lite product. Management expects base business to perform in line with market expectations, with potential upside from Neptune jobs and continued growth drivers.

Marqeta reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with net revenue up 17% to $176M, gross profit up 17% to $122M, and TPV up 32% to $120B. Adjusted EBITDA grew 31% with a 21% margin, and the company achieved its second consecutive quarter of GAAP net income at $8M. Management highlighted continued diversification from Block, with non-Block TPV growing over 2x faster, and raised expectations for the remainder of 2026 based on strong execution and product momentum.

MPLX reported Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $1.8 billion, up 5% year-over-year, overcoming the Rockies divestiture. The company highlighted strong utilization (Delaware Basin 86%, Marcellus 96%) and raised its 2026 capital outlook by $500 million to $2.9 billion, primarily pulling forward Gulf Coast fractionation spend. Management reiterated mid-single-digit EBITDA growth for 2026 and 2027, with sequential growth expected in Q3 and Q4, and maintained 12.5% distribution growth guidance for 2026 and 2027, along with a 1.3x coverage target.

MPC reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $8.5 billion, up $5.2 billion year-over-year, with EPS of $17.73. R&M EBITDA per barrel was $24.84, capture was 112%, and Gulf Coast ran at 100% utilization. MPLX raised its 2026 capital growth outlook by $500 million, and the company returned $2.8 billion including $2.5 billion in buybacks. Management expects an enhanced mid-cycle environment through 2027, but Q3 guidance implies capture headwinds from turnaround activity.

MNTN reported Q2 2026 revenue of $82.5 million, up 21% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $21.5 million, up 48%, both at the high end of guidance. Gross margins expanded 350 basis points to 80%, and active PTV customers grew 40% year-over-year to 4,225. Management guided Q3 revenue to $86-$89 million (25% growth at midpoint) and reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $347-$357 million. They announced a $100 million stock repurchase program and highlighted strong adoption of MNTN Express and QuickFrame AI, expecting bigger contributions in 2027.

Paramount reported Q2 2026 with Paramount+ revenue up 16% YoY, adding 2 million net subscribers to reach 81.6 million, ahead of expectations, with best-ever retention and double-digit engagement growth. The company raised adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow guidance, with free cash flow guidance increased 10% before transformation costs, and reiterated over $2.7 billion in run-rate efficiencies. Management remains highly confident in closing the Warner Bros. Discovery combination, noting approvals in 65 jurisdictions and citing strong content performance from UFC, Dutton Ranch, and World Cup.

Emerson's Q3 FY2026 showed underlying sales growth of 6%, with segment EBITA margin expanding 140 basis points to 28.5% and adjusted EPS of $1.71, up 13% and above guidance. Underlying orders grew 7%, with strength in Test & Measurement (up 23%), Ovation (up 23%), and growth verticals (up 27%), including semiconductor up 53%. Full-year guidance was raised: sales growth of 5% (underlying 3.5%), adjusted EPS of $6.55, and free cash flow of $3.6 billion.

Energizer reported organic growth across both batteries and lights and auto care, but moderated consumer demand led to a guidance reduction for the back half of fiscal 2026, with organic growth expected to be roughly flat to up 1% versus prior expectations of ~4%. Battery category trends softened by 200-300 basis points, but the company continues to gain share and expects Q4 gross margin north of 40% and 25% adjusted EPS growth at the midpoint. Free cash flow is expected to be strong with meaningful debt reduction.

Pediatrix reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $76 million, with consolidated revenue up 4% driven by non-same unit activity and 2% same unit growth. Same unit pricing rose 4% on strong RCM collections, payer mix, and acuity, partially offset by volumes down 2% (NICU days down 3%). Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $280-$300 million and continues share buybacks.

Q2 FY2026 global comparable sales grew 1.3%, with U.S. comps at 0.8% missing expectations due to inconsistent value execution, too many restaurant deployments, and underperforming FIFA campaign. Adjusted EPS was $3.38, up 5% constant currency, with a reduced FX tailwind; 50,000 restaurants target pushed to 2028. Management is acting to simplify ops and reallocate marketing.

MasterBrand reported Q2 2026 net sales of $815 million, including $126 million from American Woodmark post-close, with legacy sales of $690 million in line with guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $63 million (7.7% margin), with legacy margin at 8.4% down year-over-year on volume declines and inflation. The company introduced second-half guidance for the combined company, expecting $15 million in synergies in H2 and raising the long-term synergy target to over $100 million annually by year three. Management maintained a cautious market outlook, expecting continued softness and no demand recovery until 2027, while noting ongoing inflation and tariff pressures.

Mattel reported Q2 2026 net sales growth of 10% as reported and 9% constant currency, with North America up 12%, but adjusted EPS fell to $0.01 from $0.21 and adjusted operating income dropped to $39M from $96M, driven by higher advertising, SG&A, and tariff costs. Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance (net sales growth 3%-6% cc, adjusted EPS $1.27-$1.39) and expects a strong 2027 with mid-to-high single-digit top-line growth. Top-line momentum continued into Q3, and the company repurchased $100M of shares in the quarter.

In Q3 FY2026, GBDC reported adjusted net income of $0.22 per share, up from a $0.18 loss last quarter, driven by lower adjusted realized and unrealized losses. Adjusted net investment income was solid at $0.34 per share, covering the $0.33 distribution. Credit performance improved with non-accruals at 1.9%, and NAV declined slightly to $14.25. Management noted better-than-expected performance, with losses mainly from junior debt and equity positions, and highlighted stability in the core debt portfolio.

Macerich reported Q2 FY2026 FFO as adjusted of $0.35 per share, with go-forward portfolio NOI up 3.8% year-over-year. Portfolio sales reached a record $919 per square foot, and go-forward occupancy improved to 95.5%, up 270 basis points year-over-year. The SNO pipeline totals $124 million with $140 million expected total contribution; the company reaffirmed full-year 2026 NOI growth of at least 3% and expects acceleration in 2027 and 2028. Leasing remains ahead of plan (88% speedometer vs 85% target), and management highlighted a robust acquisition pipeline with $372 million in forward proceeds available, while noting one loan still in default at 29th Street.

Lumen reported Q2 2026 results in line with expectations, with total revenue slightly ahead of consensus. Strategic revenue grew 14% year-over-year and now represents 53% of total business revenue, up from 51% in Q1 and 45% a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA was $802 million, down from $877 million a year ago, primarily due to the fiber sale and revenue declines. The company reiterated its cost savings targets of $700 million exiting this year and $1 billion exiting next year. Alkira acquisition closed in early July and is viewed as upside to digital revenue targets.

Q2 revenue was a record $201 million, up 18% sequentially and 62% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.53, up over 120% year-over-year and above the high end of guidance, driven by strength across all end markets, especially compute and communications. Q3 guidance calls for FPGA revenue of $210-230 million and combined revenue of $245-265 million, including two months of AMI, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.54-0.58, which implies roughly 100% year-over-year EPS growth. The acquisition of AMI closed in late July and is expected to be accretive to EPS starting in Q4, with AMI expected to exit 2026 at a revenue run rate of more than $200 million and grow 25% in 2027. New product revenue is expected to exceed 25% of total revenue this year, and the company described a 'rule of 105' based on 62% growth and over 40% EBITDA margin.

Jacobs reported Q3 FY2026 adjusted EPS of $1.84, up 14% year-over-year, with 8% organic adjusted net revenue growth and 109 basis points of adjusted EBITDA margin expansion. Backlog reached a record $29 billion, up 27% year-over-year, with a book-to-bill of 1.4x. Management raised full-year guidance for the third consecutive time, with adjusted EPS now guided to $7.20-$7.30 and Q4 net revenue growth expected around 14%. AI-related work represents 11% of adjusted net revenue, with a strong pipeline of future AI infrastructure projects.

Zebra reported Q2 FY2026 sales of over $1.5 billion, up 20.4% total and 9.2% organic, exceeding the high end of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 7.1 points to 27.7% (including $73M tariff recovery), and non-GAAP EPS jumped 76% to $6.35. The company raised its full-year sales outlook to 14%-16% growth and expects non-GAAP EPS of $20.75-$21.25, while navigating a memory cost headwind of approximately $120M. Q3 guidance calls for adjusted EBITDA margin near 22% and non-GAAP EPS of $4.70-$4.90.

Enpro reported strong second quarter 2026 results with sales up 17.6% year-over-year to $338.8 million, adjusted EBITDA up over 22% to $86.9 million (margin 25.6%, up 90 bps), and adjusted EPS of $2.50, up 23.2%. The company raised full-year 2026 guidance: sales growth now expected 14%-16% (up from 10%-14%), adjusted EBITDA $330-$340 million (up from $315-$330 million), and EPS $9.30-$9.80 (up from $8.85-$9.50). AST sales rose 21.8% with strong semiconductor demand, and Sealing Technologies grew 15.3% overall (5% organic) despite soft commercial vehicle and European markets.

Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $1.2B, up 34% YoY, driven by the acquired LS Power portfolio, higher PJM capacity values, and Smart Home growth, but adjusted EPS fell to $1.49 from $1.73 due to higher interest and D&A. The company reaffirmed 2026 guidance but expects to be below the midpoint due to weak ERCOT prices. Management announced a 1.2 GW BYOP project with a hyperscaler, targeting late 2029 COD, with $500M annual EBITDA and $375M FCF at full operation, and plans to maintain $1B annual buybacks.

Xometry reported record Q2 FY2026 results with revenue up 41% YoY to $229 million, marketplace revenue accelerating to 45% YoY, and adjusted EBITDA improving to $14.1 million. Active buyers grew 20% YoY to over 89,000, with a record net addition of 175 accounts spending over $50,000. Management raised second-half guidance again, citing strong Q3 momentum and confidence in AI-driven growth and operating leverage. Gross margin is expected to expand toward the 35-40% target range over time, with marketplace gross margin up about 100 basis points in the first half.

United Parks reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $483.3 million, down 1.4% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $195.5 million, down $10.8 million. Attendance declined 2.9% due to Easter timing and lower international visitation, but in-park per capita spending rose 5.1% to a record. July revenue is preliminarily down 2% due to poor weather, while management continues to pursue real estate monetization and maintains its $50 million cost savings target for 2026.

Whirlpool reported Q2 2026 net sales of $3.5 billion and an ongoing EPS of -$0.21, with sequential EBIT margin improvement of 50 basis points to 1.8%. Management reaffirmed full-year operational outlook, adjusting EPS for updated interest expense, and cited strong pricing execution in North America and new product momentum. They expect further margin improvement in Q3 and Q4, supported by cost actions and new pricing in Latin America.

Q2 FY2026 total revenue was $94.5M, up 19% YoY, with U.S. revenue up 20% at $83.4M. U.S. procedures grew 21% to 13,100, softer than expected, primarily due to legacy AquaBeam accounts. HYDROS placements were strong at 65 systems, with ASP at $495,000, and gross margin improved to 66% (including a $2.9M tariff recovery). Full-year revenue and gross margin guidance were maintained, but U.S. procedure guidance was lowered to 54,000-56,000, and adjusted EBITDA loss guidance was widened to $35M-$30M.

Wix reported Q2 bookings growth of 12% YoY and revenue growth of 15% YoY, with Self-Creators revenue accelerating to 14% and Partners revenue up 17%. Base44 gross margin improved from near 0% to approximately 60% in the second half, driven by the new proprietary LLM Base1, but the company plans to reinvest these savings into sales and marketing, keeping guidance unchanged. Management expressed confidence in AI strategy and product leadership, though they noted some FX headwinds and elevated S&M expenses.

Workiva reported Q2 FY2026 with 19% growth in both subscription and total revenue, beating the high end of revenue guidance. Non-GAAP operating margin was 16.8%, a 1,300 basis point improvement year-over-year and 180 basis points above guidance. The company raised full-year non-GAAP operating margin guidance to 18%, achieving a 2027 target a year early. Demand was strong across the portfolio, with large contract cohorts growing over 30% year-over-year.

People Inc. reported Q2 2026 digital revenue growth of 6%, marking the 11th consecutive quarter of growth. Adjusted EBITDA grew 18% with margins expanding to 26% from 23%. Licensing grew 23% and performance marketing grew 13%. The company signed an agreement to watch a limited partner stake for ~$189 million, and expects mid-to-high single-digit digital revenue growth for the full year. Plans for leadership transition and increased MGM ownership were reiterated.

Pinnacle West reported Q2 2026 EPS of $1.43, down $0.15 YoY, with strong customer and sales growth (2.1% customer growth, 9.6% weather-normalized sales growth) partially offset by higher interest, depreciation, and lower transmission revenue. Management reiterated full-year guidance of $4.55-$4.75, expecting to finish at the top end, and highlighted major growth drivers including TSMC's additional $100 billion investment and a new $500 million ATM program. The company is progressing through its rate case and expects a final commission decision before year-end.

Pinterest reported Q2 2026 revenue growth of 18% globally and in UCAN, a five-point acceleration in its largest market, with 640 million monthly active users and 12th consecutive quarter of record users. The company highlighted AI-driven monetization improvements, including Performance+ and Smart Assembly, and noted early success in UCAN go-to-market transformation. Guidance and specific financials were not fully detailed in the provided excerpt, but the tone is confident with a focus on durable growth and cost-efficient AI.

Progressive discussed its Q2 FY2026 results, highlighting continued auto dominance (now the largest U.S. personal auto writer) and a property turnaround with a 75% combined ratio in 2025 and 78% YTD 2026. Management emphasized disciplined, surgical rate decreases—30 states representing 63% of premium saw new business rate cuts—and reiterated the goal of growing as fast as possible at or below a 96% combined ratio. The call focused on the long-term Robinsons opportunity, especially in agency, with investments in property capabilities expected to drive future growth. No specific financial figures (revenue, EPS) were provided in the transcript; guidance was not explicitly quantified but tone was confident about competitive positioning.

Q2 FY2026 showed strong performance with revenue of $194 million, EBT of $38.1 million, net income of $28.7 million, and diluted EPS of $1.31. AUM grew 21% year-over-year to $4.4 billion, with WAC AUM up nearly 80% to $1.4 billion. Lease rent revenue rose 6.7%, while short-term maintenance reserve revenue declined due to lower flight hours on older engines; however, management sees recovery and remains confident in growth prospects. The company closed on a $379 million portfolio transaction in July and has $1.3 billion of additional deployable capital.

Precigen reported Q2 2026 PAPZIMEOS revenue of $53.1 million, up 145% from $21.6 million in Q1, driving net income of $20.1 million and operating income of $22.6 million. Gross margin was 95% on product sales, with expectations to stabilize in the high-80s to low-90s after watching remaining pre-launch inventory. Management highlighted strong commercial momentum, broad payer coverage of ~315 million lives, and FDA-granted seven-year exclusivity, while reiterating cash flow breakeven by end of 2026.

Pfizer reported Q2 2026 revenue of $15 billion, up 1% operationally year-over-year, with a 5% operational increase excluding COVID products, and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.77, both exceeding expectations. The company raised the midpoint of full-year 2026 revenue guidance while reaffirming adjusted EPS guidance, which includes a $0.10 impact from the Innovent Biologics transaction. Management highlighted strong growth in launched and acquired products (18% operational, 27% excluding one-time items), particularly from legacy Seagen (21% US growth ex-items), and increased net cost savings expectations to $6.7 billion through 2029. A $4.3 billion non-cash intangible impairment was recorded in the quarter, primarily related to a phase III readout for SV in second-line lung cancer and removal of Vabryda revenue projections.

PSEG reported Q2 2026 non-GAAP EPS of $0.86, up from $0.77 a year earlier, and reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $4.28-$4.40 per share. The utility segment (PSE&G) grew earnings on infrastructure and energy-efficiency investments, while PSEG Power benefited from higher realized market prices and nuclear output, partially offset by the end of ZEC programs. Management announced an expected base rate case filing by year-end 2026 and cited regulatory clarity from PJM and New Jersey proceedings, including the Power in New Jersey Act enabling new nuclear development.

Pacira reported Q2 FY2026 total revenues of $192.4M, up 6% YoY, with EXPAREL net sales up 3% to $147.8M and ZILRETTA up 4% to $32.6M. Adjusted EBITDA was approximately $48.7M, and GAAP net income was $4.7M. The company highlighted significant market access wins (UnitedHealthcare separate reimbursement for EXPAREL, ZILRETTA preferred drug list), closed the iovera° divestiture to Zimmer Biomet for up to $140M, and confirmed several pipeline catalysts on track for year-end. Guidance was not explicitly reiterated but management expressed confidence in sustainable growth, noting macroeconomic softness in elective procedures but strength in outpatient settings.

Westlake delivered Q2 2026 net sales of $3.3 billion and EBITDA of $679 million, a substantial improvement from both Q1 2026 and Q2 2025. PEM EBITDA surged to $416 million, up $364 million year-over-year, driven by higher oil prices, advantaged North American feedstock costs, and the three-pillar profitability plan contributing ~$150 million. HIP revenue grew 8% year-over-year with 6% organic volume growth, but EBITDA margin contracted slightly to 22% from 24%. Management reiterated the $600 million 2026 EBITDA benefit target from the profitability plan and noted improved plant reliability with no major turnarounds expected in H2.

Williams reported Q2 2026 EBITDA of $1.92 billion, up 6% year-over-year, and increased full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance to $8.3-$8.5 billion, reflecting a $200 million midpoint raise. The company announced two major strategic moves: a Power Innovation financing JV with Blackstone providing $5.34 billion of committed capital, and the $5.5 billion acquisition of Momentum Midstream. Long-term EBITDA growth target was raised from 10%+ to 11%+ CAGR through 2030, with leverage forecast at 3.75x on a run-rate basis.

Otter Tail reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.66, down 10% year-over-year due to lower PVC pipe prices and higher corporate costs, but above expectations with strong manufacturing and plastics volumes. Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was raised to $5.68-$6.08 from $5.22-$5.62, excluding the $103.5 million PVC antitrust settlement. Plastics segment adjusted results beat forecasts, with sales volumes up 15% and ASP decline moderating to 14%, though management expects continued pricing pressure into 2027. The company also secured route permits for two transmission projects and filed its 15-year IRP with Minnesota, reaffirming a 10% rate base growth CAGR.

Wynn reported mixed Q2 results with strong Las Vegas and Macau performance, but faced notable headwinds. Las Vegas EBITDA was $215.2M on $643.2M revenue, Macau EBITDA was $297M on $1B revenue, and Boston EBITDA was $56.1M on $209.3M revenue. Management raised Al Marjan Island budget by $600M and delayed opening to September 2027. Guidance for 2026 Macau expansion CapEx is $350M-$400M, and liquidity remains strong at $4B. The company continues to invest in growth projects and returned capital via dividends.

OneSpan reported Q2 FY2026 total revenue of $60.5 million, up 1% YoY, with subscription revenue up 11% to $47 million and adjusted EBITDA margin of 28%. ARR grew 7% to $190 million, with NRR at 103%. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $248-$252 million from $244-$249 million and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $67-$71 million from $64-$68 million, citing higher e-signature overages and increased hardware bookings. Management also highlighted the launch of DigipassONE platform as a strategic milestone.

OPENLANE reported strong Q2 FY2026 results with consolidated revenue up 15% to $555 million and adjusted EBITDA up 19% to $103 million, beating expectations. Marketplace vehicles sold grew 27%, GMV up 41% to $10.5 billion, with U.S. dealer units up 31% and commercial vehicles up 39% (14% ex-new private label). The company raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $385-$400 million. Management remains optimistic about continued off-lease growth and share gains, though diesel price increases pressured transport margins and AFC loan loss rate held at 1.2%.

Opendoor reported Q2 FY2026 results with contract volume exceeding 6,000 per week, above the high end of internal projections, and pacing above the $9 billion revenue breakeven framework. Marketing spend fell to $5 million (from over $80 million historically) and contribution margins reached the target range, with fixed OpEx at 2.1% of acquisition GMV. Management reaffirmed ANI profitability by end of 2026 on a 12-month go-forward basis, citing AI-driven operational leverage and margin improvements, while acknowledging Q3 seasonal margin decline and Doma integration drag.

ONEOK reported Q2 2026 net income of $965 million, or $1.53 per diluted share, up 13% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA of $2.12 billion, up 7%. The company raised its full-year 2026 guidance for the second time, now expecting net income midpoint of $3.6 billion, EPS of $5.68, and adjusted EBITDA of $8.35 billion, driven by record NGL throughput, strong refined products demand, and volume growth. Management also extended its cash tax runway to 2031, increasing expected cumulative cash tax benefits to approximately $2.6 billion, and reaffirmed its long-term target of mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA growth.

NXRT reported Q2 2026 core FFO of $0.66 per share, a penny ahead of consensus, but total revenue declined 0.6% on a same-store basis and same-store NOI fell 2.9%. Management lowered full-year 2026 core FFO guidance to a midpoint of $2.45 from $2.57, driven mainly by higher interest expense ($0.16) and softer same-store revenue ($0.09), partially offset by lower expense growth and interest income. Leasing momentum improved, with blended trade-outs turning positive in July, and supply is declining, supporting a recovery expected in late 2026 into 2027.

BXDC completed its IPO in May 2026, raising $2 billion, the largest blind pool REIT IPO in history. Q2 GAAP net income was $0.14 per share, FFO $0.07, and AFFO $0.08, with no real estate operations yet; results reflect only post-IPO period interest income of $9.3 million and minimal expenses. Management is confident in deploying capital at attractive yields, citing a robust pipeline, strong market fundamentals (1% vacancy), and supportive comparable transactions at low-to-mid six cap rates.

loanDepot reported Q2 FY2026 adjusted net loss of $29 million, improved from $34 million in Q1, with origination volume of $8 billion (up 4% sequentially) and pull-through weighted rate lock volume of $6.6 billion (down 20% sequentially) due to HELOC mix. Gain on sale margin rose to 345 bps, within guidance, and expenses were nearly flat. Third-quarter guidance calls for origination volume of $6.25-$8.25 billion and pull-through weighted gain on sale margin of 360-390 bps, with expectations for somewhat lower expenses.

Arista Networks reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of just over $3 billion, up 37.7% year-over-year and above guidance of $2.8 billion, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.02, up 39.7% year-over-year. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $12.6 billion, implying 40% annual growth, an increase from the prior $11.5 billion projection. Gross margin was 63.4%, down from 65.6% a year ago but up from 62.4% last quarter. Management highlighted ongoing supply chain improvements, increased AI momentum with over 100 cumulative Etherlink customers, and raised guidance for the third time this year.

Vornado reported Q2 2026 comparable FFO of $0.67 per share, beating consensus by $0.10 or 17.5%. N.Y. office same store NOI grew 13.7% GAAP and 11.9% cash; N.Y. office occupancy rose to 92.2% from 84.4% trough. Management raised full-year guidance, expecting 2026 FFO above 2025, with significant growth in 2027. The company repurchased 1.8M shares at $29.92 and anticipates occupancy above 93% by year-end.

ATEC reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $214 million, up 15% year-over-year, with surgical revenue of $196 million, up 17%. Cases were up about 20% and surgeons about 24%. Adjusted EBITDA was $36 million, up about 53% year-over-year, with 17% margin and positive free cash flow of $1 million. The company reaffirmed full-year revenue guidance of approximately $882 million, but raised adjusted EBITDA guidance to $140 million from $134 million, and expects Q3 free cash flow of $4-6 million.

Arvinas reported Q2 2026 with cash of $567.9 million, down from $685.4 million at end of 2025. The FDA approved VEPPANU (first PROTAC degrader) and it was out-licensed to Rigel Pharmaceuticals. The KRAS G12D program ARV-806 is deprioritized for partnering. Clinical milestones: ARV-393 phase I data expected by end of 2026, ARV-027 healthy volunteer data in H1 2027, ARV-102 trials now expected to begin in 2027. Financials include a one-time revenue recognition from Pfizer collaboration and a $52.7 million liability for VEPPANU closeout.

Alexandria Real Estate Equities reported Q2 2026 FFO per share of $1.73, reaffirming the midpoint of 2026 guidance at $6.40 while tightening the range to ±$0.05. Leasing volume was 1.039 million sq ft, up 60% sequentially and 9% above the prior four-quarter average, but operating occupancy declined 80 bps to 86.9%. Same-property NOI declined 10.6% (8.6% cash basis), an improvement from the prior quarter's 13.1% and 3.8% cash decreases. Management remains committed to a $2.9 billion capital target, extending the credit facility to 2032, and projects 950,000 sq ft of leasing in Q3.

Aptiv reported Q2 2026 revenue of $3.3 billion (up 2% adjusted), EBITDA of $613 million with 10 bps margin expansion, and EPS of $1.63. Management lowered full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $12.6–12.8 billion (from prior ~$13 billion) due to prolonged weakness in the domestic China auto market and reduced schedules from European luxury OEMs. Despite this, non-auto revenue grew 12% and the company highlighted robotics/drone momentum, including a $500M drone award, and expects about $300M annual revenue from these markets. Share repurchases totaled $325 million year-to-date, with plans for over $600 million for the full year.

Apollo reported record FRE of $785M (+25% YoY) and record SRE of $877M, driving ANI of $1.3B ($2.11/share). Originations were $74B in Q2 with $50B signed and announced to benefit future quarters, and capital formation hit a record $60B. Management reaffirmed the $85B inflow target for the year and expects FRE/SRE growth on track. The tone is confident, stressing momentum, technological innovation, and regulatory leadership.

ADTRAN reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $281.1M, up 6.1% YoY but below guidance due to a single-customer project delay and supply constraints that caused unfavorable mix. Non-GAAP operating margin was 3.8%, down sequentially from 6.9%. Optical revenue grew 22% YoY, and enterprise/government/cloud revenue grew 47% YoY, with hyperscaler revenue up 97%. Q3 guidance of $275-295M revenue and 1.5-5.5% operating margin reflects ongoing supply uncertainty.

Record Renewables earnings drove a strong Q2 2026, with adjusted EPS of $2.15 and adjusted EBITDA of $140M, up from $0.24 and $65M in the prior year. Renewables pre-tax income surged to $88M from $10M, aided by $24M in 45Z credits, while Agribusiness pre-tax income improved to $20M. Management reaffirmed the $7 per share EPS target by 2028, citing strong execution and favorable market conditions.

Amwell's Q2 2026 revenue was $52 million, down 26.6% YoY, with subscription revenue down 36.5% YoY but up 3.2% sequentially. Adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $1.15 million from $4.7 million loss a year ago. The company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to a loss of $9-$7 million from prior range of $16-$12 million and narrowed revenue guidance to $200-$205 million. It also received an intent to award for a sole source contract from the Defense Health Agency and expects to achieve positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2026.

Amgen reported Q2 2026 total revenues exceeding $10 billion, a 10% year-over-year increase, with 22 products achieving double-digit sales growth and 17 products annualizing above $1 billion. Six key growth drivers grew 26% year-over-year and represented nearly 70% of product sales, with Repatha up 37%, EVENITY up 38%, TEZSPIRE up 42%, rare disease up 21%, innovative oncology up 18%, and biosimilars up 29%. Prolia/XGEVA declined 33% due to biosimilar competition, as expected, but management expressed confidence in durable growth driven by a strong pipeline and expanded indications.

AMETEK reported record Q2 FY2026 results with sales of $2.04 billion, up 15% YoY (organic +10%), and EPS of $2.09, up 17% and above guidance of $1.96-$2.00. Operating margins expanded 60 bps to 26.6%, core margins up 110 bps, and free cash flow rose 37% to $452 million. Orders were exceptional at $2.3 billion, up 28%, with organic orders up 25%, supporting record backlog of $4.11 billion. Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $8.20-$8.30, and sales growth guidance increased to about 10%, with organic growth now expected mid to high single digits.

AMD reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $11.5 billion, up 50% year-over-year, with data center revenue more than doubling to $6.7 billion, representing 58% of total revenue. The company raised its long-term outlook, expecting data center revenue to more than double in 2027 and tracking ahead of its prior financial model. Management expressed strong confidence in the demand environment, citing new partnerships with Anthropic and Microsoft for Helios, with supply chain tightness in server CPUs expected to ease in 2027.

Alight's Q2 2026 revenue of $511M beat market expectations, driven by higher project revenue and volumes, but total revenue fell 3% YoY and recurring revenue dropped 4.3% due to prior-year commercial activity. Adjusted EBITDA was $92M (18% margin), down from $127M (24% margin) a year ago, with adjusted EPS of $0.91 versus $2.09. Full-year revenue guidance of $2.078-2.098B and EBITDA of $400-415M imply a significant Q4 rebound after a weak Q3; management expects commercial improvements to flow through by 2028.

Ball reported Q2 FY2026 global beverage can volumes up 4.3% YoY, comparable operating earnings up 7.7%, and comparable diluted EPS up 14.4%, driven by cost discipline and capital allocation tailwinds. North America volumes grew low single digits with segment earnings down 2.4% on startup costs, EMEIA volumes rose mid-single digits with earnings up 6.6%, and South America volumes grew mid-teens with earnings up 64%. Management reaffirmed the full-year framework of 10+% comparable EPS growth, free cash flow above $900 million, and ~$800 million in shareholder returns, while noting North America remains 'notably tight' until Millersburg ramps fully in 2027.

Allegiant reported record Q2 revenue with combined TRASM up over 20% YoY for both brands, and standalone Allegiant TRASM up 24.6%. The company closed the Sun Country acquisition, is on track for full-year 2026 EPS of at least $6 per share, and expects Q3 unit revenue growth in line with Q2. Despite Sun Country pilot attrition and elevated fuel costs, management expects Q3 operating profit and full-year margin expansion.

Alamo Group reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $415.7 million, up 7.6% YoY, with organic growth of 1.3%. Adjusted EPS rose 7.2% to $2.82, and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 14.2%. Gross margin declined 120 bps to 24.6% due to mix and investments, while industrial equipment sales grew 12.8% (organic +2.6%) and vegetation management sales edged up 0.4%, marking the second consecutive quarter of growth. Management expects flattish industrial end markets near term and sees procurement savings contributing mainly next year, with a strong M&A pipeline.

Astera Labs reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $392.4 million, up 27% sequentially and 104% year-over-year, driven by broad-based strength across Aries, Scorpio, and Taurus. PCIe 6 revenue exceeded 50% of total, and Scorpio X-Series entered volume production, with Scorpio expected to become the largest product family in Q3, one quarter ahead of plan. Management raised the outlook for continued growth in the second half, with Scorpio X ramping to additional customers by year-end and multiple product lines expected to grow. The tone is confident, highlighting strong execution, expanding design wins, and a multi-year growth trajectory across AI infrastructure.

Albany International reported Q2 2026 revenue of $329.5 million, up 5.8% year-over-year, driven by a 16% increase in Engineered Composites to $150.8 million, a quarterly record. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $57.8 million (17.6% margin) from $51.9 million, with Machine Clothing EBITDA flat at $50 million despite a machine failure. Adjusted EPS exceeded forecast, but consolidated revenue was modestly below expectations due to the Machine Clothing equipment downtime and delayed tooling for a defense contract. Full-year Machine Clothing revenue is now expected to be slightly down versus 2025, while Engineered Composites is expected to grow, with Q3 guidance of $320-$330 million revenue and $0.60-$0.70 Adjusted EPS.

Q2 FY2026 FFO as adjusted was $0.14 per diluted share, with AFFO of $0.18, and the company raised full-year guidance to $0.53-$0.57. The multifamily portfolio sale proceeds materially delevered the balance sheet, and retail/office same-store NOI grew 2.9% and 8.3% year-over-year. The company repurchased over $33 million of shares and maintains a BBB credit rating.

AdaptHealth delivered strong top-line growth in Q2 FY2026, with continuing ops revenue up 12.7% YoY to $740.3M and organic growth of 15.9%, driven largely by the new West Coast capitated contract. However, Adjusted EBITDA fell to $132M from $136.4M, and management cited two major profit headwinds: a $40M expected impact from West Coast contract cost overruns and a $30M second-half hit from a manufacturer's contract termination and price increase. The company reset full-year guidance downward, announced a workforce restructuring for $19M in annualized savings, and is divesting its Diabetes Health business to sharpen focus. Free cash flow was negative at -$20.9M due to heavy capex, and a $144.2M non-cash goodwill impairment was recorded.

AGNT reported record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.4 billion, up 11% year-over-year, at the high end of guidance. Adjusted EBITDA was $25.7 million, above the high end of guidance and up 129% year-over-year. Agents grew 6% to 87,338, with transactions up 12% and productivity per agent up 6%. International revenue grew 44% and its operating loss improved 57%. Full-year revenue guidance was held at $4.85-5.15 billion, while Adjusted EBITDA guidance was tightened to $50-60 million with operating expenses guided lower to $355-365 million. Management highlighted AI-driven efficiency gains, including DocAI and task automation, and discussed the NextHome acquisition as a strategic bolt-on for multi-model growth, though it is sub-10% of revenue and not materially profitable yet.

Atlas Energy Solutions reported Q2 2026 revenue of $293.2 million and adjusted EBITDA of $49.5 million, with an EBITDA margin of about 17%. The key highlight was signing the first behind-the-meter power purchase agreement for a 120-MW facility with a projected $55 million annualized adjusted free cash flow and a payback of under 3.5 years. Oilfield power remains on track to exit the year at 180-200 MW deployed. The core sand/logistics market is described as 'nuanced,' with management expecting moderate activity ramp in Q4 and a tight market despite low pricing, with the company intentionally pushing logistics pricing to test the market.

Addus HomeCare reported Q2 2026 revenue of $377.4 million, up 8% YoY, and adjusted EPS of $1.73, up 16.1%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 11.9% to $49.2 million, with margin expanding to 13%. Personal care same-store revenue grew 6.8%, driven by 2.2% same-store hour growth; hospice same-store revenue rose 11.1%, while home health same-store revenue declined 2.8% but improved sequentially. Management raised expectations for personal care organic growth to 6-6.5% for 2026 and remains optimistic about eliminating the 80/20 rule and M&A pipeline.

ACADIA reported Q2 2026 total revenues of $308 million, up 17% year-over-year on an adjusted basis, with DAYBUE at $125 million (up 30%) and NUPLAZID at $183 million (up 10%). The company raised DAYBUE full-year guidance to $480-$510 million, reaffirmed NUPLAZID guidance at $760-$790 million, and expects total 2026 revenue of $1.24-$1.3 billion. Strong DAYBUE STIX uptake (40% of U.S. patients) and a positive CHMP opinion for trofinetide support the raised outlook. The phase II remlifanserin readout is expected in September-October, with Fast Track designation received.

Q2 FY2026 revenue grew 10% YoY to $368 million and adjusted EBITDA grew 11% to $59 million, both all-time quarterly records. Net income grew to $13 million. Illinois revenue ex-Fairmount grew 6% with average location hold per day up 9% to $992, while location and terminal counts declined. Developing markets Nebraska and Georgia grew revenue 55% and 47%, respectively, and are now contributing to EBITDA growth. Nevada revenue grew 17%, but hold per day declined ~16% due to convenience-store mix shift. Chicago licensing is progressing with Accel approved for 17 of 39 establishments; first openings expected in coming weeks. No formal guidance provided, but July results were consistent with the first half.

Atomera reported Q2 2026 revenue of $158,000, GAAP net loss of $6.3 million ($0.17 per share), and non-GAAP loss of $5 million. The company highlighted a significant Gate-All-Around milestone with one customer, a new 4F² DRAM value proposition, NAND interest, and strong GaN-on-Silicon RF results that attracted new customers. However, costs are rising, and the company now expects 2026 non-GAAP operating expenses near the high end of its $18.5 million ±$250,000 range.

ADM reported Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.84 and segment operating profit of $1.5 billion, with total segment operating profit up significantly YoY. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.15-$5.60 from $4.15-$4.70, citing strong performance in biofuels, crush volumes up ~5%, and momentum in Nutrition (especially flavors). CFO noted strong cash flow of $1.8 billion in H1, and management discussed expansion of U.S. crush capacity, natural colors opportunities, and potential share repurchases.

Boise Cascade's Q2 2026 consolidated sales rose 5% YoY to $1.8 billion, with EPS of $1.63 up from the prior year excluding asset-sale gains. Wood Products EBITDA increased to $52.4 million from $37.3 million, while BMD EBITDA fell to $85.6 million from $91.8 million. Management guided Q3 BMD EBITDA between $53-$68 million and Wood Products EBITDA between $22-$57 million, citing James Hardie transition and demand uncertainty. The company expanded its James Hardie partnership to sole nationwide distribution, expecting near-term revenue pressure, and increased its dividend by 5%.

Brightstar Lottery reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $584 million, in line with expectations, and adjusted EBITDA up 4% to $286 million, better than expected. Global same-store sales rose 1.5%, with iLottery wagers up 22% in the first half. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance, expects accelerated H2 growth, and highlighted a 3.24x leverage ratio, ahead of target, with over $400 million annual free cash flow potential.

Booking Holdings reported Q2 2026 results that exceeded the high end of guidance across all key financial metrics, with room nights growing 5% year-over-year. While international long-haul travel remained pressured due to the Middle East conflict, domestic and intraregional demand was healthy, with U.S. room nights up high single digits. The company noted modest shifts in travel behavior, including shorter booking windows and length of stay, but these began normalizing in June. AI investments are showing positive ROI, and the company maintains confidence in its long-term growth strategy.

Bed Bath & Beyond reported a second consecutive quarter of base e-commerce revenue growth after 19 quarters of decline, with omni-channel revenue up 28% and orders doubled. The company exceeded its Q2 expectations, primarily driven by SG&A savings and margin improvement. Management guided third-quarter net revenue to the low $500 million range and outlined plans to exit $50+ million in annualized costs while achieving mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA margins in a mid-cycle housing environment. They also discussed strategic acquisitions and partnerships, including Fathom's title business and Alliant Credit Union, to build an integrated homeownership platform.

Bruker returned to organic revenue growth in Q2 2026, with reported revenue up 5.2% to $838.5 million and organic growth of 2.8% (3.4% excluding U.S. tariff refunds). Non-GAAP EPS of $0.49 was up 53% year-over-year, with non-GAAP gross margin up 350 bps to 52.1% and operating margin up 510 bps to 14.1%, aided by cost savings and tariff refunds. Management raised its full-year 2026 EPS guidance despite trimming top-line guidance due to FX and tariff timing, while reiterating $140 million of annualized cost savings and expecting additional $20 million in 2027 from a new operating structure. Bookings showed strength in biopharma (up >20% organic) and deep tech (semiconductor and energy research both up >50% organic), though U.S. academic order weakness persists and some revenue is pushed to Q4 and 2027 due to long lead times.

Bio-Rad reported Q2 2026 revenue of $651M, roughly flat as reported and down 1.9% on a currency-neutral basis, with clinical diagnostics returning to modest growth and life science still soft. Digital PCR grew 6% with instrument revenue up over 20%, and the company repurchased 110,000 shares. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed, including currency-neutral revenue growth of -3% to +0.5% and operating margin of 10-12%. Management is cautiously optimistic but highlights continued softness in academic markets, China headwinds, and Middle East volatility.

BioNTech reported Q2 2026 results with a revenue guidance reduction of EUR 400 million at the midpoint, primarily due to weaker COVID-19 vaccination rates, partially offset by expected BMS collaboration revenues. The company highlighted progress in its oncology pipeline, including encouraging phase II data for pumitamig in first-line non-small cell lung cancer and the start of a phase III trial for its B7-H3 ADC in prostate cancer. Management expressed confidence in its strategy to become a multi-product company by 2030 but faced questions about milestones and competitive data read-through.

BP reported a 'good quarter' with net debt down $3 billion sequentially and financial obligations down $7 billion since Q1. However, operational performance fell short and cost reductions have not yet flowed to the bottom line; management guided to $18 billion in structural costs by end of 2026, from $22 billion in 2025. BPX production grew to 545,000 boe/d, with a new basin production record. Management emphasized 'Fit to Grow' strategy, portfolio simplification, and balance sheet strengthening, but acknowledged past impairments and slower cost progress.

BlackLine reported Q2 FY2026 revenue growth of 9.2%, non-GAAP operating margin of 23.3%, and $37 million free cash flow. Approximately $8 million of expected Q2 deals slipped, with half already closed. RPO grew 17% to over $1.1 billion, platform ARR crossed 17% of eligible ARR, and new deal sizes were up 24%. Management maintained full-year guidance despite FX headwinds and expects lower mid-market churn to dissipate as they exit 2026.

Backblaze reported Q2 2026 revenue of $42.7 million, above the high end of guidance, with adjusted EBITDA margin of 30%, also above guidance.
